Pengacara napi, Dale Baich, ngemargiang rasa syukur ring Mahkamah Agung sane ngemargiang indik kasus puniki, nglaksanayang protokol sane ada nenten prasida njamin pati sane manusiawi. Napi penggugat, Charles F. Warner, sampun kapatengin ring hukuman, sareng Richard E. Glossip iraga ngidangang dados napi sane nenten lami kasigutin ring hukuman pati. Kasus puniki dados kasuratang utama sawireh wenten eksekusi botched ring Clayton Lockett ring Oklahoma sane mewapang polemik ring cara suntikan mati pelaksanaang. Baich ngajengangang Mahkamah Agung ngelaksanayang kaji ulang ring putusan 2008 ri Baze v. Rees, rauh wenten perubahan protokol eksekusi sane ngelaksanayang pangangge obat anyar pasca kekurangan obat. Protokol ring Oklahoma nganggon tiga obat: midazolam pinaka pengelaksan pingsan, rocuronium bromide pinaka pemapasan, sareng potassium chloride pinaka ngilangang urip. Kritikus, Megan McCracken saking UC Berkeley, nglaksanayang midazolam nenten ngidangang njamin napi pingsan terus, ngwentenang rasa khawatir eksekusi nenten manusiawi, makeneh nenten dados persetujuan FDA pinaka anestesi umum. Penguasa Oklahoma, antuk Jaksa Agung Scott Pruitt, nglaksanayang pembenaran indik protokol puniki taler dados kasuratang pengesahan ring pengadilan sareng nepukin indik pemargin eksekusi ring negara liunan, sekadi Florida. Keputusan Mahkamah Agung prasida ngidangang pengaruh ageng ring tata cara eksekusi hukuman mati ring Amerika.

In 1993, Craig Pollard, a two-time cancer survivor, founded Cancer for College with a simple mission: to help young cancer survivors achieve their dreams of higher education. Pollard experienced firsthand how cancer can deeply affect families physically, emotionally, and financially. Even with good insurance, families may use up their resources caring for a sick child, leaving little for educational pursuits.

Since its inception, Cancer for College has awarded over $2 million in scholarships to more than 1,000 survivors across the United States. These scholarships offer hope and a chance for young survivors to regain normalcy and work towards their goals. Many recipients are inspired to become doctors, nurses, counselors, and some even return to work in the hospitals where they were treated.

To learn more or contribute to this cause, visit www.cancerforcollege.org.

article_content: The Federal Government has established a committee to review Nigeria's 2007 Public Procurement Act. The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), will chair the committee, which also includes the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, the Director-General of the Bureau of Public Procurement, a World Bank representative, KPMG Nigeria (serving as technical consultants), and the Permanent Secretary and Cabinet Affairs Office (Member/Secretary). According to a statement from Segun Imohiosen, Director of Information at the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), the committee was inaugurated on Thursday in Abuja by the SGF, George Akume. The committee has been given one month to complete its assignment. SGF Akume emphasized that, after implementing the Public Procurement Act for over 15 years, the current administration recognizes the need to review and strengthen it to better respond to contemporary economic challenges. The committee's goal is to ensure realistic procurement outcomes in light of the current economy, to enhance budget implementation, and to improve the ease of doing business. Members are tasked to undertake a comprehensive review of the Act, identify obstacles to compliance, and recommend ways to strengthen provisions for transparency, accountability, value for money, efficiency, and timely delivery of public goods and services. The committee is also to develop a draft amendment bill for the Federal Executive Council and address any other assignments as directed by the President. Akume urged committee members to remain dedicated to this significant task, which aims to streamline public procurement processes and improve service delivery across government agencies.

Maangin indikang rauh ring pernyataan Segun Imohiosen, Direktur Informasi di Kantor Sekretaris Negara (SGF), komite puniki ke-inaugurasi ring Kemis ring Abuja olih SGF, George Akume. Komite puniki ngantosangang waktu setunggal wulan makenyemang tugas puniki. article_content:
The Biden administration is taking steps to make student loan forgiveness more attainable for borrowers facing financial hardship. Traditionally, obtaining loan forgiveness due to general hardship has been difficult. Existing federal student debt relief programs are often limited to very specific situations, like those involving serious medical conditions, school closures, or misrepresentation by institutions. However, new reforms aim to provide borrowers with broader options.

Several relief programs exist for specific circumstances. For instance, borrowers with severe medical issues may qualify for the Total and Permanent Disability discharge. Those negatively impacted by their school's closure or false claims can also apply for loan forgiveness. Low-income borrowers may benefit from Income-Driven Repayment (IDR) plans, which offer forgiveness after 20 or 25 years of payments.

Despite these programs, broad financial hardship has historically not sufficed for loan forgiveness. One possible path is bankruptcy, which is challenging but possible if borrowers demonstrate that repaying their loans imposes an 'undue hardship.' The Biden administration's recent guidance now allows borrowers to submit a comprehensive financial attestation during bankruptcy, potentially easing this process. If government officials agree the borrower meets the undue hardship criteria, they will not oppose the discharge in court. According to recent Education Department data, this approach is seeing some success, though use remains limited. The Department of Justice is also increasing outreach to inform borrowers about this option.

In addition, a new student loan forgiveness plan is being developed under the Higher Education Act, following the Supreme Court’s rejection of a previous plan. This new initiative targets five categories of borrowers, one of which focuses specifically on financial hardship. Committees are discussing qualifying factors, such as receiving public benefits, bankruptcy or disability status, a history of low income or $0 IDR payments, or prior Pell Grant eligibility. By early 2024, final regulations are expected, promising more clarity on eligibility criteria and program details.

article_content: A severe snowstorm recently hit upstate New York, leaving parts of Buffalo buried under as much as seven feet of snow and causing the deaths of at least 13 people. Among those affected was Karen Rossi, a 47-year-old pharmacy technician, who became trapped in her car for 13 hours while trying to drive home from her job at Mercy Hospital in South Buffalo. On her way home to Lancaster around 3 a.m., Rossi's car became stuck in a snowbank, and a passing snowplow unintentionally buried her vehicle even deeper, making it impossible for her to get out. Unable to open her doors due to the packed snow, Rossi used a sweatshirt to protect her hands and cleared snow from the tailpipe to keep the engine running safely. During her ordeal, which lasted from 3 a.m. to 4 p.m., she wrote goodbye notes to her two daughters, fearing she might not survive. Rossi was finally able to attract attention by pushing a red brush through the snow and waving it until a passing monster truck driver noticed and rescued her. Authorities are now warning residents in Buffalo and surrounding areas about potential flooding as warmer temperatures are expected to rapidly melt the heavy snowfall. Governor Andrew Cuomo and Buffalo Mayor Byron Brown have advised people to remain cautious and announced that emergency shelters are ready if residents need to evacuate. The National Guard and local officials are focused on clearing snow and opening blocked drains to prepare for possible floods. More than 650 National Guard members are assisting with these efforts, and 180,000 sandbags have been prepared for flood prevention. Rainfall and temperatures as high as 60 degrees Fahrenheit are increasing concerns that streets, rivers, and creeks may flood quickly as the snow melts. Some roofs have already collapsed under the weight of the snow, and several people were trapped in their vehicles for more than 24 hours during the storm. As the region continues its recovery, officials are prioritizing public safety by clearing roads and setting up backup shelters at community colleges and state university campuses. Residents are encouraged to help clear snow from their properties, especially around drains, to minimize flood risks.

article_content: April Sue-Lyn Jones, a five-year-old girl from Machynlleth, Wales, went missing on Monday evening as she played near her home. She was last seen wearing a purple quilted coat, and her disappearance has left her parents, Coral and Paul, and the local community deeply worried and shocked. April was known for her cheerful and friendly nature, enjoying parties and time with friends—she was recently the 'belle of the ball' at a local birthday event. Her grandmother, Sue Smith, described the family's distress and their hope for April’s safe return. April’s godmother, Mair Raftree, said that April would not have got into a car with a stranger and recalled the shock after hearing of the abduction, which prompted her to help in the search. April's family includes her older sister Jasmine, 16, and her brother Harley, 10, who attended school the day after April disappeared. Teachers and students at her school are having a difficult time coping with the situation, according to the headteacher Gwenfair Glyn. At the time of her disappearance, April’s parents were at a school meeting. Coral, her mother, waited anxiously at their home on Bryn-y-Gog, not wanting to leave in case there was any news. Their house is surrounded by hills, and April had been playing with her best friend, a 7-year-old who has provided important information to police. Neighbours spoke of April as a joyful and kind child from a loving family, and many described feeling anxious for their own children’s safety. What used to be seen as a safe community now feels much more uncertain. Meanwhile, community members gathered at St Peter's Church for a candle-lit service, led by priest Kathleen Rogers, offering prayers and support for April’s family during this difficult time.

article_content: North Korea intends to hold a trial for a U.S. citizen detained there last year, state media reported Saturday, adding further strain to already tense relations between the two countries. Pae Jun Ho entered North Korea as a tourist on November 3, according to the Korean Central News Agency. Authorities detained Pae after evidence reportedly showed he had committed an unspecified crime against the state. He is said to have confessed to the alleged offense, though details were not disclosed. The news agency noted he will soon appear before the Supreme Court of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. As the United States and North Korea lack diplomatic ties, Swedish embassy officials in Pyongyang, who represent U.S. interests, visited Pae on Friday. article_content: In the height of New York's summer heat, the underground subway often feels unbearably hot to daily commuters. But comedian Fabrizio Goldstein, known as 'Fat Jew,' turned this discomfort into something positive by offering free Bikram yoga sessions to homeless individuals right in the subway stations. Once a week, Goldstein gathered participants beneath the bustling streets, substituting the subway's natural heat for the high temperatures normally created in Bikram yoga studios. He led the group through a carefully structured routine of 26 poses and 2 breathing exercises, all designed to loosen the body and encourage well-being. Goldstein documented these sessions on social media, filming the exercises and sharing uplifting messages about using the subway’s sweltering environment for a good cause. He often taught shirtless due to the extreme heat, making lighthearted jokes about the setting. Participants said the classes left them feeling more energized and grateful for the attention paid to their physical health. Media like the Crosby Press covered Goldstein's unusual initiative and highlighted the positive community impact.

Sasampun ajengan, Goldstein nenten wenten ajengan makta, nglaksanayang kelas yoga ring dasar kota nganggén pangangat alami subway dados pengganti suhu ring studio Bikram yoga. Ia muatang peserta ring tiosan 26 pose lan 2 latihan napas sane sampun kabage indik ngelaksanayang tubuh sareng metumbuhang rasa becik. article_content: Usain Bolt reaffirmed his dominance as the world's fastest man by recording the top 100-meter sprint time of the year during a meet in Daegu, South Korea, on Wednesday. Bolt is scheduled to compete next in the 200-meter event at the Diamond League meeting in Shanghai, China, on Sunday.

Italy was not expected to reach the knockout stages of the Rugby World Cup, but a 60-7 defeat to France, following a 96-17 loss to New Zealand, has intensified doubts about the future of Italian rugby.

Italy began the tournament as anticipated, securing two early victories that raised hopes for a historic run. However, their performances were underwhelming: a lackluster 52-8 win over Namibia and a second-half surge to defeat Uruguay 38-17. These results made clear the significant gap that remains between Italy and the world’s top rugby nations, despite their 24 years in the Six Nations.

“If fifteen days ago there was enthusiasm about qualifying for the 2027 World Cup—the minimum goal—now we face two heavy defeats and can’t hide from that,” said Marzio Innocenti, president of the Italian Rugby Federation. “It is time to stop being satisfied with just participating in the World Cup without being real contenders.”

Italy, reeling from the rout by New Zealand, was expected to struggle against France, though they had only lost by five points to the French in this year’s Six Nations. At the World Cup, however, France dominated from the start, scoring a try within two minutes and exposing Italy’s weaknesses.

Coach Kieran Crowley entered the tournament knowing it would be his last leading Italy, a dynamic some believe may have affected the team. “It didn’t impact my performance, I don’t think, though it added an interesting dimension,” Crowley said after the France defeat. He remains optimistic about the potential of the young squad. “I’ve said before I’d like to see this team progress. I think the next World Cup is their cycle.”

Crowley also offered a candid message to Italian rugby authorities: “These players need to be treated with more respect off the field. They need to get things in order—otherwise, I’m not sure I’d want to be involved.”

Italy’s future now rests with incoming head coach Gonzalo Quesada. Scrumhalf Stephen Varney expressed admiration for Crowley’s positive influence and hopes Quesada will have a similar impact. “Before these two years, Italian rugby wasn’t in a good place. Kieran transformed how we played and created a great environment. It’s sad to see him depart.”

For Italy to grow rugby’s profile at home and regain respect abroad, Quesada must secure wins against top-tier nations—or at least prevent further heavy losses that marked this World Cup.

article_content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has increased risk weights on the consumer credit exposure of commercial banks by 25 percentage points, bringing them up to 125%. This decision follows the RBI's recent warning regarding rapid growth in certain segments of consumer credit and its recommendation for banks and NBFCs to enhance their internal surveillance mechanisms. These higher risk weights apply to personal loans and exclude housing loans, education loans, vehicle loans, and loans secured by gold or gold jewelry. Risk weights dictate how much capital lenders are required to hold to cover potential losses from various loan categories. An increase in risk weight necessitates that banks and NBFCs set aside more capital for these loans. According to RBI data, unsecured personal loan growth is now about 23%, surpassing both the average national credit growth rate of 12–14% and the overall bank credit growth rate of approximately 15% in the past year. RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das stated on October 6, 2023, that banks and NBFCs should reinforce their internal monitoring systems and adopt suitable safeguards against risk. He underscored the importance of robust risk management and stronger lending standards. For NBFCs, consumer credit exposures classified as retail loans now carry a 125% risk weight, up from 100%. As before, this does not include housing, education, vehicle, gold, or microfinance/SHG loans. Credit card receivables of scheduled commercial banks will now be assigned a 150% risk weight, up from 125%. NBFCs’ risk weights on credit card receivables increase to 125%. Regulated Entities (REs) must review and establish board-approved sectoral exposure limits for all subcategories of consumer credit. They are now required to set prescribed limits for unsecured consumer credit exposure. Moreover, top-up loans issued against depreciating movable assets are to be assessed as unsecured loans. Governor Das noted last month that the RBI is monitoring certain fast-expanding personal loan categories for nascent stress, with particular attention to small personal loans of up to Rs 10,000 for short terms between three and four months.

Risiko sane nenten ngamolihang pinakas prasida ring pinjaminan pribadi, ngawit pinjaminan rumah, pendidikan, kendaraan, miwah sane ngemargiang jaminan emas utawi perhiasan emas. Risiko puniki ngantosang bank dados ngelaksanayang modal sane luwih akeh indik ngelindungin pinjaman punika. Nambahang risiko nyantosangang bank miwah NBFCs nglaksanayang modalan sane luwih ageng ring pinjaman puniki. Maos saking data RBI, pertumbuhan pinjaman pribadi nika wenten ring angka 23%, sampun majengang rata-rata pertumbuhan kredit nasional sane 12–14% tur pertumbuhan kredit bank ring angka 15% ring satu warsa kapungkur. Ring NBFCs, risiko kartu kredit dados 125%. Entitas Regulator (REs) sami dados ngawasin miwah nglaksanayang batasan eksposur sektoral pinjaminan konsumsi sakancan ring subkategori, miwah ngaturang watesan ring pinjaman konsumsi sane tan wenten jaminan. During her recent concert in London, acclaimed Venezuelan pianist Gabriela Montero dedicated a part of her performance to those resisting the Venezuelan government. Overcome with emotion, Montero—who has long been an outspoken critic of Nicolas Maduro and Hugo Chavez—created an improvised piano piece to express the experiences of anti-government activists facing hardship in Venezuela.

Playing at Queen Elizabeth Hall, Montero explained to her mostly British audience that her improvisations were meant to communicate the pain and frustration felt by many Venezuelans. Among the attendees were several supporters waving Venezuelan flags and wearing colorful attire representing their homeland, which deeply moved her.

Born in Caracas to an American mother and Venezuelan father, Montero rose to fame as a child prodigy and has since performed globally, including at Barack Obama’s presidential inauguration in 2009. Now based in the United States, she described Venezuela’s current situation as extremely dire, pointing to rampant violence, corruption, and a sense of national loss—issues she believes are not fully understood outside the country.

Montero consistently voices her support for those protesting against government repression and has openly condemned musicians who perform in Venezuela amidst civil unrest. Last month, she criticized notable conductors Gustavo Dudamel and Christian Vazquez for playing concerts while protests continued. In response, Dudamel emphasized his opposition to violence and described music as a means of promoting peace worldwide.

Kaantosang rasa, Montero sane sampun kadadosang ring jagate pinaka pengkritik ring pamarentah Nicolas Maduro lan Hugo Chavez, maseh ngaturang karya improvisasi piano sane ngemargiang rasa para aktivis anti-pemerintah ring Venezuela.

Nenten dados nyarengin rasa sedih, ring panggung Queen Elizabeth Hall, Montero ngaturangang ring pemirsa, sane pinaka wenten ring Inggris, indik improvisasi pianonyane sane prasida nglaksanayang rasa sedih lan frustrasi ring antuk problema ring Venezuela. Ring pemirsa, kadadosang krama sane ngalaksanayang solidaritas ring bendera Venezuela miwah nganggén ajeng-ajarengan raih warni bendera nasional.

Irage mamargiang indik dunia saking jaba taler malih nenten ngidang mangdaang pinaka parindikan punika.

Tiosan punika, Montero prasida manut dados penyokong ring perjuangan masyarakat ring pemerintah, nglaksanayang kritik ring musisi sane nampil konser ring Venezuela ring tengah keributan. article_content: LYON, France – Sam Cane will return as captain of the All Blacks for their final Rugby World Cup Pool A match against Uruguay on Thursday. A bonus-point win will guarantee New Zealand a place in the knockout rounds. Coach Ian Foster has made nine changes to the starting lineup that thrashed Italy 96-17 at OL Stadium last weekend, resting regular starters such as Ardie Savea, Aaron Smith, and Rieko Ioane ahead of the quarter-finals. "We've selected the team that we think is best for this game. It's obviously a must-win for us and that's our number one focus," Foster told reporters on Tuesday. "We've also made some tweaks, resting some players who perhaps didn't need another game, but we believe we're still in great shape as a result. You'll see plenty of continuity in the team." Lock Sam Whitelock will make his 150th test appearance, starting alongside Tupou Vaa'i in the second row. Whitelock became the most-capped All Black when he surpassed Richie McCaw’s record as a replacement against Italy. Tyrel Lomax returns to the front row at tighthead prop after recovering from a leg injury that required 30 stitches, which caused him to miss matches against France and Namibia. Cane, who came off the bench last week following a back problem, returns to the starting lineup, with Dalton Papali'i dropping out and Ethan Blackadder covering the loose forwards from the bench. Shannon Frizell continues at blindside flanker after a strong comeback from a hamstring strain, while Damian McKenzie makes a rare start at fullback, with Beauden Barrett on the bench. Jordie Barrett starts at inside centre alongside Anton Leinert-Brown, who returned from a knee injury last week. Centre David Havili (hamstring) is unavailable, and winger Leicester Fainga'anuku will provide midfield cover if needed. Foster emphasized he is not underestimating Uruguay: "The challenge of World Cups is to prepare for the present with an eye to the future. But Uruguay poses significant challenges, and we need to improve in areas they'll test us in." New Zealand team: 15-Damian McKenzie, 14-Will Jordan, 13-Anton Leinert-Brown, 12-Jordie Barrett, 11-Leicester Fainga'anuku, 10-Richie Mo'unga, 9-Cam Roigard, 8-Luke Jacobson, 7-Sam Cane (captain), 6-Shannon Frizell, 5-Tupou Vaa'i, 4-Sam Whitelock, 3-Tyrel Lomax, 2-Codie Taylor, 1-Ofa Tu'ungafasi. Replacements: 16-Samisoni Taukei’aho, 17-Tamaiti Williams, 18-Fletcher Newell, 19-Scott Barrett, 20-Ethan Blackadder, 21-Finlay Christie, 22-Beauden Barrett, 23-Caleb Clarke.

Pelatih Ian Foster sampun ngalaksanayang sangang perubahan ring tim utama sane ngalahang Italia 96-17 ring Stadion OL minggu wawu, ngorahang pemain utama pinaka Ardie Savea, Aaron Smith, tur Rieko Ioane ring ajengan babak perempat-final. "Tim sane kapilih puniki sane pinaka becik ring laga puniki. Puniki must-win tur punika fokus utama iraga," icapang Foster ring konferensi pers Rahina Selasa. Whitelock dados All Black pinaka sering main, ngalanturang rekor Richie McCaw pinaka pemain cadangan nglawan Italia. Shannon Frizell mantuk dados blindside flanker setelah penampilan becik ring ajengan saking cidra hamstring, miwah Damian McKenzie kapilih dados fullback tur Beauden Barrett ring bangku cadangan. article_content: The European Union plans to host talks between Armenian and Azerbaijani leaders by the end of October to help ease tensions after Azerbaijan’s recent swift offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh, EU chief Charles Michel announced. At the European Political Community summit in Spain, Michel said the date would be decided along with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev. Two weeks ago, Azerbaijan regained control of the Nagorno-Karabakh region after a rapid, one-day military action, ending three decades of separatist rule. The offensive caused a mass exodus, with most of the region’s estimated 120,000 ethnic Armenians fleeing to Armenia. European leaders had aimed to host Aliyev and Pashinyan’s first post-offensive meeting in Spain. However, Aliyev declined, citing France's militarisation, the EU’s regional stance, and Turkey’s absence. Later, Azerbaijan’s presidential aide, Hikmet Hajiyev, said Baku is open to tripartite Brussels talks with the EU and Armenia. Russia, long the main external power in the region, has been largely preoccupied with its war in Ukraine, so Europe is playing a bigger role in mediating the long-running dispute. France has pledged military support to Armenia after the Azerbaijani offensive, though specifics have not been disclosed. Armenian and French officials accuse Azerbaijan of ethnic cleansing in Nagorno-Karabakh, an allegation that Azerbaijan refutes. French Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna described the mass departure as forced, not voluntary, and voiced hope the displaced might return. On the ground, both countries accused each other of cross-border firing. Pashinyan has become more critical of Russia, arguing its security alliance with Armenia is ineffective and citing the peacekeepers’ lack of intervention. Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Azerbaijan’s retaking of Karabakh was inevitable and a matter of time. Russia’s Defence Ministry announced that Russian peacekeepers are dismantling frontline observation posts in the region. Amid domestic criticism, Pashinyan traveled to Granada to meet European leaders and had his first meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. This came shortly after Armenia’s parliament voted to join the International Criminal Court, which has issued an arrest warrant for Putin. Armenia and Azerbaijan have fought two wars over Nagorno-Karabakh since the late 1980s. The region, mainly populated by Armenians, has officially been part of Azerbaijan since the 1920s when Soviet authorities drew national borders. After the USSR’s dissolution in 1991, Karabakh declared independence with Armenia’s support, sparking three decades of conflict. Karabakh separatists, backed by Armenia, withstood Azerbaijani control during wars in 1988–1994 and 2020.

Ring KTT Komunitas Politik Eropa ring Spanyol, Michel ngidangangang tanggal rapat puniki becikang sareng Perdana Menteri Armenia, Nikol Pashinyan, sareng Presiden Azerbaijan, Ilham Aliyev. Dua minggu wenten, Azerbaijan nguasayang malih wilayah Nagorno-Karabakh nganggén operasi militer sane cepet, ngorreang pemisahan sane ngelaksanayang talerang telung dasa warsa. Operasi puniki ngasilang eksodus ageng—mayoritas indik 120.000 masyarakat Armenia ring wilayah punika ngungsi ring Armenia. Pemimpin Eropa ngarepakang nglaksanayang pertemuan Aliyev sane kapertama sareng Pashinyan saangka serangan puniki ring Spanyol. Nanging, Aliyev tan wenten, ngalanturang indik kebijakan militerisasi Perancis, sikap EU ring wilayah puniki, miwah absennya Turki. Dauhg puniki, pembantu presiden Azerbaijan, Hikmet Hajiyev, nyarengin yen Baku siap nglaksanayang rapat tripartit ring Brussels sareng EU lan Armenia. Rusia sane sujarah dados kekuatan utama ring wilayah puniki, mangdaang perhatian ring perang ring Ukraina, ngajantenang Eropa dados mediator utama sengketa sane suwidang. Pejabat Armenia sareng Perancis ngametuangang tuduhan ethnic cleansing ring Azerbaijan ring Nagorno-Karabakh, nanging Azerbaijan nepeangang tuduhan puniki. Menteri Luar Negeri Perancis, Catherine Colonna, nyarengin eksodus puniki dados eksodus paksa, nenten sukarela, taler nyidangangang wenten pangarep-arep sida prasida mulih ring umah sareng tana asal. Ring lapangan, Armenia sareng Azerbaijan saling tuduh matembak lintas tapal batas. Pashinyan dados tur majeng kritik ring Rusia, ngedalangang aliansi keamanan nenten efektif sareng nyorotang pasukan penjaga perdamaian mboten nenten melaksanaang tugas. Presiden Rusia, Vladimir Putin, nyarengin yen Azerbaijan nguasayang Karabakh sane punika prasida nenten dados indik waktu malih. Kementerian Pertahanan Rusia nyarengin pasukan penjaga perdamaian Rusia melaksanayang pembongkaran pos pengamatan ring wilayah puniki. Sane kasor ring kritik domestik, Pashinyan makasami ring Granada ngametuangang pemimpin Eropa sareng ngadikang pertemuan pisan sareng Presiden Ukraina, Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Puniki rauh sasampun Parlemen Armenia nylasayang becik gabung ring Pengadilan Kriminal Internasional sane natehang surat penangkapan ring Putin. Armenia sareng Azerbaijan sampun ngalaksanayang dua perang ring Nagorno-Karabakh wiadin dasa warsa 1980-an. Wilayah puniki, mayoritas rahayu masyarakat Armenia, dados bagian saking Azerbaijan sasampun pemimpin Soviet ngatur tapal-tapal ring dasa warsa 1920-an. Sasampun USSR melancaran ring 1991, Karabakh medalang kamardikan sareng dukungan Armenia, ngelingangsang konflik taler tiga dasa warsa. Separatis Karabakh, sane wantah ring pangentosan Armenia, nglaksanayang perlawanan ring Azerbaijan ring perang 1988–1994 lan warsa 2020.

article_content: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has announced it will charge Nigerian Air Force (NAF) personnel to court once its ongoing investigation concludes. This statement was made by Dele Oyewale, EFCC's Head of Media and Publicity, in a release posted on the Commission's website. Last Friday, the NAF officers were granted administrative bail by the Kaduna Zonal Command. According to Oyewale, the officers were released in strict accordance with EFCC’s bail procedures. He emphasized that no one is above the law and that due process will be followed. EFCC previously disclosed that the NAF officers were involved in a security breach. They were arrested for attempting to rescue suspected fraudsters who were in EFCC custody. On November 13, 2023, operatives of the Kaduna Zonal Command of the EFCC arrested five suspected internet fraudsters—Favour Itung, Rachael Ande, Zuleiman Haruna, Abubakar Ismaila, and Solomon Olobatoke—at a residential inn and Disney Chicken Eatery in Barnawa, Kaduna, following credible intelligence. After the operation, six military personnel who witnessed the arrests at the eatery then stormed the EFCC Kaduna Command and attempted to forcefully release the suspects. These included four Air Force officers—Lawal Abdullahi, Chukwuma Christian, Alfa Suleiman, and Emmanuel Ekwozor—and two students from the Nigerian Air Force Institute of Technology: Chidera Anuba and Joseph Tokula. They were detained for the security breach. While in custody, EFCC and NAF leadership discussed how to resolve the situation. However, on November 17, 2023, talks broke down, and some NAF officers again stormed the EFCC Command in an attempt to release their detained colleagues using aggressive tactics. EFCC noted that it exercised restraint in response and continued to work with NAF leadership, releasing the officers to the NAF Provost only after proper procedures were followed. The Commission reassured the public that it remains dedicated to tackling economic and financial crimes and assured that it will follow through with proper legal processes in this case.

Sagaponack, located in New York City’s Flatiron District, blends Asian and Mediterranean culinary influences. The restaurant, named after a Hamptons town, has been revitalized under owner Kyungil Lee and Executive Chef Phil Choy, previously of Boulud Sud. The two-level restaurant features minimalist design touches, a glass-front reminiscent of the sea, and a lively bar area separated from quieter seating in back.

Oysters are a speciality, served in inventive preparations such as with Fresno and serrano chilies, yuzu and trout roe, or roasted with varying blends. Guests applaud the creativity of these oysters ($23 for three; $21 for four roasted). The chef’s artistry continues with dishes like fluke adorned with coconut, Marcona almonds, tobiko, and a cucumber-chili-lime sauce ($22); salmon crudo with yuzu, sesame, orange, and serrano chile ($22); and Brussels sprouts enhanced with maple, soy, apple, and sesame ($14).

Notable main courses include gambas al ajillo—shrimp with garlic, pimento, and preserved lemon ($17)—and mussels in a spicy reduction. ‘Nduja mussels with pork sausage and Calabrian seasoning ($23), sea scallops with polenta and maitake mushrooms ($34), and shoyu salmon with jeweled rice and brown butter ($32) are highlights. Ricotta cavatelli with peekytoe crab, sunchokes, and lemon ($14), and a seafood paella with chorizo, saffron, clams, mussels, shrimp, and squid ($35/person) round out the menu.

For dessert, the Thai milk cake with cinnamon, mango, and pecan crumble ($17) stands out for sharing, while the crème brûlée with strawberry, Earl Grey tea, and mint ($15) is less compelling.

Though the menu leans more Mediterranean, Chef Choy’s Asian background brings unique flair to each plate, marrying spices and quality ingredients. Sagaponack serves lunch and dinner Monday through Saturday at 4 West 22nd Street (212-229-2226). Diners can expect fresh, creative seafood—distinctive from typical fried offerings, with Chef Choy’s unmistakable style.

Menu puniki langkung nganut Mediterania, Chef Choy sareng pengalamannyane prasida dadosang cita rasa unik ring sejeroning ajengan. India clinched a commanding 160-run win over the Netherlands in their final Cricket World Cup league match at M Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru. Celebrating Deepavali, the Indian team saw this encounter as preparation for their upcoming semifinal against New Zealand.

Batting first, openers Rohit Sharma (61) and Shubman Gill (51) provided a solid start. Virat Kohli followed with a composed 51, while Shreyas Iyer (128* not out) and KL Rahul (102) electrified the innings with their centuries. Iyer and Rahul took charge in the last 10 overs, adding 126 runs and taking India to an imposing 410 for 4.

Chasing an enormous target, the Netherlands displayed determination. Teja Nidamanuru (54), Sybrand Engelbrecht (45), Colin Ackermann (35), and Max O’Dowd (30) contributed notable innings, but the team was eventually bowled out for 250 in 47.5 overs. India utilized multiple bowlers, including Virat Kohli, who took the wicket of Dutch captain Scott Edwards. Rohit Sharma sealed the win by dismissing Nidamanuru.

India ended the league stage unbeaten and are set for the semifinal challenge. The match was played in a festive atmosphere, with strong support for India, while the Netherlands received credit for their fighting spirit.

Sebagai tim pemukul pertama, Rohit Sharma (61) dan Shubman Gill (51) membuka pertandingan dengan baik. Virat Kohli menambah 51 run, sedangkan Shreyas Iyer (128* tak terhentikan) dan KL Rahul (102) menggebrak dengan membuat ‘century’. India memakai banyak bowler, termasuk Virat Kohli yang mengambil wicket kapten Netherlands, Scott Edwards. Rohit Sharma menutup kemenangan dengan mematikan Nidamanuru.

India menutup fase liga dengan sempurna dan siap menuju semifinal. Suasana pertandingan penuh semangat, didukung fans India, serta Netherlands dihargai atas perjuangan mereka.

Dutch champions AZ Alkmaar have announced Dick Advocaat as their new head coach until the end of the current season. The club sought permission from the Belgian Football Association (KBVB), as Advocaat is also the national team coach of Belgium. He will combine both roles, leading AZ and continuing with Belgium. This move follows the dismissal of former coach Ronald Koeman on Saturday.

A statement on AZ's official website confirmed Advocaat's appointment and clarified that the 62-year-old will be on the bench for their upcoming match against PSV on Saturday. Last season, AZ secured the Eredivisie title under Louis van Gaal, but they have struggled this year and currently sit in seventh place, 19 points behind leaders FC Twente.

Advocaat, who previously coached the Netherlands national team, PSV Eindhoven, and Rangers, has set clear objectives for his time at AZ. He told AZ TV: "We need to qualify for European football. If we don’t achieve that, then I haven’t done my job properly."

AZ will play Standard Liege in Belgium on Wednesday for their final Champions League Group H match.

Dados punika, Advocaat nglaksanayang kalih tanggung jawab: ngelatih AZ sareng melanjutang tugas ring timnas Belgia. Keputusan puniki ngalanturang ring pemecatan Ronald Koeman dados pelatih ring Rahina Redite diki.

Ring pernyataan ring website resmi AZ, Advocaat sane umure 62 warsa, resmi dados pelatih anyar sareng prasida mebeng bench ring laga nglawan PSV ring Rahina Saniscara puniki. Ring musim dados, AZ dados juara Eredivisie ring pianak Louis van Gaal, ngan mangkin AZ kelaosan ring posisi pitu sareng 19 poin kalabahang FC Twente sane masih dados pemimpin liga.

Advocaat sane sampun ngelatih Belanda, PSV Eindhoven lan Rangers, ngicenang tujuan sane jelas ring AZ: "Tim puniki harus prasida masuk kompetisi Eropa. Dados tusing bisa punika, artinya titiang durung becik ngalaksanayang tugas." 

AZ ngadahang Standard Liege ring Belgia ring Rahina Budha puniki ring pertandingan pungkasan Group H Liga Champions.

article_content: Sunderland striker Connor Wickham remains confident that another battle for Premier League survival is not on his mind. The 21-year-old scored his fourth goal of the season in Sunderland’s 2-0 win over Burnley, lifting the club to 14th place and four points clear of the relegation zone. The win, Sunderland’s first in six league matches and only their second home victory this season, provided a much-needed boost. Wickham, whose late-season goals last year helped Sunderland make a dramatic escape from relegation, said, 'You can never guarantee you are safe—just look at last season. Nobody can be sure until it’s mathematical, so we’re not even thinking about that. My aim is to stay in the Premier League and relegation has never crossed my mind.' January signing Jermain Defoe celebrated with manager Gus Poyet following the win. Head coach Poyet, pleased with both the result and performance, cautioned that this was merely the start of an ongoing process that will require sustained effort. Poyet’s tactical switch, which saw Wickham supporting Defoe and full-backs Anthony Reveillere and Patrick van Aanholt pushing forward, paid off. Wickham headed in Reveillere’s cross to open the scoring in the 20th minute, and Defoe doubled the lead 14 minutes later, converting Van Aanholt’s cutback for his first Sunderland goal. Wickham noted, 'We played well as a team and looked comfortable. It was one of the first times I got to play with Jermain, and we both scored.' For Burnley, the result was disappointing. Ashley Barnes nearly gave them an early lead, but the team failed to capitalize and now sits just one point above the drop zone. Manager Sean Dyche reflected, 'That’s life in the Premier League. We’re learning and improving, but every week is a challenge. We can’t afford any players not performing at their best, whereas bigger clubs can carry a few off-days. We need to be at our best every match.'
translated_content: Penyerang Sunderland, Connor Wickham, merasa yakin bahwa perjuangan untuk bertahan di Premier League bukan hal yang ia pikirkan. Pemain berusia 21 tahun itu mencetak gol keempat musim ini dalam kemenangan 2-0 Sunderland atas Burnley, mengangkat klub ke posisi ke-14 dan unggul empat poin dari zona degradasi. Kemenangan ini adalah yang pertama untuk Sunderland dalam enam laga liga terakhir sekaligus kemenangan kandang kedua musim ini, memberikan dorongan yang sangat dibutuhkan. Wickham, yang gol-golnya di akhir musim lalu membantu Sunderland lolos dari degradasi, berkata, 'Kamu tidak pernah bisa jamin aman—lihat saja musim lalu. Tidak ada yang pasti sampai secara matematis, jadi kami bahkan tidak memikirkan soal itu. Target saya tetap bertahan di Premier League dan degradasi tidak pernah terlintas di benak saya.' Pemain baru bulan Januari, Jermain Defoe, merayakan bersama manajer Gus Poyet setelah kemenangan tersebut. Pelatih kepala Poyet, yang puas dengan hasil dan penampilan tim, mengingatkan bahwa ini baru permulaan dari proses panjang yang membutuhkan usaha berkelanjutan. Perubahan taktik Poyet, di mana Wickham mendukung Defoe dan bek sayap Anthony Reveillere serta Patrick van Aanholt sering maju, membuahkan hasil. Wickham menyundul umpan silang Reveillere di menit ke-20 untuk membuka skor, lalu Defoe menggandakan keunggulan 14 menit kemudian melalui umpan tarik Van Aanholt untuk gol pertamanya bersama Sunderland. Wickham berkomentar, 'Kami bermain baik sebagai tim dan terlihat nyaman. Ini salah satu kali pertama saya bermain bersama Jermain dan kami berdua mencetak gol.' Bagi Burnley, hasil ini mengecewakan. Ashley Barnes hampir membawa mereka unggul di awal, tapi tim gagal memanfaatkan peluang dan kini hanya satu poin di atas zona degradasi. Manajer Sean Dyche menegaskan, 'Itulah kehidupan di Premier League. Kami terus belajar dan berkembang, tapi setiap minggu selalu jadi tantangan. Kami tidak bisa punya pemain yang tampil di bawah standar, sementara klub besar masih bisa menutupi itu. Kami perlu selalu tampil maksimal di setiap pertandingan.'
post_content: Sunderland snaps their bad run! Wickham and new signing Defoe both on target in a 2-0 win over Burnley. Poyet loving the turnaround, but Dyche says every game’s a grind. Premier League survival fight continues! #Sunderland #PremierLeague #Football
translated_post: Sunderland ento bangkit! Wickham sareng rekrutan anyar Defoe nyetak gol nalika menang 2-0 melawan Burnley. Poyet masih wantah minta timnya terus semangat, Dyche ngaku perjuangan di Premier League abot. Masih rame persaingan! #Sunderland #LigaInggris #Bola

article_content: Broadway theatres will dim their marquee lights tonight to honor James Gandolfini, best known for his role in the television drama The Sopranos. The actor, who passed away last week at the age of 51, also had a distinguished stage career. New York theatres are set to pay a significant tribute by turning off their lights for one minute at 8pm. Gandolfini, who died suddenly in Rome, leaves behind his wife, Deborah Lin, and his son. Gandolfini appeared on stage with Hope Davis and Jeff Daniels in God of Carnage, earning a Tony Award nomination in 2009. Charlotte St. Martin, president of the Broadway League, praised him as an actor who brought individuality and authenticity to every role, making strong connections with audiences. She extended condolences to his family, friends, and fans. In addition to God of Carnage, Gandolfini performed in A Streetcar Named Desire in 1992 and On the Waterfront in 1995. He rose to fame as the lead in The Sopranos, HBO's acclaimed crime drama. Dimming the marquee lights is a rare gesture reserved for prominent figures in the theatre community. Gandolfini died in Rome last Wednesday while vacationing with his family. His 13-year-old son discovered him suffering a heart attack in their hotel room. The actor was working on a new HBO series and had two films scheduled for release next year. He had planned to attend the Taormina Film Festival in Sicily. His body was flown back to the United States on Sunday. Gandolfini's funeral will take place tomorrow at the Cathedral Church of Saint John the Divine in New York City. His sisters, Leta and Johanna, were seen at HBO offices, which produced the series that brought him international fame. According to vicar Julia Whitworth, tomorrow’s ceremony for family and friends will be a beautiful funeral Mass.

article_content: Imagine stepping onto a plane that flies quietly, doesn't burn fuel, and leaves no emissions as it lands—a future we're getting closer to. The E-Fan, designed by Airbus Group, is a prototype hybrid-electric motor glider that's set to start training pilots in Bordeaux, France by 2017. This innovative two-seater aircraft, armed with two batteries providing 60 kilowatts of power and a 30-minute flight window, had its first public flight in April 2014. Airbus’s chief technical officer Jean Botti sees E-Fan as a stepping stone towards larger electric planes. The journey began five years ago, when Airbus experimented with the Cri-Cri, one of the smallest twin-engine planes ever built. In addition to reducing noise and emissions, the E-Fan brings notable cost savings. Operating the electric glider costs just about two cents per hour—up to 50 times cheaper than conventional aircraft, according to Botti. Over time, these savings could benefit customers as electric-powered pilot training becomes widespread. In the future, Airbus envisions electric planes for regional routes, able to carry as many as 90 passengers for up to three hours. However, this development is still expected to be 15 to 20 years away. In the short term, they’re also looking at hybrid-electric helicopters. This progress is boosted by the European Commission’s 'Flightpath 2050' initiative, which aims to cut aviation CO2 emissions by 75% and noise by 65% from 2000 levels. As the E-Fan project grows, Airbus plans to involve apprenticeships and educational programs to help train the next generation of engineers. A main technical challenge remains: advancing battery technology. Botti points out that to reach their goals, much higher efficiency in energy storage is required—a focus of their new research center in Munich, Germany. Other pioneering projects are also shaping the future of aviation. Solar Impulse 2, built by Swiss innovators, is a fully solar-powered aircraft aiming for a 120-hour non-stop flight. Its predecessor broke records in 2010 with the first overnight solar flight lasting 26 hours. Meanwhile, the Antares 23E, developed collaboratively by Dutch and German teams, can glide 60 kilometers on battery power with its impressive 23-meter wingspan.

article_content: President Obama described his historic visit to Myanmar as an acknowledgement of the democratic transition underway there, but clarified that it does not constitute an endorsement of the country’s government. This message aimed to address critics who argue that the trip to the nation, also known as Burma, is premature. While Myanmar has made significant reforms, hundreds of political prisoners remain detained, and more than 100,000 people have been displaced due to ethnic violence. Obama stated that his goal in visiting Myanmar is to highlight both the progress made and the steps that still need to be taken. He also expressed his wish to congratulate the people of Myanmar for starting on the path toward greater respect for human rights and political freedom. Obama’s Asia trip began in Thailand, where he was greeted by Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra. During a welcoming ceremony at the Government House in Bangkok, Obama reviewed an honor guard and toured the Viharn of the Reclining Buddha with Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and Chaokun Suthee Thammanuwat. The president remarked that his first foreign trip after re-election demonstrated the importance of the Asia-Pacific region for America’s security and prosperity, pointing out the region’s key role in job creation and future stability. While in Asia, Obama’s agenda included meetings with government leaders and managing U.S. interests abroad. He remained attentive to the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Gaza Strip and stayed in contact with leaders including Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as well as Egyptian and Turkish officials who might influence Hamas. In Thailand, Obama’s schedule included a royal audience with King Bhumibol Adulyadej, a private meeting with Prime Minister Shinawatra, a press conference, and an official dinner. He visited the Wat Pho Royal Monastery, where he and Clinton toured and engaged with Buddhist monks. Obama joked that he hoped prayer would help resolve challenges at home, such as budget negotiations. The visit to Thailand, which lasted less than 18 hours, symbolized the close ties between the U.S. and one of its oldest allies in the region, though the relationship had experienced strains following Thailand's 2006 military coup. Deputy National Security Adviser Ben Rhodes emphasized the importance of U.S. alliances in establishing a stronger presence in Asia. Obama also highlighted efforts to open new markets for American businesses, noting that the U.S. is Thailand’s third largest trading partner after China and Japan. Becoming a counterbalance to China in the Asia-Pacific is a central feature of Obama’s regional strategy. Secretary of Defense Leon Panetta’s recent visit to Thailand strengthened security cooperation, covering topics such as weapons nonproliferation, disaster relief, and anti-piracy. National Security Adviser Tom Donilon stated that Obama’s visit aimed to build on these efforts and support the peaceful restoration of democracy in Thailand. After his activities in Thailand, Obama traveled to Myanmar, marking the first visit by a sitting U.S. president to the country. He met with the 84-year-old King Bhumibol, the world’s longest-serving monarch, who was born in the U.S. The trip is seen as a signal to other countries that the U.S. will support democratic change. Obama’s aides view Myanmar’s reforms as a positive example, with Ben Rhodes stating that successful transitions can inspire further regional progress.

Obama nyorotang usaha ngebuka pasar anyar ring bisnis Amerika, ngicenang Amerika pinaka mitra dagang ketiga ajengan ring Thailand sawise China miwah Jepang. Dados lawan imbangan pengaruh China ring Asia-Pasifik mangda dados strategi utama Presiden Obama. Sekretaris Pertahanan Leon Panetta nglaksanayang kunjungan ring Thailand negulungang kerjasama keamanan, sane nyangkutang pengendalian senjata, bantuan bencana, miwah anti-perompakan. Penasehat Keamanan Nasional Tom Donilon ngidangangang kunjungan Obama puniki nglaksanayang pangade nguatang hubungan miwah nyokong pemulihan damai ring demokrasi Thailand. Saling nglaksanayang acara ring Thailand, Obama ngelaksanayang perjalanan ring Myanmar, sane dados pisan presiden Amerika ring jaba negara sane ngidangangang kunjungan ring negara punika. Manten makta ring Raja Bhumibol sane 84 tahun, pinaka raja sane pinaka makta tur lair ring Amerika. Kunjungan puniki dados sinyal ring negara lianan yening Amerika sareng nyokong perubahan demokrasi. article_content: The European Union has launched a fact-finding mission to determine the causes of the August war between Georgia and Russia, according to an EU spokeswoman on Tuesday. Swiss diplomat Heidi Tagliavini, who previously served as the United Nations special representative for Georgia, will head the investigation. The eight-month inquiry will examine facts of the conflict with regard to international law, humanitarian concerns, and human rights, the spokeswoman said. Her name was withheld as she was not authorized to speak publicly. Investigators will also review all existing accusations concerning the conflict. The mission began on Monday and is expected to conclude by July 31, 2009, after which a report will be delivered to the EU, the United Nations, and the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE). Hostilities started on August 7, when Georgia launched a military campaign against South Ossetia, a Russian-backed separatist region. The next day, Russian forces, including tanks and armored vehicles, entered South Ossetia and Abkhazia—another breakaway territory—and advanced into Georgian cities beyond these regions. Both Georgia and Russia blame each other for starting the conflict and accuse the other side of ethnic cleansing. After the conflict, Russia recognized South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent regions.

Penyelidikan puniki mawentukan waktu wolanan, nglaksanayang pemeriksaan ring fakta perang nganut hukum internasional, urusan kemanusiaan, miwah hak asasi manusa, peseng juru bicara punika sane sampun nyilihang anak idane, karna tan dados makta ring umum. Para penyelidik dados nglaksanayang pemeriksaan ring semua tuduhan sane wenten ngametuangang konflik punika. Misi puniki sampun ngamargiang ring Rahina Senin lan prasida nyantosang laporan ring Uni Eropa, Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa (PBB), sareng Organisasi Keamanan lan Kerja Sama Eropa (OSCE) ring tanggal 31 Juli 2009. Perang ngamargiang ring tanggal 7 Agustus, waktu Georgia ngamargiang operasi militer ring South Ossetia sane dados wilayah separatis sane batuan olih Rusia. Sawise polih sehari, tentara Rusia, kalebet tank sareng kendaraan lapis baja, asung ring South Ossetia miwah Abkhazia—wilayah sané memargi nyidang nglawan Georgia—lan majeng ring kota-kota Georgia sajeroning wilayah puniki. Georgia lan Rusia saling nyalahang miwah makemitang indik pembersihan etnis. Sasampun perang puniki, Rusia ngakeni South Ossetia lan Abkhazia dados wilayah sane independent.

Traditional Startup Growth: The Venture Capital Route
Many aspiring entrepreneurs are taught that turning an idea into a high-growth business means pitching their idea, securing angel and VC funding, bringing in a seasoned CEO, and aiming for a big exit—either by selling the company or going public. However, only a tiny fraction of startups, roughly 20 out of every 100,000, find notable success through this VC-backed method. Even among entrepreneurs who built billion-dollar businesses, only about 6% used this traditional pathway.  Billion-Dollar Businesses: Rethinking the VC Playbook
A study of 85 company founders who grew their businesses from scratch to over $1 billion in sales or valuation revealed a different pattern: Over 90% launched and scaled their companies without VC money. Of those who did accept venture capital, 18% remained in charge as CEO, but the vast majority—76%—never took on venture capital at all. Those who waited to take VC funding retained twice as much of the wealth their companies generated, while those who skipped VC altogether kept seven times as much.  Nine Essential Skills for Entrepreneurs
These self-made unicorn founders relied on a toolkit of nine important skills—often called 360-degree entrepreneurship skills. Six are critical for getting a startup off the ground and maintaining control, while three more are vital for scaling the company to major success.  Six Skills That Enable a Founder to Launch and Keep Control 1. Technical know-how in a fast-changing field: Founders like Bill Gates, Sam Walton, and Mark Zuckerberg started their journeys with strong technical chops or teamed up with partners who did. 2. Sales savvy tailored to emerging markets: Successful entrepreneurs, including Dick Schulze and Joe Martin, mastered direct selling, often thriving with limited upfront capital. 3. Financial literacy specific to new ventures: Many billion-dollar founders skillfully made the most of every dollar, focusing their resources on growth. 4. Raising money while protecting ownership: Entrepreneurs such as Michael Bloomberg secured funding in ways that minimized their loss of control. 5. Strategic bootstrapping: Smart use of resources, like Bob Kierlin’s approach at Fastenal, allowed founders to gain ground with minimal outside capital. 6. Lean launch execution: Guiding a startup from idea to launch is hardest when funds are tight, requiring creativity in finding growth drivers and sustaining momentum, as Richard Burke did at UnitedHealthcare.  Three Skills for Scaling From Startup to Industry Leader 1. Skillfully overseeing business growth. 2. Structuring teams and operations to outcompete rivals. 3. Leading decisively to become a dominant force in the market.  The X-Factor: The Role of Luck
No matter how skilled you are, achieving extraordinary success often means getting a lucky break—be it timing, connections, or market shifts. Competing with icons like Gates, Bezos, or Musk, luck undeniably plays a role.  Takeaway
Entrepreneurs with a wide range of business skills—especially those who self-fund and maintain control—tend to build the strongest, most enduring companies, keeping more of the rewards of their success along the way.

article_content: A tragedy unfolded near the Italian island of Lampedusa when a boat carrying up to 500 migrants sank and caught fire, resulting in at least 110 deaths and 154 rescued, according to local authorities. Lampedusa, situated between Africa and Sicily, acts as a primary landing point for migrants trying to reach the European Union. Many undertake dangerous journeys on unseaworthy, overcrowded boats organized by traffickers. Most of the migrants on board were reportedly from Eritrea, Somalia, and Ghana, with the boat launched from Libya. Despite some wind and rain, weather conditions were not severe enough to explain the accident, according to officials. The boat sank near the well-known Rabbit Beach. Rescuers are treating survivors and transporting the deceased to the main port, where somber scenes include rows of body bags. Antonio Guterres, head of the UN refugee agency, recognized the Italian coast guard while expressing deep concern about the increase in migrant deaths at sea. Organizations like Amnesty International are calling for Italy and the European Union to dedicate more resources to search-and-rescue operations, emphasizing the need for safer alternatives to dangerous sea crossings. Pope Francis also condemned what he described as 'global indifference' and urged unified action. Lampedusa often sees increased arrivals during the calmer summer months. Arriving migrants experience overcrowded reception centers and commonly suffer from dehydration, sunburn, or gasoline burns due to cramped conditions. Authorities are collaborating with satellite communication firms to monitor distressed vessels and respond faster to emergencies. Over 200,000 migrants and refugees have entered Europe via Lampedusa since 1999, straining local infrastructures. Frontex, the EU border agency, reports continued rescue of migrants from unsafe boats, saving thousands of lives this year. Routes have shifted over time, but many continue to risk perilous crossings. Humanitarian groups urge sustained EU action to prevent further tragedies. Most crossings occur between May and September, with the majority of departures from North Africa. The UN reports 8,400 migrant arrivals in Italy and Malta in the year's first half, mostly to Italy. Although deaths declined this year, the situation remains critical and demands a united response. CNN journalists from Italy and the UK contributed to the coverage of this humanitarian emergency.

article_content: Collins Dictionary has named 'AI' (Artificial Intelligence) as its 2023 Word of the Year, capturing the remarkable rise of the technology and its role in public discourse. AI is defined as the 'modelling of human mental functions by computer programs.' Managing Director Alex Beecroft noted that AI has swiftly integrated into daily life, alongside technologies like email and streaming. The selection was informed by analysis of the Collins Corpus, a database of over 20 billion words sourced globally from media and literature. Collins Dictionary also recognized 'Bazball,' a term depicting England’s assertive Test cricket style under coach Brendon McCullum. Named after McCullum’s nickname ‘Baz,’ the word represents a proactive style of play. Bazball gained attention after McCullum became England's Test coach in May 2022 and was a significant talking point during the Ashes series, which ended 2-2 after England trailed 0-2. Despite its popularity, McCullum himself has voiced unease with the term 'Bazball.' Separately, Apple achieved record quarterly revenue in India for the September quarter. CEO Tim Cook emphasized India’s growing importance as a smartphone market. Trends in India’s luxury car market show buyers are becoming younger. Audi says two out of five of its buyers are under 40. At Mercedes-Benz India, the average buyer age is 38, reportedly the lowest for the brand worldwide. BMW India also sees strong sales among 35- to 40-year-olds. In the entertainment sector, Punit Goenka’s role as CEO of the planned Sony-Zee merger is in question amid an ongoing SEBI investigation into alleged fund diversion, impacting future leadership arrangements.

article_content: A new study has revealed that North American monarch butterflies migrate across the continent without relying on an internal map. Instead, these butterflies use basic orientation techniques and significant geographic landmarks to guide their journey from Canada and the United States to Mexico. Researchers from the University of Guelph in Ontario, Canada, suggest that monarchs also depend on an internal compass, using cues from the sun and Earth's magnetic field to reach their wintering sites. This challenges the previous belief that monarchs had a more sophisticated internal navigation system. Monarch butterflies are found in North America, New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Western Europe. With a wingspan between 8.9 and 10.2 cm, they are renowned for their annual migration between Canada/the U.S. and Mexico. The southward migration begins with the season's first frost, and the return north occurs in the spring. A single monarch's lifespan is typically less than two months, so the entire migratory cycle involves several generations. The butterflies migrate south because they cannot survive freezing temperatures and return north because their larval food plants do not grow at their wintering sites. The research team analyzed over 50 years of migration data to uncover how monarchs navigate to their winter habitats in Mexico—a journey most complete only a part of in their lifetime. The study found that when butterflies are blown off course, they likely use major landmarks such as coastlines, and the Rocky and Appalachian Mountains to reorient themselves. Monarchs don't appear to detect shifts in longitude, which could otherwise leave them lost. To support this, lead researcher Rachael Derbyshire and her team tested butterflies' flight patterns in Ontario and in Calgary, 2,500 kilometers away. In both locations, the butterflies flew in the same general southwest direction, indicating they did not perceive the displacement. Further analysis of monarchs tagged and recaptured across North America from 1952 to 2004 confirmed that migrating monarchs do not use an internal map to reach Mexico. Instead, they navigate using prominent landmarks. Professor Ryan Norris highlighted, 'Given the challenge of this migratory journey and the fact that these insects weigh less than a gram, it's remarkable that they travel thousands of kilometers to a site they've never seen.' Despite these insights, the exact method monarchs use to locate their overwintering sites in central Mexico remains unknown. Derbyshire proposes that, like some other migratory animals, monarchs could be using their sense of smell to find the precise location—a hypothesis that still requires testing.

article_content: Joyce Ladner, an 80-year-old civil rights activist, reflects on her memory of standing on the Lincoln Memorial stage during the 1963 March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. She still remembers being moved by the sight of 250,000 people gathered—the largest peaceful demonstration in America at the time. This historic march, renowned for Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech, played a pivotal role in paving the way for landmark civil rights laws. While many know King's speech, fewer recognize Bayard Rustin as the driving force behind the event's organization. Despite facing prejudice for being openly gay, even from some fellow activists, Rustin masterminded the logistics and inspired a tide of volunteers in just eight weeks. Netflix’s film 'Rustin' (streaming Nov. 17) finally brings his lesser-known story into the spotlight. Roy Wilkins of the NAACP initially removed Rustin from his leadership role, but A. Philip Randolph—appointed director—restored Rustin as deputy director, giving him practical control even if not in title. Together, their efforts were saluted by Life Magazine, which ran a cover of Randolph and Rustin following the march, hailing its ‘astonishingly well-executed’ organization. Joyce Ladner, along with Eleanor Holmes Norton—now a U.S. congresswoman—and Ladner’s sister Dorie, were young members of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee. They worked out of a modest Harlem workspace, the Utopia Neighborhood Club House, and often stayed in the apartment of logistics leader Rachelle Horowitz. These stories are now depicted in 'Rustin', with Ladner even visiting the set during filming. In interviews, Ladner and Norton recall how Rustin guided them and countless other volunteers through the hard labor of recruiting, fundraising, and organizing. Norton notes how remarkable it was that, in just two months, Rustin and the team could coordinate such a monumental gathering—which included 22,000 chartered buses, 40 special trains, several flights, and high-profile supporters like Harry Belafonte and Marlon Brando. The national scale of the march marked the first time the civil rights struggle became a shared, collective experience across the country, according to Ladner. She says it gave ‘ownership’ of the movement to every American. Despite Rustin's accomplishments, he endured both external and internal discrimination. Suspicions about his sexuality led figures like Roy Wilkins to sideline him, while Adam Clayton Powell and Strom Thurmond resorted to threats and public smears, including references to a past arrest. Nevertheless, Ladner praises Rustin’s resilience, noting how rare it was at the time for someone to be openly gay, let alone an influential leader. Rustin stood true to himself and to the cause, undeterred by stigma or persecution.

Sanajan sukses sane wenten ring Rustin, ia tetap ngalaksanayang diskriminasi saking jaba lan ring tim sane nglaksanayang gawain. Masalah indetitas gender nyane ngantosang Roy Wilkins utawi pihak lianan nenten ngajengang, riantukan Adam Clayton Powell lan Strom Thurmond ngantosangang fitnah lan ngidangang kasus masa kepungkur nyane Rustin. Nanging, Ladner tetap nyujurang ketangguhan Rustin ring waktu puniki—wentenin wantah ring jagat sane terang ngejangang dirinye pinaka gay, apalagi dados pemimpin penggerak. Rustin tetap sadar sane ia dados sareng perjuangan, nenten keanggen raina utawi ancaman.

article_content: Jody Lee Hunt, the main suspect in a deadly string of shootings that claimed four lives in Monongalia County, West Virginia, was confirmed dead, according to both state police and the county’s Homeland Security Emergency Management Agency. Authorities did not disclose how or where Hunt died. Police had launched a search for Hunt, suspected of carrying out attacks at three different sites throughout Monongalia County in the northeastern part of the state. Among these, one shooting happened in Westover and another in an unincorporated area of the county. Investigators say Hunt knew each of the victims and point to substantial evidence—such as activity on his social media accounts—linking him to the shootings. State Police Lieutenant Michael Baylous mentioned that while investigators have possible theories about motive, they are not ready to release those details right now.

article_content:
TIME sat down with Humza Yousaf in Edinburgh this August, spotlighting him as Scotland’s first Muslim and non-white, as well as its youngest, First Minister. Yousaf assumed the role following Nicola Sturgeon’s abrupt departure, and has since faced a turbulent start, marked by an ongoing SNP finances investigation and pessimistic projections for his party’s performance.

Rather than enjoying a grace period, Yousaf’s early tenure has featured internal party divisions, police probes, and challenges from Westminster, which continues to block another independence referendum. The UK Supreme Court confirmed Scotland needs British government consent for a vote, yet Yousaf argues showing strong, steady support among Scots could eventually push Westminster to act. He refers to how Scotland’s own Parliament once came about when public support could no longer be ignored.

Political competition in Scotland is intensifying, with Labour led by Keir Starmer aiming for gains essential to forming a UK government. The current by-election, triggered by Margaret Ferrier’s COVID-19 rule-breaking, is seen as a tough first test for Yousaf, who warns Labour against complacency and criticizes Starmer's approach for lacking bold vision and authenticity.

A separate flashpoint is the UK government vetoing Scotland’s gender recognition reform legislation. Yousaf sees this as undermining Scottish democracy and connects his advocacy for trans and minority rights to his personal experience as someone from a marginalized group, stating that defending these rights is vital for society as a whole.

Yousaf associates many of Scotland’s economic and social difficulties with its status within the UK and the repercussions of Brexit, believing independence offers a path to improvement. 

He also recalls apprehension about sharing his family’s Ramadan celebrations publicly, but his wife encouraged him to embrace their identity. Such openness has helped highlight growing diversity at the top of UK politics, alongside figures like Rishi Sunak, Sadiq Khan, and Anas Sarwar.

article_content: Reflecting on what 2012 could bring for Google, it’s helpful to review the company’s eventful previous year. While major product launches—a social network, a mobile payment system, and a music store—grabbed headlines, the most intriguing developments were the products and features Google discontinued in 2011. Google routinely undertakes 'spring cleaning' to trim its portfolio, but the number and significance of projects cut last year were notable. Many of these were initially intended as major company focuses. Among the services discontinued or merged with others were Buzz, Knol, Checkout, PowerMeter, Health, and Wave. Even its initiative targeting coal-fired power plants was dropped. This large-scale streamlining reflects the leadership style of CEO Larry Page, who returned to the role after a decade with Eric Schmidt at the helm. During Schmidt’s tenure, Google focused on broad experimentation. Now under Page, the company is moving forward with a sharper focus. Google’s recent moves under Page clarify which technologies have the company’s strongest commitment—products failing to meet that bar have been discontinued. While seriousness is not the same as success, it is a critical foundation. Google is moving aggressively in social networking, mobile payments, and mobile devices, with fierce competition ahead in 2012. Google+ emerges as a key product. Launched in 2011, it combines elements from Twitter and Facebook but stands as a unique platform. The launch quickly drew in tech- and media-savvy users, but Google+ remains relatively unknown to the general public and is perceived as mainly for technology enthusiasts. For wider adoption, Google must highlight its unique features, such as multi-user video Hangouts, and clarify its identity beyond being 'like Facebook.' Users themselves are shaping the platform, with many treating it as a dynamic blogging service. Still, it’s unlikely Google+ will surpass Facebook’s user base, which is expected to reach one billion this year. Android faces ongoing criticism over device fragmentation—differing hardware and software across numerous devices hinder consistent updates. Google’s acquisition of Motorola aims to improve this by ensuring clear upgrade paths for Motorola devices, while also encouraging other partners to align with Google’s approach. Concerns about Android malware have grown. While Google has responded effectively to threats, a more proactive security strategy may be necessary, potentially through acquiring a security company like Lookout. Tablet competition presents challenges. The Amazon Kindle Fire has become the top-selling Android tablet, despite not running Google’s tablet-optimized operating system. Amazon’s unique platform on Android has outpaced Google’s own efforts. Google Books and Google TV have struggled, while Google Music is newly launched with limited recognition. As tablets remain primarily media consumption devices, Google’s limited content offerings have hampered its competitive standing. Improving content quality and reputation will be essential before Google can challenge Apple or Amazon in this space. Original content on YouTube is a positive first step, with more expansion expected in 2012. Google’s dominance in cloud services is likely to strengthen with the anticipated launch of GDrive, a Dropbox-like storage platform. Google’s reputation in search, email, and the cloud remains formidable, with Bing rising slowly and Gmail widely regarded as a top email service. Overall, Larry Page’s leadership has refocused Google—investing in strong-performing products and ending weaker ones. Although the outcomes of some bets, such as mobile payments or renewable energy, remain uncertain, Page has shown the capacity to marshal Google’s resources behind promising opportunities. article_content: The Nevada desert, generally known for its vast casinos and luxury hotels, is set to become a major hub for the automotive industry as Tesla’s $5 billion Gigafactory takes shape. This massive project is part of co-founder and CEO Elon Musk’s efforts to reduce the cost of electric vehicles. In September, the South African-born entrepreneur announced that a site near Reno, Nevada, had been selected for the lithium-ion battery plant. The Gigafactory is expected to cut the price of the Tesla Model 3 by nearly $3,000. Once completed, the Gigafactory will be able to produce 500,000 lithium-ion batteries per year and will cover between 5 and 10 million square feet, an area comparable to the size of the Pentagon. The project began in July with site preparation at an industrial park along U.S. Interstate 80, about 15 miles east of Sparks, a suburb of Reno. Since then, construction has progressed quickly, with partial production scheduled to start in 2017 and full completion targeted for 2020. The facility aims to supply enough batteries for 500,000 vehicles annually and to provide batteries for use in electronics like toys and drones. Currently, Tesla’s production is based in Fremont, California, but that facility cannot satisfy the company’s future needs. The new factory is projected to generate 6,500 permanent jobs in Nevada and provide $100 billion in economic benefits, according to CNBC. In return, the state has offered Tesla up to $1.3 billion in tax incentives. Construction has already created 700 jobs, with projections indicating the Gigafactory will boost the area’s population by 35,000 by 2032. Panasonic is a key partner in the project, reportedly investing billions of dollars. Despite Reno attracting companies like Apple and Amazon, some concerns remain about whether local infrastructure can handle the expected increase in demand. Nevada Governor Brian Sandoval said the Gigafactory further establishes the state as a leader in technological innovation, also noting major expansions like the Switch data center. Overall, Nevada’s population is expected to grow by 528,000 over the next 20 years to 3.3 million, with the Gigafactory having a particularly significant impact on northern Nevada. Images from nearby hills highlight the scale and isolation of the project, while ongoing road improvements are expected to benefit the state and help support new business ventures around the factory. An artist’s rendering shows what the completed site could look like in 2020. Elon Musk’s ambitious project aims to make electric cars more affordable and further solidify Nevada’s position in the future of technology.

article_content: MEXICO CITY — Thousands of people gathered on Saturday to watch Mexico City’s Day of the Dead parade as costumed dancers, drummers, and floats made their way down Paseo de la Reforma boulevard to the historic main square. The parade featured marching bands dressed as skeletons and dancers with skull face paint wearing Indigenous costumes. The scent of traditional copal incense filled the air. A skeleton drum group played samba rhythms, while dancers nearby twirled in skirts painted to resemble monarch butterfly wings. Monarch butterflies traditionally return to Mexico for the winter around the Day of the Dead. A group of drag performers dressed as 'Catrinas,' skeleton figures in 1870s-style fashion, reflected social change during the event. The holiday begins on October 31, to remember those who died in accidents, continues on November 1 to honor children who have passed away, and on November 2 to celebrate adults who have died. The city also marks the Day of the Dead with a large altar and a procession of colorful, fantastical sculptures known as 'alebrijes.' While such parades are new to most of Mexico’s Day of the Dead traditions, the southern state of Oaxaca holds similar 'muerteadas' celebrations. Mexico City adopted the Hollywood-style parade in 2016 after the 2015 James Bond film 'Spectre,' which featured a fictional Day of the Dead parade in its opening scenes shot in the city. Inspired by the film, officials organized their own version, drawing millions of viewers and visitors. Mexico City resident Rocío Morán attended the parade in skull makeup. Morán, who runs a company that measures ratings, said she supports the blending of old and new traditions. 'It became fashionable with the James Bond movie, and I think it's good because it brings economic activity to the city,' Morán said. 'I like it. I like progress, I like that tourists are coming to see this.' 'I think that Day of the Dead has always existed,' Morán added. 'Now they’re using marketing and visualization so the whole world can see it.'
