article_content: Conservative MP John Whittingdale has criticized the Hacked Off campaign for refusing to negotiate over proposals for press regulation. Whittingdale, who chairs the Culture, Media and Sport Select Committee, warned that the position taken by Hacked Off—an organization closely linked to the Labour Party—could result in no Royal Charter for a new press watchdog, which he described as a 'disaster.' He said that the group's refusal to consider compromise may mean that even if a 'recognition body' for the Press is created, no newspapers may seek recognition, undermining the system. After rejecting a plan drawn up by politicians and Hacked Off, British newspapers proposed their own independent Royal Charter for press regulation. Whittingdale stated he would 'nearly sign' the Press's proposed charter but found progress difficult due to opposition from Labour and Hacked Off. At a Broadcasting Press Guild event, he remarked: 'We are either very close to a happy outcome or a total shambles. The Labour Party still seems very much tied to Hacked Off. If Labour refuses to discuss changes to the Government's version, reaching an agreement may be impossible.' He added: 'Hacked Off has clearly rejected the industry's watchdog proposal and insists that Parliament’s decision must be followed.' Professor Brian Cathcart, executive director of Hacked Off, appeared alongside Jacqui Hames and Charlotte Church. A Hacked Off spokesperson said: 'The Royal Charter approved by Parliament has the support of all parties, victims of press abuse, and most of the public. Unfortunately, some in the Press have resisted change, and the draft charter now proposed by newspapers reflects this.' However, Lord Wakeham, former president of the Privy Council, pointed out that Parliament had not voted on the March 18 charter but only on a motion to consider the Prime Minister's intention to submit it to the Privy Council.

article_content: Google has come under scrutiny after a Harvard University professor alleged that its advertising system shows signs of racial bias. The study found that online ads suggesting criminality appeared more often when searching for names typically associated with Black individuals, compared to those associated with White individuals. Professor Latanya Sweeney’s research revealed that searches using Black-sounding names, such as 'Ebony' and 'DeShawn,' were 25 percent more likely to yield ads related to criminal records than searches with White-sounding names like 'Jill' and 'Geoffrey.' This is concerning because people commonly use Google to look up potential employees, clients, or acquaintances. Sweeney analyzed over 2,000 racially suggestive names by entering them into Google and Reuters' Google-powered platform, then documented the ads that appeared. She discovered that while most names returned ads for public records in general, Black-sounding names were far more likely to trigger ads featuring the word 'arrest.' These ads were primarily for the background-check service instantcheckmate.com. For example, searches for Latanya Farrell, Latanya Sweeney, and Latanya Lockett each generated ads for arrest-checking services, yet only Latanya Lockett had an actual arrest record. In contrast, searches for White-sounding names such as Kristen Haring, Kristen Sparrow, and Kristen Lindquist did not yield the same ads, even when instantcheckmate.com’s own database listed arrest records for some of those individuals. The study’s findings are particularly relevant given the documented racial disparities in arrests—for instance, in the UK, Black individuals are 3.3 times more likely than White individuals to be arrested, and those of mixed ethnicity are 2.3 times more likely. Additional research highlighted in the article shows that individuals with stronger implicit racial biases may literally perceive Black and White faces as more different based on brain activity. These findings raise important questions about whether Google’s advertising algorithms are unintentionally reflecting or amplifying societal biases. Google and instantcheckmate.com both denied intentionally engaging in racial profiling, maintaining that ad placement is dictated by advertiser choices and neutral algorithms. Google stated that its policies prohibit ads advocating against any person or group, while Instant Checkmate emphasized their systems do not consider the race linked to a name. The study was supported by the National Science Foundation and received a grant from Google.

article_content: Victoria Meppen-Walter, a 44-year-old former teacher, died by suicide after suffering severe distress following a mole removal at the Transform Clinic in Greater Manchester in 2011. She held the clinic and her surgeon responsible, leaving heartfelt notes describing her pain and emotional turmoil. Victoria told her husband, Ashley, about persistent burning and stabbing pains in her face, neck, and chest post-surgery. She felt her appearance had been altered so much that she no longer recognized herself, leading her to avoid social contact. In her suicide note, she asked that the surgeon's name be engraved on her headstone as a symbol of her suffering, stating she wished life was about happiness, not constant pain. Ashley recalled the procedure was meant to last only 25 minutes but became problematic with unexpected bleeding and eventually a permanent scar. After the operation, Victoria became withdrawn, depressed, and often mentioned suicide. Her disappearance led her family to search their home. Her body was found days later in a locked spare room, and initially, Ashley, their daughter, and another man were briefly arrested but cleared of suspicion soon after. Transform Clinic stated that the standard of care given to Victoria was high and suggested her difficulties may not have been caused solely by the operation. The surgeon said Victoria had a skin cancer diagnosis and prior psychiatric care; authorities were involved at times due to challenging circumstances. Victoria was also the step-grandmother of former footballer Courtney Meppen-Walter, who was imprisoned after a fatal car crash.

article_content: Billionaire Citadel founder Ken Griffin appears to have shifted his support in the GOP presidential primary, now favoring former South Carolina Gov. Nikki Haley. Griffin stated, 'We're going to see Governor DeSantis face pressure to justify and explain his decisions, and that's an opportunity for him to mature.' He added that DeSantis needs to win Iowa to remain competitive. Regarding another candidate, Griffin commented that Chris Christie—supported by billionaire Steve Cohen—would have to win New Hampshire to continue his campaign. Griffin, who leads Citadel and Citadel Securities, has been vocal about seeking a Republican alternative to former President Donald Trump, who currently leads the polls despite facing several indictments. Speaking at the Robin Hood charity event, Griffin suggested there is a meaningful chance that someone other than Trump or President Joe Biden could win the 2024 election. Citadel declined to comment on the event. Griffin also addressed financial market risks, especially the growing adoption of passive investment strategies in the derivatives market. He warned that these strategies may not provide sufficient liquidity during market turbulence. Addressing the conference audience, he emphasized the role of active managers in maintaining efficient capital markets and urged the SEC to encourage active management and support the hedge fund sector, rather than imposing additional burdens.

article_content: A recent investigation has revealed that many UK patients face high charges when calling NHS GP surgeries using 0844 or 0845 phone numbers, especially from mobile phones. Patients seeking to book appointments often experience hold times of up to 30 minutes, sometimes incurring bills as high as £12. Callers are not informed that mobile rates can reach up to 41p per minute, compared to as little as 2p per minute when calling standard landline numbers. It is estimated that six million patients are affected nationwide, with companies providing these numbers generating significant profits. Daisy Surgery Line, the largest provider with contracts at around 1,000 GP practices, made £5.8 million in profit from £14 million in sales last year. The company was founded by Matthew Riley in 2001, who is reportedly worth £85 million. The investigation by the Sunday Mirror involved 80 surgeries. The longest recorded wait was nearly 29 minutes at Dun Cow Surgery in south London, costing a mobile caller £11.82 at 41p per minute. Calling from a BT landline at 5p per minute would have cost only £1.43. At Crawcrook Surgery in Gateshead, a wait of just over 13 minutes cost £5.36 from a mobile, or 65p via a landline. Padiham Medical Centre in Burnley kept callers on hold for eight minutes and 20 seconds, racking up a bill of £3.41 from a 40p-per-minute BT landline. In all cases, patients were not warned about the potential costs when calling the 0844 and 0845 numbers from mobiles. The average recorded wait time was one minute and 54 seconds. A spokesperson for the Patients' Association told the Sunday Mirror, 'It is morally wrong for GPs to charge patients these rates – many have no idea. This needs to be stopped.' Former Labour Minister John Healey, who successfully campaigned for local GPs to drop such lines, added, 'No one should be forced to use these rip-off numbers. The government needs to enforce the rules.' In 2010, the Department of Health urged GPs to phase out these premium-rate lines, but many medical centres are locked into long-term contracts with telecom providers. Dun Cow Surgery stated that the 28-minute wait was 'definitely not typical,' while Crawcrook Surgery attributed its delay to a 'major problem' with its phone system. Crawcrook also noted it installed the 0844 number after patients complained their standard lines were often busy. A Daisy Surgery Line spokesperson said, 'It's important to note that 084 numbers are not premium-rate numbers. NHS regulations permit their use as long as patients are not charged more than a local rate call. Surgery Line also offers the option of a geographic number.'

article_content: ‘It’s a Wonderful Knife’ begins with all the charm of a classic Christmas movie, featuring cheerful scenes and bright visuals. But this festive atmosphere is soon interrupted by shocking, violent events. The creators purposely set up this contrast to breathe new life into the slasher genre by blending it with holiday spirit. Screenwriter Michael Kennedy says their goal was to subvert expectations, turning familiar moments into surprises. The movie is a horror version of ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’: just as George Bailey once wished he’d never existed, Winnie Carruthers makes the same wish, only to find that a masked killer has reappeared in her absence. Known as the Angel, this frightening figure terrorizes the town in the alternate reality. ‘It’s a Wonderful Knife’ is part of a modern wave of horror films that twist well-known stories, such as ‘Happy Death Day’ and ‘Freaky,’ both connected to Kennedy and Christopher Landon. Kennedy conceived the film during pandemic lockdowns, seeking something positive despite the gruesome content. He takes pride in viewers calling it a wholesome slasher. Director Tyler MacIntyre, who grew up enjoying horror comedies, finds that humor and horror go hand in hand, both relying on the element of surprise. He modeled the film’s setting on beloved Christmas films like ‘Miracle on 34th Street’ and ‘Home Alone,’ using these visuals to set up dramatic turns. The movie skillfully moves between the cozy feelings of a holiday favorite and the unsettling reality of its alternate timeline, offering unexpected fun through this sharp contrast. Kennedy hints at another project in the works with Landon, though it might not have the same genre mashup. ‘It’s a Wonderful Knife’ is currently in theaters, starring Jane Widdop as Winnie, with Justin Long, Joel McHale, and Jess McLeod co-starring. Follow the reporter’s social media for more film news.

article_content: Anheuser-Busch InBev, the world's largest beer producer, notes that India's stable business climate and robust economic growth have elevated the country's status as a key investment destination. However, the company advocates for reforms in alcohol excise laws to further stimulate demand. Jan Craps, co-chair and CEO of Budweiser APAC—the Asia-Pacific division of AB InBev, which owns Budweiser, Corona, and Hoegaarden—remarked, 'India's stable business environment and strong GDP growth have improved its investment appeal. To make the environment even more attractive, changes such as reduced taxes on beer and more predictable regulations would be beneficial.' He added, 'Over the past decade, we've invested $1.5 billion in India and pay nearly $500 million in taxes annually.' AB InBev, based in Belgium, produces about a quarter of the world's beer. India has now become the fourth-largest market for Budweiser by volume, moving up from sixth place last year after surpassing Canada and the UK. Premium brands now account for about two-thirds of AB InBev’s sales in India, compared to a third three years ago. The company has expanded its portfolio in India, introducing energy drinks, whiskey, spiced rum, vodka, and gin. India, with its warm climate, youthful demographics, and growing affluence, remains a significant market for global brewers. Still, it is heavily taxed and has only 80,000 alcohol retail licenses, including stores, pubs, and bars. Each year, over 20 million people reach legal drinking age. Yet, beer represents only 10% of India's spirits market, with per capita beer consumption at just 2 liters—lower than most other Asian countries. Craps stated, 'Excise on beer is nearly 1.8 times higher than on whiskey, influencing consumers to choose higher-alcohol beverages. This tax disparity restricts beer consumption.' He also mentioned that in some states, AB InBev has to wait for payment until beer is sold, while others allow deferred taxation, offering a more favorable business climate and supporting investments and cash flow. United Breweries, owner of Kingfisher, leads the Indian beer segment with over half of the market, while AB InBev holds about a 23% share. Strong beer comprises over 80% of beer volumes in India, and many drinkers also purchase lower-priced spirits. According to IWSR Drinks Market Analysis, if beer prices rise due to regulations, consumers may choose cheaper Indian-made foreign liquor instead. The company pointed to West Bengal as an example, where reducing beer taxes led to a 90% increase in consumption and a 40% rise in excise revenue.

article_content: Scientists have discovered 13 mummified leaf-eared mice atop three volcanoes in Chile and Argentina, prompting new questions about mammalian survival at extreme altitudes. The mummies were found at elevations around 20,000 feet above sea level, where freezing temperatures, low oxygen levels, and high winds dominate a barren landscape of rock, ice, and snow. Jay Storz, a biologist at the University of Nebraska—Lincoln and lead author of the study, described these volcano summits as 'incredibly hostile environments, especially for small, warm-blooded animals like mice.' Leaf-eared mice are known to inhabit high elevations, but previously, such extreme heights were thought to be completely uninhabitable for mammals. The findings suggest that these mice have been reaching the volcano summits for hundreds, if not thousands, of years. According to Storz, the species has inhabited the high Andes for many hundreds of thousands of years, indicating they could have regularly visited these summits over a long period. Significantly, the research team also found a living mouse and evidence of active burrows at similar altitudes. This represents the highest recorded altitude for mammalian life anywhere in the world. The study was published Monday in the journal Current Biology. Storz and his colleagues began unearthing freeze-dried mouse remains—some just decades old, others several centuries—in the crevices of volcanic rock. Genomic analysis revealed equal numbers of male and female mice, with some closely related individuals, hinting at the existence of established mouse communities rather than sporadic visitors. While the motivation for the mice’s high-altitude habit remains unclear, Storz suggests one potential benefit is the lack of predators atop these volcanoes. However, many mysteries remain, including how the mice manage to survive in such harsh conditions. Researchers are continuing to investigate potential physiological adaptations that allow these mice to withstand low oxygen levels. By collecting mice from various elevations and subjecting them to controlled experiments, the team hopes to identify unique survival traits among the summit-dwelling mice. Storz and his team continue to search volcano summits for further evidence of mice, both living and mummified. He commented, 'Whether it’s the top of the highest mountains or the darkest depths of the ocean, it’s always exciting to discover animals living where nobody expects them.'

Tikus-tikus puniki kapanggih ring ketinggian sekitar 20.000 kaki saking segara, ring kayun suhu kadek lokalang suba, oksigen alit ring udara, miwah angin kenceng nyeken padag batu, es, miwah salju. article_content: A recent study has found that people are more likely to die at Christmas than at any other time of the year. U.S. researchers examined death certificates and discovered that the highest risk days for death are Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year’s Day. This pattern was seen among those dying of natural causes, such as circulatory problems, respiratory diseases, and cancer. The trend holds true for all age groups except children. Researchers from the University of California, San Diego, led by Professor David Phillips, reported that people of all ages except children are affected. CNN covered the findings. A similar study in Britain found that emergency hospital admissions on Christmas Day are also associated with a higher risk of death compared to other days, including weekends. The team is unsure why death rates are higher during the Christmas period but suggested several theories. Some believe it could be due to increased stress or feelings of sadness during the holidays. Obituary writer Andrew Meacham told CNN that he notices an increase in obituaries during this time and has observed patterns such as one partner dying soon after the other, suggesting a possible mind-body connection. Professor Phillips also studied deaths in people with Alzheimer’s disease and found more cardiac-related deaths during the holidays. He hypothesizes that stress and changes to routine for those with dementia could be factors. To rule out cold weather as a cause, the team compared colder U.S. states to warmer ones and found the increase was actually lower in cold states bordering Canada than in those near the Gulf of Mexico. They also considered if festive eating and drinking could be responsible, but saw increased deaths even among hospital inpatients with controlled diets. Surprisingly, suicide and homicide rates are at their lowest in December. The researchers believe reduced access to healthcare during the holidays is the most likely explanation. Some people put off seeing a doctor, and hospitals may have fewer staff available, increasing the risk. The spike is especially notable among emergency trauma cases, where staff experience can make a critical difference, Professor Phillips noted. Meanwhile, experts at New York University reported that heart problems—including both fatal and nonfatal heart attacks and irregular heartbeats—also rise at Christmas, according to CBS News. Possible causes include stress, cold weather, or overindulgence, though no single reason is definitive.

article_content: LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) – Comic book fans have long awaited a film adaptation of 'Watchmen,' the acclaimed graphic novel about misfit crimefighters confronting a plot against them as the threat of nuclear war looms. Malin Akerman, who plays Laurie Jupiter/Silk Spectre II, says the film will make fans proud. Now that the movie is complete and scheduled for release on Friday, the cast is confident it will meet high expectations. "We've heard from diehard fans who say they're really impressed," Akerman said. She praised director Zack Snyder, known for '300' and 'Dawn of the Dead,' crediting his passion and attention to the original story for the film's authenticity. "This was a huge undertaking for Zack, but his dedication as a true fan meant he remained faithful to the material," she added. 'Watchmen' took years to reach the screen. The original comic series, created by Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons, was published in 1986-87, later compiled into a graphic novel, and recognized by Time magazine as one of the 20th century's greatest novels. The adaptation passed through several studios and directors, such as Terry Gilliam and Paul Greengrass, before landing at Warner Bros. with Zack Snyder. Snyder, a longtime fan, insisted on staying true to the source material. Deborah Snyder, his wife and producing partner, affirmed his commitment to fidelity in adaptation. Jackie Earle Haley, who plays Rorschach, believes Snyder's dedication will resonate with fans. "The film elevates the comic book movie genre, just as 'Watchmen' did for comics—it adds depth and intelligence," Haley explained. Jeffrey Dean Morgan (Edward Blake/The Comedian) acknowledged the scrutiny from fans but is confident the film will surpass their high expectations. Recreating the alternate 1985 setting, with the U.S. and Soviet Union on the brink of nuclear war, required close attention to period details. Superhero features like the flying ship 'Archie' and Dr. Manhattan, a powerful blue figure played by Billy Crudup, called for advanced visual effects. Carla Gugino, as Sally Jupiter, Laurie’s mother and an original crimefighter, said her transformation with age makeup helped her fully embrace the character. Billy Crudup was amazed by the computer-generated effects used to portray Dr. Manhattan. The cast expressed excitement for their roles. Morgan noted that playing a superhero fulfilled his childhood dreams. "We got to play superheroes, which I loved as a kid. Now I get to do it as an adult," he said. CNN.com's Elham Khatami contributed to this report.

article_content: Thousands of master’s students from Mumbai University who took their final semester exams in June and July are still awaiting their results. All MA results, including those from distance education, are pending, and several key MSc results are yet to be released. For some subjects, even semester III results were announced only a few days ago, delaying students’ future plans such as job applications and PhD enrollments. Although the university's examination section stated that the pending results will be announced soon, teachers attributed the delay to technical issues with the on-screen assessment software. An MA (Economics) student from a college in the western suburbs explained that she had to forgo a PhD seat in Surat this year because her master’s degree results were not declared on time. She said, 'My final exam was in the first week of June. I secured a PhD seat, but lost the admission because the institute required my master’s degree. I have already lost a year. However, some colleges have given provisional admissions, but students may lose those if scorecards aren't submitted soon.' A university official from the examination department confirmed that results for MSc in IT, biotechnology, statistics, life sciences, biophysics, and bioanalytical science have already been announced. The assessment of MA papers, including distance education, is complete and results will be declared soon, the official said. Assessment for other MSc subjects, such as physics and chemistry, is nearly done, with results expected soon. A physics teacher mentioned that results for other MSc semester III papers were announced recently, but results for physics and chemistry have been delayed. 'Semester IV results will be released only after semester III results are declared. There was a problem with the assessment software. Some teachers couldn’t log in on time, and others had trouble accessing papers. While the software's security system was robust, it also made assessing the papers challenging,' said the teacher.

article_content: Prior to the launch of the Quest 3, it was assumed that the new pancake lenses, with a 40% slimmer optic profile than those in the Quest 2, would make the headset lighter and more comfortable. However, this is only partly true. The Meta Quest 3 actually weighs 12 grams more than the Oculus Quest 2. While this difference is small, the Quest 3 offers a snugger, more supported fit right out of the box. When asked about the increased weight, a Meta PR representative explained that the Quest 3 and Quest 2 are not directly comparable in terms of weight because they use different components. The Quest 3 introduces a mixed-reality depth sensor, new RGB cameras, and an optical distance adjuster, all of which contribute to the extra weight. Additional upgrades like the Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 processor and more RAM support enhanced games but also add to the overall weight. The Quest 3 features a larger face gasket that allows users to adjust the distance of the pancake lenses from their face, leaving enough space for glasses. Looking from the side, the white plastic of the headset is slimmer, while the silicone area is wider than before. Hands-on testing praised the Quest 3 for its better center of gravity, making it more comfortable than the front-heavy Quest 2. Improved venting and more space for glasses were also noted. A second cloth strap provides additional support, though it may add a bit to the overall weight. Although slightly heavier, the Quest 3 is seen as a design improvement thanks to its upgraded features. Without the new pancake lenses, it likely would have been even heavier due to the other enhancements over the Quest 2. Still, those expecting a very light headset may find the Quest 3 somewhat heavy. It weighs just over a pound, with most of the weight at the front. Similar to the Quest 2, users may want to purchase the Elite Strap with battery for a more secure fit and better weight balance. This accessory adds about $130 to the $500 headset price, which could be costly for budget-conscious VR fans. Preordering the 128GB Meta Quest 3 before October 9 includes a free copy of Asgard’s Wrath 2 (valued at $59.99) and a six-month Meta Quest Plus subscription (normally $7.99 per month).

Walaupun selisihnya sedikit, Quest 3 memberikan fitting yang lebih pas dan dukungan yang lebih baik langsung dari kotak. Menanggapi soal tambahan berat tersebut, perwakilan PR Meta menjelaskan bahwa Quest 3 dan Quest 2 tidak bisa dibandingkan langsung, karena menggunakan komponen yang cukup berbeda. Quest 3 punya sensor kedalaman mixed-reality, kamera RGB baru, dan optical distance adjuster, semua menambah berat. Tambahan prosesor Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 dan RAM ekstra juga meningkatkan kemampuan gaming, tapi berkontribusi pada berat total. Quest 3 punya gasket muka yang lebih besar, sehingga pengguna dapat mengatur jarak lensa pancake dari wajahnya, memberi ruang untuk kacamata. Dilihat dari samping, plastik putih headset lebih ramping, sementara bagian silikon lebih lebar daripada sebelumnya. Dari uji coba langsung, Quest 3 mendapat pujian soal pusat gravitasi yang lebih baik, jadi lebih nyaman dibanding Quest 2 yang berat di depan. Ventilasi lebih baik dan ruang untuk kacamata juga jadi kelebihan. Strap kain kedua menambah dukungan, walau juga sedikit menambah berat. Meski sedikit lebih berat, Quest 3 diakui sebagai peningkatan desain karena fitur-fitur barunya. Tanpa lensa pancake, kemungkinan akan jauh lebih berat karena banyak peningkatan lain dibanding Quest 2. Meski begitu, buat yang berharap headset super ringan bisa merasa agak kecewa. Quest 3 masih lebih dari satu pon, dengan sebagian besar berat di bagian depan. Sama seperti Quest 2, disarankan menggunakan Elite Strap dengan baterai agar lebih nyaman dan seimbang. Tapi, aksesori ini menambah sekitar $130 ke harga headset $500, yang mungkin memberatkan untuk penggemar VR dengan anggaran terbatas. Pemesanan Quest 3 128GB sebelum 9 Oktober akan mendapatkan gratis Asgard's Wrath 2 (senilai $59.99) dan langganan Meta Quest Plus enam bulan (biasanya $7,99 per bulan).

article_content: Manuel Pellegrini has stated that Manchester City will be 'the team to beat' this season and aims to make at least one more signing before the season starts next month. The Chilean manager led City to a Premier League and Capital One Cup double in his first season in England and is determined to build on that success. City have already signed goalkeeper Willy Caballero, defender Bacary Sagna, and midfielder Fernando, and hope to add £32 million FC Porto centre-back Eliaquim Mangala before facing Arsenal in the Community Shield. Speaking ahead of City's opening game of their US tour against Sporting Kansas City, Pellegrini said, 'The squad isn’t finished and we will have until the end of the window to make our moves.' He added: 'We have options to change things. If we need another player or not, it’s very important to see what we have in these matches. Maybe one player will leave, but we have over a month to decide.' Pellegrini continued, 'This year may be difficult, but I think everyone knows Manchester City will be the team to beat. There are six strong teams who want to win the title, but we trust in our group of good players to repeat last season’s success.' 'One of our targets is to do well in the Champions League. Last year we reached the last 16 for the first time, but we are confident we can do better this year.' Pellegrini also acknowledged that rivals Manchester United will pose a greater threat under new manager Louis van Gaal after a disappointing season with David Moyes. He said, 'Of course, I think United will have a very different season compared to last year. Van Gaal is an experienced manager at big clubs, so we expect another strong competitor for the Premier League. United will be strong this year, even if we don’t know exactly what will happen.' Pellegrini confirmed that striker Alvaro Negredo has had surgery on his right foot after fracturing a metatarsal in last Friday's friendly against Hearts. Negredo, who had been linked with a move away before his injury, will be out for at least two months. 'Alvaro had surgery today on his broken foot and he will be a big miss for our squad because he is an important player for us,' said Pellegrini.

article_content: Ahead of the highly anticipated World Cup final between India and Australia, Australian captain Pat Cummins has urged his teammates to embrace the challenge of playing against a passionate home crowd in Ahmedabad. The final will take place on Sunday at the Narendra Modi Stadium, the world's largest cricket venue, which is expected to draw a record-breaking crowd of around 130,000 spectators. With the tournament held in India, the majority of fans will be rooting for the hosts, who are aiming for their third men's ODI World Cup title and their second win on home soil, following their 2011 victory. However, India faces a formidable opponent in five-time champions Australia. Cummins addressed the media at a pre-match news conference, acknowledging the one-sided support: 'I think you've got to embrace it, the crowd's obviously going to be very one-sided. But also, as an opposition player, there's nothing more satisfying than hearing a big crowd go silent, and that's our aim tomorrow.' He added that the team aims to finish their campaign with no regrets, noting that the experience of playing in such a large stadium is unique. Each Australian player has their own way of preparing for the occasion. For instance, David Warner is known for his energetic dancing, while others prefer a more focused approach. Cummins praised his squad's spirit and commitment throughout the tournament, saying, 'The guys have been awesome. They're up for every game. Reaching the final would cap off an incredible, potentially career-defining year for many of us.' In the semifinals, India secured their spot by defeating New Zealand with a comprehensive 70-run victory, thanks to strong batting performances from Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, and Shreyas Iyer, as well as a standout seven-wicket haul from Mohammed Shami. Australia narrowly overcame South Africa in their semifinal, winning by three wickets on a difficult pitch in Kolkata. Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc played crucial roles in steering their team to victory. The excitement around the match has driven hotel and flight prices in Ahmedabad to soar, with many fans adjusting plans in response to the increased costs. In other news, OpenAI recently ousted its CEO Sam Altman after internal disagreements on AI safety and business direction. Additionally, the Indian government has approved IT hardware manufacturing investments from 27 companies, including major global players.

article_content: President Joe Biden is attending this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in San Francisco to demonstrate ongoing U.S. engagement in the region despite multiple challenges at home and worldwide. The focus will be on Biden’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping as the leaders work to improve U.S.-China relations after a difficult year. Beyond China, the Biden administration aims to reassure Asia-Pacific nations that the U.S. remains committed to their interests while also managing conflicts like the Israel-Hamas war and sustaining aid to Ukraine as it resists Russia’s invasion. National security adviser Jake Sullivan noted that Biden’s schedule includes much more than talks with Xi. The president will present his economic agenda for the Pacific, spotlighting the U.S. as a driver of regional progress. He is set to introduce plans for clean energy investment and anti-corruption efforts through the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF), a strategic initiative launched last year. However, some APEC members remain wary. Interests such as bolstering supply chains and expanding clean energy cooperation are welcome, but many want more access to American markets—something Biden is hesitant to offer through new broad trade deals. Earlier trade agreements, like the Trans-Pacific Partnership, faltered after the U.S. pulled out in 2017, fueling ongoing skepticism. This week, Biden held talks with Indonesia’s President Joko Widodo at the White House to collaborate on climate and other priorities, even as they disagreed sharply regarding the Israel-Hamas war. Such differences echo broader frictions among summit participants. Reaching a unified declaration at the summit may prove difficult, given contrasting views, particularly about conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. U.S. APEC ambassador Matt Murray acknowledged efforts to build consensus face obstacles. Biden will also emphasize U.S. defense commitments to regional allies like the Philippines, especially after recent confrontations between Chinese and Philippine vessels in the disputed South China Sea. Regional tensions persist due to China’s territorial claims and North Korea’s nuclear activity. Meanwhile, the possibility of a U.S. government shutdown looms, as Congress struggles to finalize funding for foreign aid and border security. National security adviser Sullivan has warned that a shutdown could harm America’s credibility and reputation globally during these turbulent times.

Fokus utama ring warsa puniki punika presiden Biden ketemu Presiden Tiongkok, Xi Jinping, nglaksanayang upaya nyikang hubungan Amerika-Tiongkok sane ngametuangang warsa ringkang keras. article_content: A UK court heard allegations that human traffickers instruct some young adult asylum seekers to pretend to be minors to qualify for greater benefits. The case surfaced during a judicial review involving an Afghan asylum seeker claiming to be 16, though officials believe he is closer to 20. The individual's identity remains protected by a court order. He initially reported his age as 14 upon arrival in Britain in 2009. Social workers in the UK assessed him at intake and concluded he appeared to be an adult, possibly trained to behave as someone younger. With the support of public legal aid, he has challenged these conclusions at the High Court, contending that his appearance is influenced by his ethnicity. He also argued that learning difficulties would entitle him to full-time education in Britain until age 25. Ealing Borough Council assessors concluded he was over 18 and noted his avoidance of eye contact and hesitance during interviews, behaviors possibly stemming from outside guidance. Despite reserved behavior in interviews, he was quick to request legal counsel after placement with a foster family, and was seen using a mobile phone, the court heard. His asylum claim was rejected in May 2010 after a tribunal found his statements lacking credibility. Nonetheless, his removal from the UK, scheduled for November 2010, was postponed after his lawyers contested both the age assessment and the Home Office's removal decision. Child migrants in the UK receive benefits and support not given to adult migrants; being classed as a minor can increase the chance of remaining in the country. His barrister, Azeem Suterwalla, argued the age assessment didn't fully consider how ethnicity might affect appearance, and that youth in rural Middle Eastern areas may mature more quickly than British youth. He attributed some interview issues to learning difficulties, with a psychologist reporting his cognitive abilities were in the bottom one percent. An Afghan identity document provided gave a birth year of 1374 in the Afghan calendar (1995), but Mrs Justice Lang described it as 'mysterious.' After a day of arguments, Mrs Justice Lang reserved her decision, with a ruling to come later.

article_content: Patients admitted to Spanish hospitals on weekends are reportedly being given towels to use as makeshift pillows due to linen shortages. According to Spanish media, hospitals have outsourced linen cleaning to private firms to reduce costs, but these firms do not operate on Saturdays and Sundays, leading to a lack of pillows for some patients. A patient at Clinical Hospital in Valencia photographed a folded towel used as a pillow and sent the image to local news website LasProvincias.es. Reports indicate this issue is not isolated to Valencia, and similar incidents have occurred across various hospitals in Spain. Hospital sources described the situation as abnormal but acknowledged it was not uncommon, especially on busy weekends. Austerity measures imposed by the Spanish Department of Health have resulted in patients having to keep the same cutlery throughout their stay, and the midday glass of milk previously given to patients has been discontinued to save costs. Last month, thousands of healthcare workers protested in 16 Spanish cities against government budget cuts and plans to partially privatize the healthcare system. The government, led by Mariano Rajoy’s centre-right Popular Party, is trying to reduce the national deficit, leading to public spending cuts and high unemployment, which surpassed five million in February 2013.

article_content: The U.S. Justice Department has requested that the Ferguson, Missouri, Police Department instruct its officers not to wear bracelets supporting Darren Wilson, the white police officer who fatally shot unarmed black teenager Michael Brown last month. This incident sparked widespread protests in the predominantly African American city. In a letter to Ferguson Police Chief Tom Jackson, the Justice Department stated that residents observed officers wearing 'I am Darren Wilson' bracelets while managing protest sites. The Department noted that these bracelets have 'upset and agitated' people, reinforcing an 'us versus them' mentality that many Ferguson residents believe exists. The Justice Department has launched an investigation into both the shooting and the police department's handling of protesters—a response to criticism that officers used overly harsh tactics. County and state police officials assisting in Ferguson have assured federal investigators that their officers will not wear the bracelets. The Ferguson police could not be reached for comment. Additionally, the Justice Department sent a separate letter earlier in the week, observing that some Ferguson officers were not wearing name tags or had concealed them, which violates department rules. The letter stressed that such anonymity could suggest officers might act with impunity. After facing significant criticism and calls to resign, Chief Jackson issued a video apology to Brown’s parents and later joined a protest march. During the event, a disturbance broke out, leading to several arrests. A St. Louis County grand jury is also reviewing the case. Protesters continue to demand charges against Wilson and have called for Jackson’s removal. On Friday night, several dozen people assembled in downtown Ferguson, with police maintaining a low-key presence, in contrast to previous, more aggressive tactics. Despite Ferguson’s predominantly African American population, its police department and political leadership are mainly white. Activists argue that Michael Brown’s death is the result of years of unfair policing targeting black residents.

article_content: Hong Kong, China (CNN) -- Rapidly rising inflation in China has prompted the government to introduce new measures, according to state media on Wednesday. Initiatives under consideration include providing food subsidies, imposing price controls, increasing penalties for food speculation, and measures to prevent hoarding, China Daily reported. Mayors may also be held accountable for inadequate vegetable supplies and volatile prices. Inflation is rising so quickly in China that shoppers are crossing the border to Hong Kong to purchase essentials like meat and produce, bringing back as much as they can carry by train. Hong Kong, just a day trip from some mainland areas, offers mainland shoppers savings, including at fast-food restaurants like McDonald's. Due to rising food costs, McDonald's is raising menu prices in China by up to 1 yuan (approximately 15 US cents) per item, the first such increase this year, according to Xinhua. In contrast, McDonald's is maintaining its prices in Hong Kong. According to the Ministry of Commerce, average wholesale prices for 18 types of vegetables in 36 Chinese cities have surged by 62.4 percent compared to a year ago. Mainland shoppers in Hong Kong are also stockpiling other essentials like toilet paper, diapers, and shampoo, frequenting supermarkets and markets near train stations. One shopper noted that oranges in China sell for about twice as much as those in Hong Kong. The state-run Xinhua news agency reported last week that China's consumer price index (CPI) reached a 25-month high of 4.4 percent in October, exceeding the government's full-year inflation target of 3 percent. To stabilize prices, the Ministry of Commerce has released 62,400 tons of pork and 210,000 tons of sugar from reserves since the end of September. The ministry also states it will collaborate with other agencies in ongoing efforts to curb inflation. China is experiencing increased economic pressure due to substantial capital inflows, according to Central Bank Governor Zhou Xiaochuan cited by China Daily. In October, the country received approximately $7.7 billion in foreign direct investment, up 7.9 percent from a year earlier. Hong Kong functions as a special administrative region of China, generally governing itself. Unlike the yuan (renminbi), Hong Kong's currency is pegged to the U.S. dollar.

Inflasi ring Tiongkok prasida nyenahang warga nyanggra ring Hong Kong ngajeng ajengan utama, daging tur sayur, nyidangangang maneh sekancan angkat kereta. Hong Kong, sane prasida kedadosang trip ring rahina saking daratan, ngidangangangang pengiritan ring warung ajengan McDonald’s. McDonald’s manutangang harga dados ring Tiongkok ngantos 1 yuan (kira 15 sen USD) ring ajengan, punika sane pinaka pisan warsa puniki ring Xinhua. Hong Kong durung manutang harga anyar ring menu McDonald's. Maketut ring Kementerian Komersial, harga grosir rata-rata ring 18 jenis sayur ring 36 kota ring Tiongkok naik 62,4% ring dadosang warsa. Kementerian Komersial ngelaksanayang stabilisasi harga, ngewacenang 62.400 ton daging celeng miwah 210.000 ton gula saking cadangan ring akhir September. article_content: Chef Daniel Humm, renowned for leading Eleven Madison Park to earn three Michelin stars and the accolade of ‘Best Restaurant in the World,’ chose a new direction for his restaurant after the pandemic. Driven by environmental concerns and his experiences with food insecurity, Humm reinvented Eleven Madison Park with a fully plant-based menu. Humm’s culinary path began after his career as a professional cyclist ended with an injury. Growing up in Europe, he developed an appreciation for wine and food culture, which later fueled his dedication to excellence in the kitchen. When the pandemic struck, Humm’s involvement with Rethink Food—a non-profit organization combating food insecurity—inspired him to convert Eleven Madison Park into a kitchen producing thousands of meals daily for New Yorkers in need. Reflecting on the restaurant’s 25th anniversary, Humm recalled how relentless pursuit of awards built his team’s strength, but also led him to seek a deeper purpose. Changes in food sourcing and quality triggered by environmental shifts motivated him to address bigger issues through cooking. Switching to a plant-based menu presented a creative challenge and responded to urgent concerns like climate change. The team explored uncharted territory, even collaborating with Zen Buddhist monks and establishing their own upstate New York farm. With his new book, ‘Eat More Plants,’ Humm advocates for gradual progress, emphasizing that even small moves toward plant-centric eating can have a positive impact. Hosting famous guests such as Roger Federer has added to Eleven Madison Park’s prestige, though Humm jokes that not everyone should expect to walk into his kitchen unannounced. Humm’s journey reflects innovation, social responsibility, and a continuing drive for creative evolution in the culinary arts.

article_content: Researchers have found that the more time people spend commuting to and from work, the less likely they are to be satisfied with their lives. Being crammed in crowded trains or stuck in traffic jams is unpleasant for most people. Unsurprisingly, longer commute times are linked to greater feelings of time pressure, reducing the time available for hobbies and exercise. Margo Hilbrecht, a professor in Applied Health Sciences at the University of Waterloo in Canada and associate director of research for the Canadian Index of Wellbeing, stated: 'We found that the longer it takes someone to get to work, the lower their overall life satisfaction.' She pointed out that factors beyond just bad traffic or delays can have an impact. The study, published in the World Leisure Journal, used data from Statistics Canada to explore how commuting time affects well-being. Besides observing a link with lower life satisfaction, the researchers found that long commutes are associated with an increased sense of time pressure. 'Some people may enjoy a commute, but generally, longer travel time is linked to time pressure, which can raise stress levels,' Professor Hilbrecht said. Previous research has shown that lengthy commutes are linked to poorer mental and physical health, including higher risks of hypertension, obesity, fatigue, and increased work absences due to illness. The study also found a strong relationship between physical activity and greater life satisfaction among commuters. Another finding from separate research revealed that office environments with more plants improved worker happiness and productivity by 15%. In studies conducted in the UK and the Netherlands, lead researcher Marlon Nieuwenhuis from the School of Psychology said, 'Investing in office plants increases workers' quality of life and productivity.' Commuters who managed to make time for physical activity reported higher satisfaction with life. Professor Hilbrecht noted that physical activity can help reduce stress related to commuting when workers can include it in their daily routines, but long commutes often limit this possibility. She also highlighted that flexible work hours and higher household income are linked to higher life satisfaction. According to the study, women and people with partners reported higher levels of time pressure. Professor Hilbrecht hopes the findings will help guide workplace policies aimed at improving employee well-being. She suggested that employers support flexible work hours or provide opportunities for physical activity, as these can contribute to increased employee satisfaction. 'A long commute is detrimental to health. Sometimes it's better to choose a job closer to home, even if it means earning less, because of the positive effects on well-being,' she concluded.
translated_content: Para panaliti nyarengin indik makin lami waktu ngajengan perjalanan ka kantor tur mulih, makin suud rasa puen ring uripnyane. Ngantos keno sesak ring kereta api sane padet pisan utawi ngantosin kemacetan ring jalan ten prasida nyidaang rasa seneng. Lamanya perjalanan nyantosin rasa tekanan waktu, ngalanturin ngidangang waktu ngalaksanayang hobi utawi olahraga. Margo Hilbrecht, profesor ring Applied Health Sciences ring Universitas Waterloo ring Kanada, tur dados associate director riset ring Canadian Index of Wellbeing, nglanturang: 'Wenten indik makin lami perjalanan ka kantor, makin tipis rasa puen ring urip umumnyane.' Dadosang, ten kabukti indik macet ring jalan ajak telate dogen. Riset sane kasurat ring World Leisure Journal nganggén data saking Statistics Canada ngajenganang indik hubungan antara waktu perjalanan lan kesejahteraan. Salin nincapang indik rasa puen sane makin turun, panaliti ngametuangang perjalanan lami nambahang rasa tekanan waktu. 'Wenten sane demen perjalanan, nanging, secara umum, makin lami perjalanan, makin kuat rasa tekanan waktu sane prasida nambihin stres,' rauh Margo Hilbrecht. Riset ring warsa sane lintang ngidang ngemetuangang perjalanan lami dadosang kesehatan mental lan fisik makin suud, kalebet resiko hipertensi, obesitas, lemes, miwah alit presensi ring kantor krana sakit. Panaliti nentenangang setata hubungan antara aktivitas fisik miwah rasa puen ring urip para komuter. Panalitian lianan ngidangang kantor sane akehang tetanduran majantenang krama kantor makin bahagia miwah produktif nganti 15%. Ring studi ring UK miwah Belanda, Marlon Nieuwenhuis saking School of Psychology ngungsap, 'anggen tetanduran ring kantor prasida nambah kualitas urip miwah produktivitas krama kantor.' Para komuter sane prasida nyidang melaksanayang aktivitas fisik madué rasa puen ring urip sane luwih becik. Margo Hilbrecht nyebatang aktivitas fisik prasida nyingakin stres perjalanan yen prasida kalaksanayang ring rutinitas seharinane, nanging perjalanan lami biasane nenten ngametuangang indik punika. Dadosang, waktu kerja fleksibel miwah penghasilan umah sane langkung taler ngiringin rasa puen ring urip krama. Riset ngemetuangang, krama makurenan miwah sane dados pasangan ngalaksanayang tekanan waktu sane langkung. Margo Hilbrecht ngarepang indik hasil riset puniki prasida ngametuangang kebijakan kantor sane ngemargiang perhatosan ring kesejahteraan karyawan. Ida ngantosang boss kantor nyidaang waktu kerja fleksibel utawi peluang aktivitas fisik, krana punika prasida nambah rasa puen karyawan. 'Perjalanan lami suud ring kesehatan. Kadangkala becik milih kerjaan sane tosan ring griya, ajengan alit nyidaangang indik kesejahteraan,' rauhnyane.

article_content: The Delhi government is considering artificial rain through cloud seeding to help combat the city's severe air pollution, Environment Minister Gopal Rai confirmed on Wednesday. Rai stated that a meeting was held with scientists from IIT Kanpur, who advised that cloud seeding is only possible if adequate clouds or atmospheric moisture are present. Experts anticipate suitable conditions may develop around November 20-21. The Delhi government has asked the scientists to prepare a proposal on cloud seeding, which will be submitted to the Supreme Court. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, Director General of the India Meteorological Department, told PTI that artificial rain research is ongoing globally and in parts of India, including Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. Artificial rain requires specific conditions—such as sufficient clouds or moisture—under which certain particles are dispersed into clouds to facilitate rain. However, he noted that although India continues to research artificial rain, significant progress is still underway. In related news, the Tata Group recently acquired Wistron's manufacturing facility in a $750 million deal, becoming the first Indian company to assemble iPhones. India has also surpassed Mainland China to become the country with the most representations in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2024, reflecting the country's growing higher education prominence. Meanwhile, independent directors at Religare Enterprises Ltd have raised concerns over a takeover attempt by the Burman family, alleging fraud and regulatory breaches.

article_content: NFL Pro Era II, the follow-up to last year’s virtual reality football title from Status Pro, offers several substantial enhancements. Released for Meta Quest 2, Meta Quest 3, and other platforms, this edition introduces improved graphics, smarter computer-controlled players, current team rosters, and a redesigned locker room. A key new feature is online multiplayer, letting players compete head-to-head in real NFL-style games. The foundational gameplay remains familiar but is now more refined, with passing mechanics feeling smoother and overall reliability improved. An added system, Coach’s Confidence, incentivizes strong performance by unlocking new quarterback plays and abilities. The locker room serves as a hub with an extensive video board for stats, avatar customization, and viewing real-world team schedules. It also includes arcade-style mini-games for skill practice and various menu interactions via virtual wristband or by walking around the space. Multiplayer mode stands out as the most significant change. Gamers can now challenge friends or strangers in live matches, elevating the social element and nostalgia of classic in-person football video gaming. Some minor gameplay quirks persist, such as inconsistent AI receiver catches, but overall, the update feels more polished. The experience is notably better on the lightweight, advanced Meta Quest 3, although it remains playable on Quest 2. For fans seeking head-to-head action and deeper engagement, NFL Pro Era II’s expanded multiplayer makes it a meaningful upgrade. NFL Pro Era II is available on Quest Store, PlayStation Store, and Steam Store.

article_content: SpaceX has postponed the planned launch of Starship from Friday to Saturday following the discovery that the grid fin actuator on the Super Heavy booster—essential for steering the craft back to Earth—needs replacement. Elon Musk, SpaceX’s CEO, shared the news on social media. The updated launch, approved by the FAA, will be the second uncrewed test flight for the Starship. In April’s initial test, the spacecraft failed to reach orbit, and controllers were forced to destroy it mid-flight after an anomaly emerged soon after takeoff. Ahead of this next attempt, SpaceX engineers are focused on ensuring the vehicle can reach orbit for the first time. Starship is designed as a next-generation spacecraft meant to carry future crews to the Moon, Mars, and beyond, but first it must prove it can enter orbit successfully. The combined power of 33 Raptor engines provides Starship and its Super Heavy booster a launch thrust of 17 million pounds, making it even more powerful than the Saturn V and NASA’s SLS moon rocket. A pivotal part of the mission is whether the Starship can properly separate from its Super Heavy booster—a step that was unsuccessful during the April flight. If the separation procedure works, Starship will continue its journey to orbit and land in waters near Hawaii, while the Super Heavy booster is set to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico. Future projects aim for both pieces to be reusable and land back on Earth. The upcoming launch is scheduled for Saturday, November 18, at the Starbase facility in Boca Chica, Texas, with liftoff possible anytime during a two-hour window starting at 8 a.m. ET (5 a.m. PT). The event will be live-streamed on SpaceX’s website and its X (formerly Twitter) account. Fans are advised to monitor SpaceX’s social media channels for any eleventh-hour changes.

article_content: The U.S. Postal Service has unveiled a Forever stamp honoring Ruth Bader Ginsburg, with a portrait based on a 2017 photo taken in her Supreme Court office. Photographer Philip Bermingham, Ginsburg’s neighbor, created the striking image by kneeling on the floor so she could look directly into his lens, which resulted in a portrait that truly captured her presence. Bermingham and Ginsburg shared a warm camaraderie, often discussing their love for opera and teasing each other about their significant height difference. Ginsburg once emphasized in a note that although she looked up to Bermingham, she was never afraid of him. USPS art director Ethel Kessler, recognizing the strength of the photograph, selected it as the source for the commemorative stamp. Kessler, who considers Ginsburg a pioneer for justice, called this project a highlight of her career. Michael Deas, an artist from New Orleans, was commissioned to create the oil painting for the stamp, which portrays Ginsburg in her judicial robes and her signature white beaded collar from Cape Town, South Africa. This was one of her favorite pieces. Ginsburg, who passed away in September 2020, is the first Supreme Court justice to be honored with an individual U.S. stamp since Thurgood Marshall in 2003.

article_content: Laura Hathaway, from Atlanta, Georgia, had no regrets when she got a tattoo on her lower back at age 21. Now, a decade later, she wants it removed. Hathaway, now a pharmaceutical sales representative and mother of a two-year-old son, says the tattoo no longer fits her lifestyle. She recalls her son recently noticing the tattoo and asking about it, reinforcing her decision to have it removed. Dr. Scott Karempelis of Atlanta Dermatology Associates is treating Hathaway with a laser procedure that gradually erases tattoos, usually with minimal scarring. The process is described as painful, expensive, and time-consuming. Despite these drawbacks, Dr. Karempelis reports high demand, with him and his colleagues seeing more than 30 tattoo removal patients daily. According to the American Academy of Dermatology, tattoo regret is widespread in the United States. Among surveyed adults aged 18 to 50 in 2004, 24 percent reported having tattoos, and 17 percent of those had considered removal. The laser targets the pigment in the tattoo using specific wavelengths, breaking up the ink so that it can be reabsorbed by the body via the lymphatic system. Multiple sessions are required to prevent skin damage. Hathaway expects to undergo 10 sessions, each less than a minute long and spaced several weeks apart. She notes the process is a lot more painful than getting the tattoo, describing it as feeling like repeated bee stings. The discomfort typically fades after a few hours. Patients with larger tattoos may use a topical anesthetic, increasing the cost. Dr. Karempelis charges by the square inch. Hathaway expects her total bill to exceed $2,200. Scarring remains a risk, and some temporary discoloration is common, but in most cases, the area appears normal after about a year. Certain ink colors, such as green, yellow, and purple, are more difficult to remove, particularly for people with darker skin. Tattoo location also affects removal success; areas farthest from the heart, like the ankles, are the toughest to treat. New tattoo ink technology, such as Freedom-2’s microencapsulated dye, might allow tattoos to be removed with a single laser treatment in the future. Until then, Dr. Karempelis expects more patients to seek removal of tattoos tied to their past, especially names of former partners. For Hathaway, her floral tattoo no longer aligns with the image she wants. She says she got the tattoo before low-rise pants became popular and wanted it to remain private. Judy Fortin contributed reporting for CNN Medical News.

article_content: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has declared its readiness to sanction and prosecute any fleet operators who fail to comply with established national safety standards. This announcement was made by FRSC Corps Marshal Dauda Biu, represented by Assistant Corps Marshal Ms Amuche Nwaka, during the 2023 annual safety managers retreat in Abuja. Biu emphasized that the Corps will no longer accept fleet operators' failure to adhere strictly to the Road Transport Safety Standardisation Scheme (RTSSS). The purpose of the retreat was to assess the management of fleet operations over the past year and address significant issues. According to recent investigations, many crashes involving fleet operations could have been avoided if safety managers fulfilled their duties responsibly. 'This retreat serves as a wake-up call for all of us as safety managers,' Biu stated. He pointed out ongoing deficiencies in RTSSS implementation, especially regarding Speed Limiting Devices (SLDs). Recent public transport reviews indicate that national compliance levels remain low. Specific infractions noted include failure to install or tampering with SLDs, calibrating devices above approved speed limits, and collaborating with unauthorized vendors to issue fake compliance certificates. 'Such actions will no longer be tolerated. The Corps will promptly sanction non-compliant operators,' Biu added. Reflecting on the 2022 fleet operator certification, Biu announced that stringent measures, supported by law, would be enforced. Non-compliant operators will receive pre-action notices for prosecution. Operators denying certification teams access or failing standards more than once will face suspension. Certified vehicle stickers will only be granted to vehicles with functioning Speed Limiting Devices. Earlier, FCCPC Executive Vice Chairman Mr. Babatunde Irukera (represented by Mrs. Olubunmi Oti) highlighted the serious effects of road traffic crashes (RTCs) on lives and the economy. He advocated for collaboration among stakeholders to promote robust safety measures. The RTSSS was praised as a step forward, and the FRSC was commended for striving toward international standards. Irukera also emphasized the importance of continuous learning and strategic updates among regulators and transport stakeholders to address pressing safety concerns. The FRSC’s strategic aim of achieving a 5% reduction in RTCs and injuries aligns with broader goals for consumer safety and protection. The event featured goodwill messages from leaders in the transport sector, including Dangote Cement Transport, BUA Cement Transport, and the Public Transport Owners of Nigeria Association.

article_content: Jasmine Johnson believed she was planning ahead when she called her local nursery at 20 weeks pregnant to reserve a place for her baby, only to find out it was fully booked until September 2025. By then, her child will be almost two years old, so Jasmine will miss out on the first year of funded childcare she is eligible for. Experts warn that securing nursery and childminder spaces is getting more difficult due to government plans to expand funded childcare hours for working parents in England over the next two years. BBC News analysis suggests demand could rise by roughly 15%—meaning over 100,000 more children will need full-time care. Jasmine, a primary-school teacher in a small village with only one nursery, hoped to return to work in September 2024. Now, she feels 'no choice' but to rely on her parents for help and apply for reduced hours at work. If her flexible working request is turned down, she may have to leave her job. 'When the increase in funded hours was announced, I thought it was perfect timing and would help me return to work,' Jasmine says. 'But now, even thinking about it makes me anxious.' At present, parents of three- and four-year-olds in England are entitled to 30 hours of funded childcare each week during school term time (38 weeks a year). By September 2025, this support—sometimes called 'free' hours—will be available for all children aged nine months to two years. The Department for Education (DfE) says childminders and nurseries will have time to prepare, as the rollout will happen in stages. Joeli Brearley, founder of Pregnant Then Screwed, says thousands of parents are anxiously awaiting the expansion so they can boost their work hours. She now worries this will lead to 'incredibly long waiting lists and more uncertainty.' A 15% increase in childcare demand in England equates to more than four million extra hours a week—over 100,000 additional children in care for 40 hours a week. This is before considering parents currently not working who may start jobs—one of the government's aims in funding more childcare. Gillian Paull of Frontier Economics says meeting the increased demand will be 'challenging' because of financial pressures and difficulty in recruiting staff, but it's not impossible. 'Even with some unmet demand, many working parents will save money with lower childcare costs,' she says. 'If more mothers of young children choose to work, it will also help gender equality.' Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland also offer government-funded hours, though each has different schemes. At Eagley School House Nurseries in Bolton, many parents eligible for extra funded hours are already requesting more days. With a waiting list until March 2025, the nursery is turning down requests for extra hours—even from staff members. Sophie Eckersley, a part-time nursery worker finishing her university exams, hoped to increase her two-year-old daughter's funded hours in April. Government-funded childcare would help 'especially with money,' Sophie says, but nursery owner Julie Robinson is struggling to meet the demand. 'We just don’t have the places,' Julie says. Neil Leitch from the Early Years Alliance notes that BBC News’s analysis suggests the expansion may be 'undeliverable in practice.' Without proper support and more funding, some providers might limit funded spaces or opt out. The sector’s major challenge remains staffing. There were 9,800 fewer childcare workers in 2022 compared to 2019, and the number of childminders has dropped by over 20%. Nursery provider Busy Bees, caring for 40,000 children, is training 1,300 apprentices but needs even more. 'We must recruit another 1,500 staff in the next two years,' says Chris McCandless, European Chief Executive. He welcomes government investment but says it 'needs to cover the true cost of childcare.' Parents are urged to register soon as spots 'will be hard to come by.' Earlier this year, charity Coram found fewer childcare spots in England, with only half of local areas having enough spaces for under-twos. Councils monitor childcare provision and distribute government funding to nurseries and childminders. Louise Gittins, chair of the Local Government Association's Children and Young People Board, says provision is already insufficient—especially in deprived and rural areas—and that there’s not much time left to prepare before the expansion. 'We can't control new providers entering areas where there is enough provision,' she says. 'Other areas lacking places will result in inequality and disappointment for parents.' There is added concern for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), who already struggle to find places. 'Each time these changes happen, SEND provision drops,' says Catherine McLeod, chief executive of Dingley’s Promise. A DfE official said the department is delivering 'the biggest-ever investment in childcare in England’s history... backed by £8bn a year once fully rolled out.' The government says it's 'already investing hundreds of millions to increase hourly funding rates' and will provide £100m in capital funding to create more early-years and wraparound spaces, plus begin a recruitment campaign soon. BBC News used Family Resources Survey data to estimate eligibility—based on each child’s age and whether parents work at least 16 hours a week at minimum wage—and government data to estimate increased use once the expansion occurs. Calculations were based on hours used, not just places, as families use varying amounts of care. Are you pregnant and on a nursery waiting list? Struggling to get more hours for your toddler? Facing long journeys for childcare? Email haveyoursay@bbc.co.uk to share your story. Include a contact number if you’re happy to talk to a BBC journalist. Alternatively, contact via the BBC website or email, and include your name, age, and location.

article_content: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has forecasted a 'near-normal' Atlantic hurricane season for 2009, with four to seven hurricanes likely to form. This outlook was announced less than two weeks before the season’s official start on June 1. Commerce Secretary Gary Locke emphasized the importance of preparation, stating, 'While we cannot prevent hurricanes, we can prepare, and we must.' NOAA predicts there will be nine to fourteen named storms this season, with four to seven expected to become hurricanes. Of these, one to three are expected to reach major hurricane status (Category 3 or higher on the Saffir-Simpson scale), with sustained winds of 111 miles per hour or more. The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 through the end of November. In 2008, there were 16 named storms, eight of which became hurricanes, including five major hurricanes. The 2008 season was among the busiest and most costly, causing approximately $54 billion in damages, according to the National Climatic Data Center. NOAA’s hurricane outlook for 2009 is similar to those from other organizations: AccuWeather (13 named storms, eight hurricanes), Colorado State University (14 named storms, seven hurricanes), WSI Corp. (13 named storms, seven hurricanes), and the Weather Research Center (seven named storms, four hurricanes). NOAA attributes its outlook to competing climate factors, including increased rainfall over West Africa, warmer Atlantic waters, and reduced wind shear, all of which can encourage storm development. However, if El Nino develops in the eastern Pacific or ocean temperatures in the eastern tropical Atlantic remain cool, hurricane activity could decrease. NOAA will issue an updated hurricane outlook in August, before the historically peak period for storm activity. Craig Fugate, the recently appointed Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) director, and NOAA Administrator Jane Lubchenco both stressed the need for residents of coastal areas to be ready for hurricane season. Lubchenco stated, 'NOAA's message is clear -- be prepared, have a plan.' The first named storm of the 2009 Atlantic hurricane season will be Ana.

Wacikan puniki kaumumayang kirang saking kalih minggu sadurungang musim puniki ngamargiang kapertama ring tanggal 1 Juni. Sekretaris Komersial Gary Locke ngejangangang prasida maktaang persiapan, “Sanajan tong bisa ngalanturang angin topan, prasida maktaang persiapan, punika wajib.” NOAA nglaksanayang prakiraan indik sangang ngantos kalih welas angin sane bakat kadadosang storm warsa puniki, ring antuk patang ngantos pitu wentenang dadosang angin topan. Antuk punika, sane dadosang angin topan ageng taler dadosang pisan ngantos tiosan telu (Kategori 3 utawi langkung ring Saffir-Simpson scale), wentenang nyantos 111 mil per jam utawi luwih. Musim angin topan Atlantic ngametuang ring 1 Juni ngantos pungkasan sasi November. Warsa 2008 kapertiyang wenten 16 storm, 8 dadosang angin topan, kalebet 5 angin topan ageng. Warsa puniki pinaka musim paling sibuk miwah ngalanturang kerugian taler nyantos $54 miliar, wantah saking National Climatic Data Center. Prakiraan NOAA ring 2009 sami sareng prakiraan saking organisasi lenan: AccuWeather (13 storm, 8 angin topan), Colorado State University (14 storm, 7 angin topan), WSI Corp. Yening El Nino kadadosang ring Pasifik Wetan utawi toya ring Atlantic Tropical Wetan nenten anget, kadadosang angin topan prasida alit. NOAA bakal ngerilis apdet prakiraan ring sasih Agustus, sane dadosang pinaka wewidangan musim puncak. Craig Fugate, Kepala Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) sane anyar, sareng Administrator NOAA Jane Lubchenco, ngajakang krama sane tinggal ring pesisir prasida maktaang persiapan ring musim angin topan puniki. Lubchenco ngaturang, “Pesan NOAA jelas -- maktaang persiapan, ajegang rencana.” Angin pisan sane magiang nama ring musim angin topan Atlantic warsa 2009 maktaang ‘Ana’.

article_content: Daniel Danino, CEO and founder of Volta Metals, leads an international group specializing in energy, industry, trading, and aviation within the EMEA region. The African aviation sector has historically faced significant challenges, including infrastructure deficits and complex regulatory environments. However, the sector is now showing remarkable promise, particularly in West Africa, where a wave of transformation is underway. Countries such as Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, and Ivory Coast are emerging as leaders by revitalizing both national and regional airlines. Through policy reforms, strategic investments, and renewed regional collaboration, these nations are redefining the future of African aviation. For example, Air Senegal has expanded its international routes to cities like Paris and Barcelona, targeting both leisure and business travelers, and positioning itself as a key ambassador for Senegalese and West African tourism and trade. Nigeria Air is preparing for its highly anticipated launch in 2023, with plans to operate domestic and international routes, aiming to enhance connectivity and economic growth within the country and across the region. Air Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana's Africa World Airlines are also modernizing fleets, improving services, and expanding route networks to include secondary cities, making air travel more accessible to a broader population. The resurgence in West Africa's aviation sector is propelled by targeted investments, policy updates, regional initiatives, and technological advancements—all contributing to its growing global recognition. Regional airlines such as Passion Air in Ghana and Air Burkina play a key role by offering flights to less-served destinations, increasing accessibility and supporting regional trade and tourism. The sector is attracting considerable investments, further supported by investor-friendly policies. For instance, Qatar Airways’ investment in Air Rwanda underscores international confidence in the region’s aviation future. Key policy reforms, notably the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM), are driving industry liberalization, reducing operational costs, increasing competition, and promoting connectivity. Investments in technology and airport infrastructure are also enhancing the passenger experience and improving operational standards. Business leaders are advised to focus on tapping niche markets, building strategic partnerships, employing advanced technologies, engaging with communities, and promoting sustainable practices. Such strategies align with contemporary global trends and can help small businesses capitalize on the expanding aviation market in West Africa. Drawing on over twenty years of aviation experience in the region, I observe that these changes represent a revolutionary shift, positioning the sector for future resilience and competitiveness. Continuous commitment to reform, technology, and infrastructure is establishing a solid foundation for inclusive growth. Small businesses and stakeholders have an opportunity to significantly contribute to, and benefit from, the sector’s ongoing transformation. For those considering involvement in West Africa’s aviation industry, the current moment offers unique prospects for influencing the region’s economic trajectory.

article_content: While Jesse Owens' four gold medal victories at the 1936 Berlin Olympics are widely celebrated for challenging Nazi ideology, another significant American triumph from those Games is getting new attention. 'The Boys in the Boat,' a film from MGM Amazon Studios directed by George Clooney, tells the inspiring story of the University of Washington's underdog rowing team that claimed gold on Hitler's home turf. The making of the film wasn't easy—according to producer Grant Heslov, the cast had to undergo intensive training under Olympic-level rowing coaches before filming began. Initially, both Heslov and Clooney were skeptical that the actors could convincingly master the sport. 'After about a month and a half of solid practice, we saw them row and worried we’d made a huge mistake,' Heslov recalled. However, by the time the cameras rolled, the actors had risen to the challenge. Screenwriter Mark L. Smith adapted the story from Daniel James Brown’s nonfiction book, following Joe Rantz—a University of Washington student struggling financially and living out of his car—as he joins coach Al Ulbrickson’s determined team. Through relentless effort and teamwork, Rantz and his peers became an elite crew, overcoming personal and athletic obstacles. Positioned alongside beloved sports dramas like 'Miracle' and 'Chariots of Fire,' the movie transcends athletic competition by exploring the resilience and unity of young people facing adversity during the Great Depression. Heslov emphasized that rowing was more than just sport for these students—it was a path to food, shelter, and education, as well as personal growth. Tanya Swerling, the film's editor, paid close attention to authenticity in depicting rowing. She watched documentaries and consulted with real-life rowers to ensure accuracy, wanting to honor the legacy of the crew and provide fans a believable cinematic experience. With its heartfelt narrative and commitment to realism, 'The Boys in the Boat' captures both a pivotal sports victory and the enduring spirit of perseverance.

'Sampun latihan bulan setengah, rauh nyidangangang performa, prasida wenten rasayang salah pilih. Nanging tiosan shooting, para aktor prasida prasida ngamolihang kemajuan sane matibayang,' sewala Heslov. Screenwriter Mark L.
