article_content: Inmates at Brazil's Arisvaldo de Campos Pires maximum security prison are gaining new skills through crochet and knitting. The project, launched in 2009 by fashion designer Raquel Guimaraes, gives inmates one day off their sentence for every three days spent knitting or crocheting. Guimaraes, unable to find enough skilled knitters for her Doiselles label, turned to the prison for assistance. She trained 18 prisoners convicted of various offenses, including robbery and murder. Their hand-made garments are carefully quality-checked and sold in around 70 stores across Brazil, as well as exported to countries such as America, France, and Japan. Known as the Flor de Lotus ('Lotus Flower') Project, the initiative allows inmates to earn a starting salary of 75% of Brazil's minimum wage. A quarter of their earnings is kept aside and paid upon release, helping support their transition back into society. Former inmate Celio Tavares said the program helps participants gain confidence and skills useful for finding work after their sentences. Since its inception, Raquel Guimaraes has trained approximately 100 inmates. The project not only provides focus and structure within the prison, but also offers hope and practical benefits for life after release. According to Guimaraes, ‘The program gives them self-esteem and opens doors to employment.’

Guimaraes, yang kesulitan mencari tukang nyulam untuk label Doiselles-nya, mendatangi lapas tersebut untuk meminta bantuan. Sejak dimulai, Raquel Guimaraes telah melatih sekitar 100 napi. Proyek ini tak hanya memberikan ruang aktivitas dan struktur selama di lapas, tapi juga harapan dan manfaat praktis setelah keluar. article_content: Two international bridges connecting Nuevo Laredo, Mexico, and Laredo, Texas, were closed on Wednesday due to rising water levels in the Rio Grande, according to Laredo officials. International Bridge I, one of four bridges linking the cities, was closed because it sits at the lowest elevation, said Laredo spokeswoman Xochitl Mora Garcia. Concerned that high water could damage the bridge, workers are removing steel canopy shades to reduce stress on the structure. The bridge is expected to remain closed for at least three days. The Rio Grande, which normally measures 6 to 10 feet deep at Laredo, is forecast to crest at nearly 39 feet on Thursday. Additionally, the Colombia Bridge was closed as water there rose even higher, according to Mora Garcia. It will remain closed until further notice. Removing the canopies from International Bridge I will take about a day, with another day needed to reinstall them once water levels recede. Each day, an estimated 10,000 to 12,000 pedestrians and 12,000 to 14,000 non-commercial vehicles cross International Bridge I. The Laredo population of about 250,000 typically increases to 350,000 to 400,000 as visitors from Mexico come for shopping, family visits, and recreation. Laredo is the country's leading inland port. International Bridge II and the World Trade Bridge remain open. The city owns and operates all four bridges. Authorities are encouraging pedestrians needing to return to Nuevo Laredo to do so immediately, or to travel by vehicle over Bridge II, as this bridge will not accept pedestrians returning to Mexico. The Colombia and World Trade bridges can accommodate pedestrians. Buses from Nuevo Laredo are transporting pedestrians on Bridge II, typically reserved for vehicles, in an arrangement between U.S. and Mexican officials during the emergency. Laredo is preparing to open an emergency operations center, and residents living in the 100-year floodplain will be alerted for possible evacuation. The Laredo Civic Center can be converted into a shelter if needed. On Wednesday, Texas Governor Rick Perry announced he was dispatching vehicles, guardsmen, and rescue divers to the Laredo area. He emphasized continued monitoring as heavy rains from Hurricane Alex threaten more flooding along the Rio Grande. Laredo’s water services are unaffected, but Nuevo Laredo may experience service at half of its normal capacity. Communities across northeastern Mexico have been hit by severe flooding caused by rainfall from Hurricane Alex nearly two weeks ago. In Reynosa, Tamaulipas, 23,000 people were at risk from flooding by the Rio Bravo (as the Rio Grande is called in Mexico), reported the Notimex news agency. Hurricane Alex made landfall as a Category 2 storm on June 30, resulting in at least six deaths in Nuevo Leon state.
translated_content: Kalih jembatan internasional sane nyambungang antara Nuevo Laredo, Meksiko, sareng Laredo, Texas, sampun kantun tutup ring Rahina Budha puniki sebab toya dongkang ring Kali Rio Grande, makudang saking pejabat Laredo. International Bridge I, silih tunggil saking pat jembatan sane ngamolihang sambungan ring indik punika, sampun tutup awit anggen jembatan puniki ring elevasi paling tegeh, nyantos ngidangangang indik Juru Bicara Laredo, Xochitl Mora Garcia. Kerana rasa waspada toya dongkang prasida ngetuging kerusakan jembatan, para pekerja ngalaksanayang ngantos shade baja saking payon supaya beban sareng tekanan ring struktur dados langkung alit. Laredo dados pelabuhan darat utama ring negari. International Bridge II sareng World Trade Bridge tetep kabuka. Kota puniki sane ngoperasikang pat jembatan punika. Pejabat nyarengin pejalan kaki kedas pisan sane prasida mulih ring Nuevo Laredo prasida melaksanaang reramae, utawi miwahang kendaraan ngantos Bridge II, nanging ring jembatan punika nenten prasida ngemolihang pejalan kaki mulih ring Meksiko. Colombia Bridge sareng World Trade Bridge prasida nampa pejalan kaki. Bus saking Nuevo Laredo ngemargiang antuk pejalan kaki ring Bridge II sane biasane prasida dados kendaraan, ring pengaturan antar pejabat Amérika Saréng Meksiko ring mangda nglaksanayang situasi darurat punika. Laredo ngamolihang pusat operasi darurat, sareng warga ring floodplain 100-taun prasida kabarangi yening wenten indikasi presida ngungsi. Civic Center Laredo prasida dados pangungsian yening dados kabutuhan. Ring Rahina Budha puniki, Gubernur Texas Rick Perry ngawedarang ngirim kendaraan, anggota gardha, miwah penyelam penyelamat ring wewidangan Laredo. Janji ngawastanin pengawasan antuk ujan ageng saking Hurricane Alex sane prasida akutang banjir ring segara Rio Grande. Pelayanan toya ring Laredo nenten kaupang, nanging pelayanan toya ring Nuevo Laredo prasida nyantos setengah kapasitas normal ring kota punika. Komunitas ring wetan laut Meksiko kathah ngalantarang banjir ageng indik ujan saking Hurricane Alex silih kalih minggu taler. Ring kota Reynosa, Tamaulipas, 23.000 krama ring bahaya banjir saking Rio Bravo (asapunika sebutan Rio Grande ring Meksiko), nganut kantor berita Notimex. article_content: Queen Elizabeth II is recuperating after a recent illness, preventing her from attending the Commonwealth Observance service in London, Buckingham Palace announced. The monarch, 86, spent a brief period in hospital on March 3 with symptoms of gastroenteritis and was released the next day. Palace sources say her condition is not serious, though she cannot attend the event at Westminster Abbey. However, the Queen will participate in the Commonwealth Reception at Marlborough House that evening, where she is expected to sign a new Commonwealth Charter promoting equal rights in all 54 member nations. Adopted last December, the Charter opposes discrimination based on gender, race, belief, or politics, and emphasizes the importance of democracy and human rights. Some observers interpret the Queen's signing of the Charter as support for women's rights and LGBTQ equality, but officials clarify that she acts as an impartial Head of the Commonwealth. The Charter’s principles may be difficult to apply in certain countries, like Nigeria and Uganda, that still outlaw same-sex relationships. Although the Queen will not be at the Abbey service, Prince Philip will attend on her behalf. A recorded message from the Queen will be played, where she highlights the theme 'Opportunity through enterprise' and stresses the Commonwealth's shared values of inclusion, peace, and justice. Buckingham Palace added that, after marking her 60th year as monarch in 2012, the Queen hopes to attend other official events later in the week, health permitting.

article_content: Images of missing Israelis are displayed around Tel Aviv, reflecting national anguish after more than 240 individuals were abducted on October 7. Victims included people of all ages, from infants to the elderly, taken by armed militants from homes, workplaces, and public gatherings near Gaza. After being captured by Hamas and taken to Gaza, most hostages’ situations remain unclear, leaving families in distress. Eyal Nouri, showing a photo of his 72-year-old aunt Amina Moshe, remembers how she was seized from her kibbutz residence. Nouri emphasizes, ‘Children, babies, and elderly women should never be involved in conflict—it’s inhumane.’ Israel’s history includes several hostage crises and high-profile prisoner exchanges, freeing some who later became militant leaders—such as Sheikh Ahmad Yassin and Yahya Sinwar—in return for Israeli citizens. Among these was Gilad Shalit, an Israeli soldier kidnapped in 2006. His release, after extensive negotiations, required a large prisoner swap that included Sinwar, now a Hamas leader accused of masterminding the recent attacks. Gershon Baskin, a peace activist who aided Shalit’s release, notes the current hostage crisis is complicated by the devastation of the recent violence and the urgent timeline, making negotiations particularly difficult. Despite mediation by Qatar and Egypt resulting in a few hostages being freed, broader agreements have not been reached. Recently, Hamas offered to exchange up to 70 women and children hostages for a five-day ceasefire, but Israel is only willing to accept limited humanitarian pauses. Israeli public opinion, according to surveys, generally supports continued military action alongside hostage negotiations, with many fearing that a ceasefire could increase risks or prevent achieving key goals. Hostage families and their supporters continue to press for government intervention with powerful public demonstrations—installing empty beds in public squares and marching from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem. With reports of hostages killed in airstrikes and mounting uncertainty, there’s growing urgency to resolve the crisis, as the nation draws lessons from past exchanges and grapples with the challenges of the current conflict.

article_content: Members of the feminist punk band Pussy Riot compared Australia’s asylum seeker policies to Russian prison conditions during their panel at the Sydney Festival of Dangerous Ideas, held at the Sydney Opera House. Maria (Masha) Alyokhina and Nadezhda (Nadya) Tolokonnikova began by addressing proposals from Australian activists suggesting they boycott the event, due to connections between one of the festival’s co-organisers, the St James Ethics Centre, and the Australian government’s asylum seeker strategy. Instead of boycotting, Alyokhina and Tolokonnikova chose to speak at the festival, hoping to draw attention to issues surrounding Australia’s detention camps, which they noted were similar in some respects to situations in Russia. The two also called for Australia to rescind its invitation to Russian President Vladimir Putin for the upcoming G20 summit. Alyokhina stated, 'We think that this person has no place at the G20.' Both Alyokhina and Tolokonnikova were sentenced to two years in prison after staging a protest performance at Moscow’s Cathedral of Christ the Savior in 2012 and were released in December 2013. They said current conditions in Russia remain so repressive that such a performance could not be repeated. Since their release, the two have continued to campaign for prisoners’ rights. During a court hearing in Moscow in August 2012, band members Nadezhda Tolokonnikova, Maria Alyokhina, and Yekaterina Samutsevich were photographed seated in a glass-walled cage. In December 2013, Tolokonnikova was seen in front of the Cathedral of Christ the Savior in Moscow.

article_content: Norway is home to many supernatural legends and chilling ghost stories, found across the country. Akershus Fortress in Oslo is particularly known for paranormal tales. Guarding the capital's harbor for over 700 years, it has never been breached by foreign forces, but its history includes bloodshed and years as a prison for notorious criminals. The prison, infamous for harsh conditions, closed in 1950. Many have reported unexplained whispers, scratching, and sensations of being pushed in the castle's corridors. Dalen Hotel in Telemark is one of Norway's most renowned haunted hotels. Room 17 is infamous for the ghost called 'The English Lady,' thought to be Miss Greenfield, who arrived in the late 1800s. After a tragic event involving a secret pregnancy, a deceased infant, and Miss Greenfield's suicide, a table is still set for her in the hotel restaurant. Nidaros Cathedral in Trondheim is host to the story of 'The Monk,' a ghost reportedly seen since 1924, associated with mysterious chanting and organ music at night. Some historians question whether monks ever served at the cathedral, but the tales endure. Hotel Union Øye in Norangsfjorden is linked to a tragic love story between a servant named Linda and a German duke. When denied a future together, both took their own lives, and Linda's ghost is said to weep in The Blue Room. Bærums Verk near Oslo, and especially the historic Værtshuset restaurant, is well-known for haunting reports involving Anna Krefting, who managed the site for fifty years. Sightings of her in green have been reported on the restaurant's second floor. The restaurant was established in 1640. There is also a story of an unexplained ringing phone in the administration building. The former mining site Blaafarveværket in Eastern Norway, now a museum, is associated with the ghost 'Blåmannen,' who reportedly warned miners of disasters by appearing with a lantern. In 1854, the site's worst accident happened when six miners died. Munkholmen, a small island north of Trondheim, was once an abbey, fort, and prison. Visitors have reported mysterious presences believed to be prisoner Peder Schumacher Griffenfeld, who was held there for 18 years. Today, Munkholmen is a popular summer tourist attraction with regular boat trips and guided tours. The ruins of Nes church in Vormsund, Eastern Norway, are associated with stories of the ghost of priest Jacob Christian Finckenhagen. Accounts of his fate vary, but visitors report strange phenomena, sluggish movement, and malfunctioning electronics near the ruins. Fredriksten Fortress in Halden, a significant border fortress, is now a museum and event site. It is said to be haunted by 'Den Hvite Dame' (the White Lady), once the commander's mistress. After her lover's death in battle, she reportedly leaped from the fortress wall, and is said to appear near the white tower at midnight.

article_content: A mother, Brandy Turner, has been reunited with her three-year-old son, Luke, four days after he was abducted by the child’s father. According to police, Monty Turner attacked Brandy with pepper spray and a stun gun before taking Luke from their home in Longmont, Colorado, last Saturday. The incident triggered an Amber Alert that spanned several states. Monty Turner, 51, was arrested in Brandon, Manitoba, Canada, on Sunday. He is being held on suspicion of kidnapping, burglary, and assault. A hearing about his status in Canada was held on Tuesday. At a news conference on Tuesday, Brandy Turner said she felt terrified and in disbelief when her son was taken, followed by anxiety while trying to bring him home. Luke was found safe, and they were reunited. Monty Turner faces the possibility of being extradited to Colorado within five days to three weeks, although he could contest the extradition, according to a spokesperson for the Boulder County District Attorney. Court records indicate that Monty Turner was under a protection order that barred him from coming within 100 feet of Brandy or Luke after a previous abduction incident last year. On Saturday, he reportedly hid in Brandy’s garage and attacked her around 10 a.m. when she stepped outside. Brandy told police that she tried to lock herself inside and call 911, but Monty forced his way in. She said their son saw the attack and pleaded with his father not to hurt his mother. Brandy described fighting her estranged husband, but said he overpowered her with the stun gun and pepper spray before taking Luke from the kitchen table. After the abduction, authorities issued an Amber Alert and began searching for Monty Turner and Luke. The FBI and Canadian police traced Monty’s credit card usage to the Casablanca Motor Inn in Brandon, Manitoba, where he was arrested and Luke was recovered safely. Brandy Turner could not travel to Canada to retrieve her son because she did not have a passport. At the news conference, she expressed immense relief at having her son back.

article_content: The European Union’s top court has decided that asylum seekers who say they are gay should not be forced to undergo any kind of test or provide explicit proof of their sexuality. This important ruling comes after three men—one Ugandan and one from a Muslim country—were denied asylum in the Netherlands for not proving their sexual orientation. The European Court of Justice (ECJ) declared that every EU state is required to respect applicants' human dignity during the asylum process. The court stated that officials cannot demand or accept physical examinations or explicit recordings from applicants, even if offered, as these violate basic rights. This case comes at a time when more people from sub-Saharan Africa, where same-sex relationships are often illegal, are seeking asylum in Europe. In 2011, Czech authorities were criticized for using arousal ('phallometric') tests on LGBTQ+ asylum seekers, a method called degrading and outdated. With its latest ruling, the ECJ clarified that officials are allowed to ask questions about a person's sexual orientation generally, but are not allowed to probe into personal sexual practices. Asylum claims should not be rejected if an applicant does not talk about their sexuality right away or refuses to answer very personal questions. Mistreatment of gay and lesbian refugees has also attracted attention in the UK after findings showed a significant portion of interviews included inappropriate or demeaning questions. Previously, the ECJ also ruled that LGBTQ+ people risking jail in their home countries can be granted asylum in the EU.

Putusan puniki kadadosang dados indik kasus tiga krama — pinaka sane saking Uganda tur saking negara Islam — sane kasor ring Belanda krana nenten kabuktiang ngidang nyidayang orientasi seksualitas. Kasus punika dados ring warsa indik akeh warga saking Afrika Sub-Sahara, sane ring negara sane makejang nenten ngidang ngametuin hubungan sejenis, ngametuang indik suaka ring Eropa. article_content: An inquest has stated that it could take up to six months to determine the full circumstances of Mr. Mark Duggan's death. Test results suggest that Mr. Duggan, whose shooting by police in Tottenham led to riots, did not fire at officers before he was killed. The Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) reported that ballistic analysis indicates a handgun found at the scene had not been fired during the incident. Mr. Duggan, 29, who police believed was a member of a gang, died from a single gunshot wound to the chest last Thursday. His death triggered riots in Tottenham, which spread to other areas over the next two days. Investigations have found that his death followed two shots fired by an armed officer from Scotland Yard’s CO19 unit. Forensic officers confirmed that a bullet found in a police radio at the scene was police-issued. The IPCC also said forensic experts could not definitively say if the handgun near Mr. Duggan was fired. The IPCC has launched an investigation into the shooting at Tottenham Hale and continues to review CCTV footage. At the time, Mr. Duggan was a passenger in a silver Toyota Estima minicab, which police stopped in Ferry Lane, near Tottenham Hale Tube station. Earlier reports revealed Mr. Duggan was carrying a converted blank-firing handgun capable of firing live ammunition when he was shot. This kind of weapon is commonly used among London’s criminal gangs. Mr. Duggan, a father of four, was fatally shot by armed police as part of a pre-planned operation. At the opening of the inquest, it was confirmed Mr. Duggan died from a single shot to the chest. He reportedly sent a text to his partner, Semone Wilson, minutes before his death, stating: 'The Feds are following me.' The investigation is expected to last up to six months, and during this period, the family might not have access to full details about his death. Mr. Duggan was officially identified by his family on August 6. Coroner Andrew Walker stated there are reasonable grounds to hold an inquest. The case was adjourned for further investigation, with the IPCC estimating a report could take four to six months. After the hearing, Mr. Duggan’s family expressed their distress over the riots that followed his death. Helen Shaw, representing the charity Inquest, said the family wants the truth to be established and does not condone the unrest that occurred afterwards. A pre-inquest review is scheduled for December 12.

A temporary agreement between Israel and Hamas has brought a brief break in the fighting in Gaza. Peace advocates in the United States recognize this as a diplomatic success but caution that more is needed. The four-day truce, brokered with Qatar and Egypt’s assistance and supported by President Biden, will see Hamas release 50 Israeli women and children, while Israel will free 150 Palestinian women and children. During this period, humanitarian aid deliveries to Gaza will increase.

Hassan El-Tayyab, a Middle East policy director, stressed the importance of this step but emphasized that it does not resolve the conflict. He called for sustained action towards a full ceasefire, release of all hostages, unobstructed aid flow, and a path to peace for both sides. The truce, expected to start Friday following Israeli cabinet approval, is the first since hostilities began.

Despite the break, Israeli officials signal plans to resume military operations. Advocates warn that continued fighting is unlikely to bring lasting peace, urging for a longer cessation, deeper negotiations, and addressing root issues like the ongoing oppression of Palestinians.

President Biden, thanking Qatar, Egypt, and Israeli leaders, commended the agreement and humanitarian provisions but has stopped short of endorsing a permanent ceasefire. His administration advocates only for temporary pauses, holding that Israel must first confront Hamas militarily.

Nancy Okail, president of the Center for International Policy, sees the truce as important for delivering aid and protecting workers, while pushing for a lasting ceasefire. Over 14,500 people in Gaza have been killed since October 7, when Hamas’s attack resulted in about 1,200 Israeli deaths and over 200 captives. Thousands of Palestinians, including children, remain imprisoned in Israel.

Experts and human rights organizations warn of potential genocide and ethnic cleansing, citing mass displacement and ongoing civilian casualties. Okail argues the cease in violence should also extend to the West Bank, where violence has increased. She urges US leaders to draw firmer boundaries against war crimes and for international legal standards in the use of American arms. Despite calls for restricting military aid, such measures have not been adopted. Israel receives $3.8 billion in US aid each year, with Biden requesting even more.

Groups like Amnesty International have accused Israel of enforcing apartheid policies. Despite demands, the US has not imposed significant consequences. Reports suggest officials worry the current pause could lead to greater media coverage of Gaza and shift public opinion.

Advocates call for independent monitoring in Gaza to reveal the reality on the ground, even if it sparks greater opposition to the war. There are also deep fears that attacks will shift to southern Gaza, where many have sought safety from earlier bombings.

Although the pause offers temporary relief, US support for Israel is expected to continue. Historian Juan Cole cites American backing as a reason for the conflict’s duration and notes internal Israeli debates over the truce. Despite ongoing efforts, Hamas’s leadership and military presence remain.

US progressive groups like Justice Democrats and Adalah Justice Project urge a stop to unconditional US support for Israel. They regard the pause as much-needed, but maintain that only a permanent ceasefire and meaningful change will halt the violence. Advocacy for a lasting end to hostilities grows stronger.

Asian stock markets ended the week positively, with Hong Kong and Mainland China leading, while the Philippines and Singapore underperformed. Internet companies listed in Hong Kong outperformed their US counterparts, fueling optimism in US trading as well. Diplomatic progress between China and the US continues, including a meeting between China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi and US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, as well as a planned meeting with President Biden. There is increased anticipation for a potential summit between President Biden and President Xi at the upcoming APEC conference. The Associated Press quoted Wang Yi on the need for a stable and healthy US-China relationship.

China's industrial profits for September grew by 11.9% year-over-year. Although this is a slower pace than the previous month, the cumulative year-to-date decline also narrowed, indicating steady recovery. Talk continues around a possible reduction in the bank reserve requirement ratio (RRR), coinciding with a scheduled government economic meeting next week. Leading Chinese firms, such as CATL, Livzon Pharmaceutical, and Joincare Pharmaceutical, announced significant buybacks; CATL’s stock gained after revealing a RMB 2–3 billion buyback for employee incentives. Major financial groups, including HSBC, AIA, and Standard Chartered, also repurchased shares.

Foreign investors remained net buyers of mainland Chinese stocks through Northbound Stock Connect for the second day, adding $627 million. The healthcare sector was the top performer, highlighted by CSPC Pharmaceuticals' share surge after a cancer trial approval. Internet leaders Tencent, Alibaba, and Meituan reported notable increases, coinciding with strong early Singles Day sales indicators.

According to Chinese metrics, the US does not register a trade deficit with China when including revenue made by US companies operating there. Both the Hang Seng and Hang Seng Tech indexes recorded gains of over 2%, and overall trading activity increased with less short selling. Growth stocks and small-cap companies outperformed, and all sectors advanced—especially healthcare, real estate, and consumer staples.

Mainland China’s indices (Shanghai, Shenzhen, and STAR Board) all rose, with elevated trading volumes. Sectors such as healthcare, industrials, and communications excelled, while insurance, coal, and precious metals lagged. Mainland and foreign investors showed continued interest in Chinese stocks, with Tianqi Lithium as a significant focus.

Webinars on China’s real estate sector and financial outlook are scheduled on November 1 and 2.

article_content: Google has officially launched its Maps app for the iPhone 5, offering users a reliable alternative to the problematic Apple Maps. Since Apple swapped out Google Maps for its own service in September, users have encountered a slew of errors, leading to heavy criticism and even safety warnings from Australian authorities after Apple Maps reportedly led people into unsafe areas. Apple faced intense backlash, prompting public apologies and a shakeup in its software leadership. In answer to these issues, Google built a completely redesigned Maps app for iOS, available on iPhone and iPod Touch with iOS 5.1 or newer, and supporting more than 40 countries and 29 languages. Daniel Graf, head of Google Maps for Mobile, said the app now offers improved navigation, expanded map visibility, public transit routes, live traffic updates, 2D/3D map views, and the popular Street View feature. These enhancements are aimed at resolving shortcomings found in Apple’s mapping software. Apple's map service, developed using data from partners like TomTom and aerial surveys, initially received poor feedback due to missing locations, misdirected routes, and unclear images. One notable case involved drivers ending up in remote Australian outback, a situation local police called 'potentially life-threatening' due to harsh environmental conditions. The widespread discontent was echoed on social media platforms, leading CEO Tim Cook to apologize and encourage users to consider alternatives until improvements were implemented. Two executives in charge of the project were eventually replaced. While the new Google Maps for iOS is still missing some features found on Android—such as indoor navigation—and doesn’t yet have a version for iPad, it boasts a robust database and an easy-to-use design. Apple Maps has made progress since its debut but has yet to match Google’s reliability for everyday navigation. Some analysts believe the map controversy contributed to a dip in Apple’s share price, raising concerns about future innovation. For now, Google Maps returns much-needed confidence to iPhone users seeking dependable directions.

The U.S. economy added 150,000 jobs in October, a notable decrease from previous months, as the unemployment rate rose to 3.9%. Significant job losses were recorded in manufacturing, largely due to the auto-workers strike. The entertainment industry also continued to lose positions, with 5,400 jobs cut in motion picture and sound recording, reducing employment in the sector to 428,200. Since May, the industry has shed 44,000 jobs, attributed at least in part to ongoing strikes. Earlier this month, the Writers Guild of America (WGA) approved a new contract, but negotiations between SAG-AFTRA and the studios are still underway.

Previous estimates that showed robust job growth—336,000 jobs added in September—were revised down to 297,000 by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), while August's numbers were also corrected downward by 62,000 to 165,000. The BLS often makes such adjustments as it receives more comprehensive data. October's job gains fell short of expectations and were below the 12-month average of 258,000 per month.

Meanwhile, the United Auto Workers (UAW) union reached a tentative agreement with General Motors this week, concluding its labor actions against Detroit automakers. Manufacturing employment declined by 35,000 in October, with 33,000 of these lost in motor vehicles and parts, mainly due to strike activity.

The Federal Reserve held its key interest rate steady at 5.25%–5.5% this week, following 11 previous hikes aimed at curbing inflation and achieving a so-called "soft landing" for the economy.

Justin Wolfers, a University of Michigan professor, noted that these jobs figures closely follow the ideal scenario for a soft landing. "I might have liked a somewhat stronger report, but if you had asked the Fed for dream numbers, these are them," he wrote on X/Twitter. "Employment growth is moderating to sustainable levels, labor supply remains robust, and wage growth is moderating to rates consistent with the inflation target."

Noah Yasif, lead labor economist at UKG, commented that the labor market is "finding its calm." He wrote, "The days of explosive growth are gone, as the labor market shifts into healthier and more sustainable territory. All indicators point to a continued lull in the immediate future. It’s a slowdown, not a collapse."

Additionally, publishing saw a loss of 4,500 jobs, reducing total employment to 925,300, while employment in broadcasting and among content providers held steady at 347,700. The largest job gains in October occurred in the health care, government, and social assistance sectors. More information is expected to follow.

Sasampun punika, Writers Guild of America (WGA) sampun ngesahang kontrak anyar ring bulan puniki, tur negosiasi antara SAG-AFTRA sareng studio masih kalaksanayang. 

Estimasi pertumbuhan pekerjaan bulan September sane prasida nyenengin—336.000—sampun kasenggakan dados 297.000 olih Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), tur angka bulan Agustus prasida kasenggakan olih 62.000 dados 165.000. BLS rika ngelaksanayang revisi yening sampun ngancan dados sane luwih lengkap. Tambahan pekerjaan ring Oktober puniki prasida ngantos di bawah rata-rata bulanan sane wenten ring 258.000. 

Sewenten punika, United Auto Workers (UAW) sampun ngemargiang kesepakatan indik tentatif sareng General Motors minggu puniki, nyidayang aksi buruh ring perusahaan otomotif Detroit. Lapangan kerja manufaktur ngestahangang penyusutan 35.000 ring Oktober, sareng 33.000 ring antuk mobil tur sparepart, sane sebagian besar antuk mogok kerama. 

Federal Reserve mantenang suku bunga utama ring 5,25%–5,5% minggu puniki, sampun ngelaksanayang 11 kali naikang suku bunga ngatengin inflasi lan ngajegang ekonomi ring 'soft landing'. 

Justin Wolfers, guru besar ring University of Michigan, ngesengin angka sane ngemargiang 'soft landing'. "Tiang prasida ngajengang laporan sané dadua becik, napi malih yening Fed nyantosangang angka ngidang, puniki," pesu ring X/Twitter. "Pertumbuhan pekerjaan nyarengin tingkatan sane sustainable, pasokan tenaga kerja tetap kuat, miwah pertumbuhan upah nyantosangang target inflasi." 

Noah Yasif, ekonom ring UKG, ngidangang pasar kerja dados langkung tenang. "Warsa pertumbuhan sane meledak sampun lewat, pasar tenaga kerja ngalantur ring arah sane langkung sehat tur sustainable. Apang indikasi prasida nganut peredam ring jagi, puniki slowing, nenten kolaps." 

Industri penerbit ngumang 4.500 pekerjaan (total dados 925.300), ring broadcasting sareng penyedia konten tetep ajeg ring 347.700. Lapangan kerja sane nglaksanayang pertumbuhan ageng ring bidang kesehatan, pemerintahan, miwah bantuan sosial. Malih dados jagi rauh.

Bruce Jenner has stated he is cooperating with police as they investigate a fatal car accident involving the well-known reality TV star. In a statement released Sunday by his publicist, Alan Nierob, Jenner expressed condolences to the family and loved ones affected by the tragedy and said he is praying for them. Jenner also assured he would continue to assist the investigation in every way possible.

Initial reports suggested that paparazzi were pursuing Jenner during the incident. However, Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department investigators have found no evidence suggesting that photographers contributed to the crash. Lt. John Lecrivain stated that while having paparazzi around is common for Jenner, there is no indication they played a role in this accident.

Authorities have not yet determined who was at fault, and details about the victim remain undisclosed. According to Sgt. Phillip Brooks, Jenner was driving a black Cadillac SUV, which became the third vehicle in a multiple rear-end collision on the Pacific Coast Highway in Malibu. The collision began with a black Toyota Prius, followed by a white Lexus sedan. Jenner's SUV, which was towing a trailer with an all-terrain vehicle, collided with the Lexus from behind, pushing it into oncoming traffic where it was struck by a Hummer H2. The driver of the Lexus was killed. No information about the deceased was immediately available.

Jenner, 65, was not injured. Reports indicate Jenner's SUV left skid marks at the scene. The crash occurred shortly after noon, and the Sheriff's Department has since opened a vehicular manslaughter investigation, which will examine all drivers involved. The department stated that all surviving drivers, including Jenner, are cooperating. Jenner voluntarily took a field sobriety test before leaving the scene.

Five children and two adults were hospitalized with injuries. The accident happened on a challenging stretch of highway characterized by narrow, twisting roads. In an unrelated event, a vehicle later drove through safety barriers at the scene and struck two cars involved in the original accident. The driver was arrested for suspected DUI.

Jenner rose to fame after winning the 1976 Olympic decathlon and later appeared in commercials and television shows, most recently gaining prominence as a member of the Kardashian family on their E! reality show. Jenner and Kris Jenner, his former spouse, divorced last year. E! reported that Jenner was not filming 'Keeping Up with the Kardashians' at the time of the accident.

article_content: Bettie Page, legendary pinup icon, died at age 85 in a Los Angeles hospital after suffering a heart attack and pneumonia, her agent confirmed on Thursday. Recognized for helping usher in the sexual revolution, Page captivated the public with her free-spirited attitude and open sensuality. 'She embodied beauty and captured the imagination of generations,' said her agent Mark Roesler. Often cited as one of the most photographed women of the 20th century, Page became reclusive in her later years. Despite her seclusion, her images remained influential, spurring a wide range of merchandise, from action figures to clothing lines. Her enduring popularity was evident as BettiePage.com received around 20 million hits monthly, and a TVGuide.com poll named her the 'ultimate sex goddess,' surpassing cultural icons like Marilyn Monroe. Born in Tennessee on April 22, 1923, Page grew up in poverty. Though originally named 'Betty' on her birth certificate, she later adopted the spelling 'Bettie.' At a time when few women attended college, she earned a Bachelor of Arts in Education from Peabody College in 1944. However, her teaching career struggled due to her striking appearance, as she reportedly had difficulty managing students, particularly boys. After ending her marriage to Billy Neal in 1947, Page’s modeling career began, catalyzed by a police officer-photographer who suggested her trademark black bangs. She soon appeared on countless magazine covers and became a popular pinup figure, including her Playboy centerfold in January 1955. Playboy founder Hugh Hefner regarded Page as a milestone, noting her compelling smile and personality. Her collaboration with Irving Klaw in playful bondage and fetish photography later influenced popular culture. Page’s acting career was said to be impeded by her Southern accent and refusal to conform to Hollywood norms, including declining to sleep with a producer. She later expressed regret over missing a screening opportunity from Jack Warner, as she was attempting to save her marriage at the time. In 1958, Page withdrew from public life. She later cited a religious conversion and move to Florida for her absence. According to her biography, her life became challenging in the late 1970s after her third marriage ended. Page faced mental instability, mood swings, and legal troubles, and was eventually diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia. She reemerged in 2003 at Playboy’s 50th anniversary party, her first public appearance in decades. Bettie Page’s private funeral service is scheduled for Tuesday at Westwood Cemetery in Los Angeles, where she will be buried close to Marilyn Monroe.

Over the past year, the adoption and interest in artificial intelligence (AI) have soared, especially as generative AI technology becomes more widely available. This rapid expansion has brought issues of data protection and privacy to the forefront for business leaders, governments, and consumers alike.

The Exponential Rise of Data
While data-driven innovations—like Google search, smart assistants, and healthcare technologies—have generated significant benefits, the unchecked growth in data collection, storage, and sharing has also led to serious risks, including data breaches, cyberattacks, identity theft, and misuse of personal information. The global amount of data is estimated at 120 zettabytes (120 trillion gigabytes), a figure expected to climb as digital technologies and internet usage expand through mobile devices, social media, and connected systems.

As more technologies leverage vast data resources, such as AI and IoT, leaders face the challenge of utilizing data for progress while ensuring responsibility and compliance.

The Downside of More Data
The explosive growth of personal data has sometimes resulted in privacy invasions, as greater data availability increases the risk of cyber threats. Individuals are increasingly concerned about privacy and security, leading governments to introduce regulations like GDPR, CCPA, COPPA, and HIPAA to manage data access, collection, storage, and sharing. For example, Japan recently warned OpenAI about collecting sensitive data without consent. As data crosses borders, international collaboration is becoming essential to protect privacy.

As regulations tighten, organizations are reassessing their data management strategies and boosting cybersecurity measures such as identity verification and multifactor authentication. Protecting customer data has become crucial to maintaining customer trust, as people become more aware of the value and implications of their information.

Evolving Data Privacy and Protection
Privacy is evolving due to legal frameworks, shifting social expectations, and technological advancements. Businesses are facing four major trends:

1. Growing demand for control—Consumers, businesses, and regions increasingly want control over how their data is accessed and used, expecting data sharing to occur ethically and with informed consent. Strict privacy regulations are being enacted worldwide.

2. Expectations for transparency and accountability—Organizations are expected to be transparent about data collection and usage, adopting clear privacy commitments and facing consequences for breaches or noncompliance.

3. Rise of privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs)—Innovations are emerging to minimize data collection, storage, and sharing. These technologies are becoming standard but continued progress is needed to further strengthen privacy safeguards.

4. Integration of privacy into design—"Privacy by design" is being embraced, with companies like WhatsApp leading early efforts in privacy-centric user experiences.

Impact on Customer Experience
According to Gartner, 84% of businesses now view data privacy as the most critical factor when selecting software. Strong privacy standards are increasingly mandatory, and those organizations that excel in data protection can gain a competitive edge. Customer experience (CX) leaders need to embed privacy measures—such as data masking, minimization, anonymization, and robust access controls—across the customer journey. Enhanced privacy technologies will make it easier for companies to protect data and maintain consumer trust. As we approach 2024, the role of AI in bringing privacy issues to the forefront is set to keep growing.

Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for top-level CIOs, CTOs, and technology executives.

Ring warsa puniki, panganggén tur kapentingan ring kecanggihan buatan (AI) ngametuangang ngelantur ageng utamanye ring AI generatif sane dados wenten ring akéh krama. Puniki medadosang indik proteksi data tur kerahasiaan dados pisan ring pemimpin bisnis, pemerintah, miwah para konsumen.

Data Ngalantur Ngantos Ageng
Ring inovasi berbasis data—makadi Google search, smart assistant, miwah teknologi kesehatan—nyangloka indik kamarginan sane becik, nanging pertumbuhan data sane tan kaaturang prasida ngalanturang risiko, makadi kebocoran data, serangan siber, maling identitas, miwah penyalahgunaan data pribadi. Total data global prasida kaduga ngantos 120 zettabytes (120 triliun gigabyte), lan angka punika presida nambah majalaran pertumbuhan teknologi digital, panganggén internet, piranti mobile, sosial media, lan sistem sané nyambung liu.

Teknologi sané berkembang massa, makadi AI tur IoT, nglaksanayang pemimpin prasida ngatur data secara tanggung jawab tur manut hukum.

Sisi Lain Data Ageng
Pertumbuhan data pribadi marrupaang gangguan privasi, sekancan ancaman siber madagingin. Krama mulai kukuh ring privasi miwah keamanan, pemerintah makta peraturan kadadosang GDPR, CCPA, COPPA, HIPAA ngaatur akses, ngumpul, nyimpen, miwah ngayahang data. Upaminya, Jepang nimbali OpenAI becik nglaksanayang data sensitif tan wenten idin ring krama. Data sane mlali ring antar negara duaning dados puniki saling perluang kerjasama internasional ring perlindungan privasi.

Makta aturan makin ketat, organisasi ngelaksanayang peninjauan ulang pengelolaan data tur ngelaksanayang penguatan keamanan siber sekancan verifikasi identitas miwah otentikasi multifaktor. Proteksi data pelanggan dados banget utama ngempanin kapercayaan pelanggan utamannya, krama prasida ngidangang keanggen data dirine.

Evolusi Kerahasiaan Data
Perkembangan privasi data kasabab hukum anyar, perubahan norma sosial, lan teknologi. Bisnis prasida ngalaksanayang 4 tren dados utama:

1. Peningkatan kontrol—Konsumen, bisnis, miwah wilayah prasida ajengan kontrol ring data driki, ngametuang akses tur pemangdaang data sane etis miwah ring idin sane jelas. Regulasi privasi ketat dados katah ring jagat.

2. Transparansi dan tanggung jawab—Organisasi prasida jelas transparan ring ngumpul tur ngajegang data, ngatur komitmen privasi miwah ngalaksanayang tanggung jawab utawi nampi sangsi yening kaanggen ngalantur data.

3. Teknologi pelindung privasi (PET)—Inovasi ring minim data sane kasub ngumpul tur ngajegang. PET sampun dados standar, inovasi taler wenten dados nambah kekuatan perlindungan.

4. Integrasi privasi ring desain produk—'Privacy by design' doanh kang nglaksanayang ring ngembangang aplikasi miwah produk, makadi WhatsApp sane dados pelopor jagat user privacy.

article_content: The US economy experienced much higher GDP growth in the third quarter compared to the first two quarters of the year. Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annualized rate of 4.9%, according to the advance estimate for Q3 from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, surpassing the forecast of 4.3%. This suggests significantly stronger growth than the roughly 2% rates recorded in Q1 and Q2 of the year. Real personal consumption expenditures rose by 4.0%, which is notably higher than the 0.8% growth in the second quarter, based on seasonally adjusted annual rates. Meanwhile, real fixed investments slowed down from 5.2% in Q2 to 0.8% in Q3. According to a news release about the data, 'The increase in real GDP reflected increases in consumer spending, private inventory investment, exports, state and local government spending, federal government spending, and residential fixed investment, partly offset by a decrease in nonresidential fixed investment. Imports, which are subtracted in the calculation of GDP, increased.' The Biden Administration celebrated the robust economic numbers. Joelle Gamble, deputy director of the White House National Economic Council, told Insider that recent GDP reports show solid growth, with consumer spending and manufacturing investments being key contributors, while inflation is cooling. Gamble emphasized the resilience of both the US economy and its workers, stating, 'We're seeing an economy that is growing strong—from the middle out and the bottom up, not the top down.' Despite the positive growth, some economists warn of challenges ahead. Gregory Daco, chief economist at EY, commented that while signs of strength might fuel speculation about a reaccelerating economy, he does not expect the momentum to last. 'Cost fatigue, rising debt servicing costs, and slowing job growth are about to be felt more widely by consumers and businesses,' Daco said, adding that the drop in business equipment investment is concerning. While the advance estimates and earlier results show strong GDP gains, some experts predict a recession could occur, though likely a mild one. The Conference Board forecasts a mild downturn next year, stating, 'While the prospects for a soft landing have risen, The Conference Board believes it is more probable that the US economy will slip into a short and shallow recession in early 2024.' According to the brief, both the economy and the labor market are expected to cool in early 2024. The US labor market added 336,000 jobs in September, following a revised gain of 227,000 in August. Larry Adam of Raymond James noted in a recent report that growth will likely slow over the next nine months, leading to a mild recession. Rising headwinds for consumers are cited as a contributing factor. Although some concerns persist regarding a mild recession, a recent post about Bankrate’s quarterly survey of economists observed that the chances of a recession, based on the average forecast among respondents, have dropped from 65% in Q3 2022 to 46% in Q3 this year.

article_content: Warren Buffett has donated $2.8 billion worth of Berkshire Hathaway stock to five charities this week, as part of his continued plan to give away nearly all of his fortune. At age 83, Buffett gave about 21.73 million Class B shares of Berkshire Hathaway, his well-known investment company, according to a regulatory filing. About 16.6 million shares, valued at over $2.1 billion, were given to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, which focuses on improving education, health, and reducing poverty. The rest went to four family charities, including a foundation named after his late first wife, Susan, along with foundations for his children Howard, Peter, and Susan. This $2.8 billion gift is Buffett’s largest donation to these organizations so far, reflecting Berkshire Hathaway’s near-record share price. He has made annual gifts to such foundations since 2006. Even after this donation, Buffett still owns nearly 20 percent of Berkshire Hathaway’s stock, making his net worth $65.8 billion on the donation day, according to Forbes magazine. Forbes reported that only Carlos Slim, the Mexican telecommunications magnate, and Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft and director at Berkshire, had higher net worths. Berkshire Hathaway operates over 80 businesses and ended March with more than $146 billion in stock and bond investments. Buffett has led the Omaha, Nebraska-based company since 1965 and is widely considered one of the most successful investors of the 20th century.

article_content: Your phone's lock screen could soon become a space for branded advertisements, appearing every time you turn on your device. This concept is central to a new Android app, Lockscreen Lockview, which is set to launch soon. Rather than simple poster ads, the entire lock screen would display a company's branding and supply users with information. The app is being developed in partnership with online advertising company Conduit. ‘This is truly prime real estate,’ said Ori Lavie, Conduit's VP of mobile strategy. ‘Brands gain much higher exposure, driving more traffic to their app or website.’ These branded lock screens are expected to be created with companies that provide regular updates—like sports results or stock prices—giving users an incentive to use the app. A test version of Lockscreen Lockview is currently available for free on Google Play. This version is not branded and allows users to customize their lock screen, including shortcuts to recent apps or photo galleries. Conduit has stated that the current free version will not be developed further. Instead, the company will release new branded versions in collaboration with companies offering informational updates. Importantly, Conduit emphasized that it will not allow purely advertisement-based apps; the lock screen must offer useful features.

Aplikasi puniki dikembangang sareng perusahaan iklan online, Conduit. ‘Puniki tanah emas sejati,’ rauh Ori Lavie, VP strategi seluler Conduit. ‘Merek dadosang paplusan sane ageng, nglaksanayang wah ring aplikasi utawi website mereka.’ Layar kunci ber-merek puniki kedagingangang sekancan perusahaan sane ngelanturang update rutin—nebeng hasil olahraga utawi harga saham—ngewantuang pengguna dados prasida nganggon aplikasi puniki. article_content: Ken Mattingly, a prominent figure in NASA history renowned for his pivotal contributions during the Apollo 13 crisis, has died at 87, NASA confirmed. In a Thursday statement, NASA Administrator Bill Nelson honored Thomas Kenneth Mattingly II for his vital role in the Apollo Program and remarked that Mattingly's character would be remembered for generations. NASA did not disclose the cause or location of death, but The New York Times indicated he died in Arlington, Virginia. A former Navy pilot, Mattingly joined NASA in 1966, playing a significant part in the development of spacesuits and life-support backpacks for the Apollo missions. His first venture into space came in 1972 as the command module pilot of Apollo 16, where he orbited the moon while his fellow crew members landed on its surface. As the mission returned to Earth, Mattingly conducted a spacewalk to retrieve photographic film from the lunar orbit. In addition to his Apollo 16 mission, Mattingly went on to command two space shuttle flights, eventually retiring as a rear admiral from both the Navy and NASA. Notably, his most dramatic impact came on a mission he did not fly: Mattingly was removed from the Apollo 13 crew days before launch due to exposure to German measles, though he never became ill. His seat was filled by John Swigert Jr. When an oxygen tank explosion jeopardized Apollo 13’s astronauts, Mattingly, with intricate knowledge of the spacecraft, worked closely with engineers and support staff to develop life-saving strategies for James Lovell, Fred Haise, and John Swigert. Their safe return—after four days using the lunar module as a lifeboat—became one of the most famous rescues in space history. Nelson stressed Mattingly's essential behind-the-scenes role, highlighting his real-time decisions that helped bring the crew safely home. Reflecting on Apollo 13 in a 2001 NASA interview, Mattingly shared that their success started with the mindset that failure was not an option from the very beginning. Apollo 13’s story was immortalized in James Lovell’s book 'Lost Moon' and brought to a global audience through the 1995 film 'Apollo 13,' with actor Gary Sinise depicting Mattingly.

article_content:
US President Joe Biden and Chinese President Xi Jinping are preparing for a high-stakes meeting in California, with a range of challenging topics likely to take center stage. Expected subjects include trade, the conflict in the Middle East, Taiwan, the South China Sea, technology export bans, fentanyl trafficking, and concerns about election interference.

The past year has been politically tumultuous for Xi Jinping, marked by the unexpected removal of top appointees—including the foreign minister and defense minister—an overhaul of military leadership, and economic headwinds such as rising youth unemployment and persistent challenges in the housing and technology sectors. As a result, Xi has strong motivation to project strength and stability both at home and abroad. 

For Biden, one of the primary objectives is to re-establish military communications between Washington and Beijing to reduce the risk of misunderstandings turning into dangerous confrontations. The US also aims to urge China to use its influence with Iran to encourage regional stability in the Middle East and warn against providing military aid to Russia. 

While no major diplomatic breakthroughs are anticipated, officials view the meeting as crucial for preventing a further deterioration in US-China relations. The leaders are unlikely to sign any dramatic agreements, but continued dialogue may help ease tensions—especially around Taiwan and other flashpoints such as technology trade restrictions. 

Additionally, American concerns include the influx of Chinese-made fentanyl and potential interference in upcoming US elections. Xi is expected to leverage coverage of the summit in Chinese media to bolster his domestic image, while Biden is hoping his diplomatic experience can help defuse tensions. Observers agree the significance of the meeting lies not in dramatic outcomes but in maintaining communication and avoiding escalation between the world’s two largest powers.

article_content: HBO's Succession is an award-winning satirical comedy-drama series that captivated audiences each week, eager to see the next move of the dysfunctional Roy family. Created by Jesse Armstrong, the show has received numerous accolades for its gripping stories centered around Waystar RoyCo, the global media and entertainment conglomerate every family member is vying to control. Although episodes like 'All the Bells Say' and 'Connor’s Wedding' have sparked intense discussion among fans and critics, many underrated Succession episodes also deserve recognition. While these stories may not feature the dramatic twists of the most popular episodes, they provide crucial moments of character development and subtle plot advancement, and are essential to the overall narrative. In 'Mass in Time of War,' patriarch Logan Roy (Brian Cox) is at his weakest, confined to Sarajevo as his children conspire against him. Kendall (Jeremy Strong) gathers his siblings at Rava’s (Natalie Gold) apartment and insists their unity will guarantee his victory. However, tensions mount when Kendall hints he will be CEO, and a timely delivery of donuts from their watchful father unnerves Shiv (Sarah Snook), Roman (Kieran Culkin), and Connor (Alan Ruck), who ultimately side with Logan. Despite being less action-packed than other episodes, 'Mass in Time of War' stands out as a brilliant example of Succession’s strengths, especially in depicting the Roy children's unease, vulnerabilities, and self-interest. While they long to escape their father's control, they remain uncomfortably tethered to him, believing alliances with Logan still bring them closer to power. As the GoJo acquisition negotiations grow more complex, Kendall navigates shifting loyalties after a call from GoJo’s Lukas Matsson (Alexander Skarsgård), which he keeps secret. Meanwhile, Connor faces heartbreak as his fiancée Willa (Justine Lupe) considers backing out of their engagement. The siblings find camaraderie at a karaoke bar but soon face another confrontation when Logan unexpectedly joins them. Though 'Rehearsal' may seem forgettable at first, revisiting the episode reveals how effectively it makes the flawed, often unlikeable characters relatable. The episode humanizes the Roys by showing their pain, driven by both present pressures and past traumas. This is especially evident when Kendall and Shiv demand an apology from Logan for his past abuse, a moment contrasted by Roman’s hesitation to break away from their father. Following the dramatic first season climax—Kendall’s accident during Shiv and Tom’s wedding—the episode 'The Summer Palace' had high expectations. It manages to meet them, portraying Kendall haunted by his involvement in a tragic accident as he faces the press and backs down from a takeover. Logan’s swift reclaiming of power over his son is clear when Kendall claims: 'I saw their plan, and my dad’s plan was better.' Kendall’s awkward meeting with Stewy (Arian Moayed) only hints at how often he and his siblings shift allegiances, driven more by desperation than strategy. Succession often skillfully parodies real-life figures and events, such as the lifestyles of the extremely wealthy and the volatility of digital media. In 'Vaulter,' Kendall and Roman are assigned to evaluate the startup Vaulter, now owned by Waystar. While Kendall sees potential, Roman is skeptical and notes staff efforts to unionize. Ultimately, Kendall must fire Vaulter’s staff. The episode bluntly exposes the harsh realities of media acquisitions and shutdowns, offering a nuanced critique of the industry. Jeremy Strong’s understated performance as Kendall highlights his father's control and the show’s unique blend of tragedy and comedy. When fans seek similar series, they're often drawn by Succession’s blend of political intrigue and chaotic family relationships. In 'The Disruption,' Logan and Kendall each attempt public relations maneuvers, Shiv fights for her reputation, and Tom Wambsgans (Matthew Macfadyen) even volunteers to take the fall for Logan if federal investigations escalate. Tensions peak when Kendall sabotages Shiv's speech by playing Nirvana’s 'Rape Me.' The episode is emotionally charged, ending with Shiv’s public letter targeting Kendall’s mental health, underscoring the increasingly hostile family dynamic. 'Austerlitz' takes place on Connor’s ranch in New Mexico, featuring an attempted family therapy session. The episode explores each Roy’s troubled past, including Kendall’s relapse—tragically confirmed after media rumors. A confrontation with Logan highlights the emotional and physical scars within the family. Seamlessly blending dark humor and emotional gravity, 'Austerlitz' captures Succession’s signature storytelling, offering greater understanding of the Roys’ complexities, especially through Jeremy Strong’s performance as Kendall. As Kendall’s involvement in the cruise scandal is exposed, the family travels to the Future Freedom Summit in Richmond, Virginia to select a presidential candidate who will protect Waystar’s interests. Meeting the controversial Jeryd Mencken (Justin Kirk), Logan sees his potential for Waystar’s right-leaning news network. 'What It Takes' delivers sharp commentary on behind-the-scenes political machinations and the influence wielded by powerful families like the Roys. While its focus on political dealings may alienate some viewers, the writing and acting remain top-notch, with clear parallels to real-world politics.

article_content: On October 1, health insurance marketplaces established by the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) will begin allowing Americans to enroll, with new coverage set to begin on January 1, 2014. At the same time, the U.S. government risks a partial shutdown if Congress cannot agree on a funding bill. This political dispute is largely tied to debate over Obamacare, but most of the law’s functions will continue regardless because its key funding sources are not tied to the regular budget cycle. If you receive insurance through your job or government programs like Medicare or Medicaid, your situation will mostly remain the same for now. There may be gradual changes by some employers, like reducing benefits or hours for some workers, but these effects are not immediate. People who buy their own health insurance may have to adapt. Obamacare mandates that plans cover a minimum set of services and limits how insurers set premiums. Existing plans that don’t meet these standards may be discontinued, requiring customers to select new options from the exchanges. For some healthy individuals, premiums may rise, but those with greater health needs could see costs decrease due to broader coverage. Uninsured individuals are required to obtain health coverage—either by enrolling in expanded Medicaid (where available) or by purchasing private insurance from the new exchanges. Government subsidies will help lower the cost for individuals and families who meet income requirements, such as singles earning less than $45,960 or families of four under $94,200. Obamacare doesn’t mean most Americans will get their health insurance from the government directly. The law establishes online marketplaces offering private plans, with the government setting rules to make coverage accessible and affordable. Anyone choosing not to purchase insurance will face a penalty—either $95 per adult or 1% of income over $10,000, whichever is higher—considered a tax by the Supreme Court. This aims to ensure a broad pool of participants for the insurance system. Despite political battles in Congress and the potential for a government shutdown, these major elements of Obamacare will go ahead as planned, giving millions access to new forms of health coverage.

article_content: Dr. Benjamin Neel, a prominent Jewish cancer biologist and former director of the Perlmutter Cancer Center at NYU Langone Health, has filed a lawsuit against the medical center and New York University. Dr. Neel alleges he was wrongfully terminated due to social media posts he made regarding the Israel-Hamas war. According to the lawsuit, Neel was dismissed after reposting tweets on X (formerly Twitter) that criticized those supporting violence against Israelis in the aftermath of the October 7 attacks by Hamas. The civil suit, filed in New York State Supreme Court, claims the 67-year-old physician was made a 'sacrificial lamb' to give the appearance of impartiality by NYU Langone Health. The lawsuit seeks a jury trial and at least $500,000 in damages. NYU Langone Health spokesperson Steve Ritea stated that the institution stands by its decision to terminate Dr. Neel, emphasizing a commitment to maintaining high standards and a safe, inclusive environment. Ritea added that Dr. Neel, as a leader, violated social media policies in a series of public posts and later locked his account. The lawsuit says Dr. Neel was initially suspended and subsequently fired on November 10, allegedly in breach of his employment agreement, which damaged his professional reputation. One of the reposts cited in the lawsuit included a cartoon featuring climate activist Greta Thunberg. Another repost referenced a flag displayed at a Brooklyn protest indicating solidarity between the LGBTQ+ and Palestinian communities, with Neel adding the caption, 'Talk about an oxymoron…' Dr. Neel's attorney, Milton Williams, called the firing a 'travesty,' stating that Neel is possibly the first to lose his job and reputation over private social media posts challenging those celebrating attacks on innocent people in Israel.

Dr. Neel mengklaim bahwa ia diberhentikan secara tidak adil karena postingan di media sosial terkait perang Israel-Hamas. article_content: The European Union’s top court has ruled that individuals fleeing persecution in their home countries due to their sexual orientation are entitled to seek asylum across EU member states. According to the European Court of Justice (ECJ), laws that criminalize homosexuality—and especially those that are enforced through imprisonment—can be considered a form of persecution. The court emphasized that requiring someone to conceal their sexuality to avoid such treatment would mean denying them a fundamental aspect of their identity. International agreements require asylum seekers to provide evidence that they face a credible threat of persecution on grounds including race, religion, ethnicity, or political opinion. With this new decision, sexual orientation has been recognized as grounds for asylum. However, it remains unclear how authorities should determine whether an applicant's claim regarding their sexuality is genuine. This decision arose from three cases involving individuals from Sierra Leone, Uganda, and Senegal, who sought asylum in the Netherlands. The Dutch Supreme Court asked the ECJ to clarify how EU laws should be applied in such scenarios. While the ECJ established that national authorities need to assess whether anti-gay laws are enforced in a way that amounts to persecution, the court has not yet provided specific guidance on how to evaluate the authenticity of an applicant’s sexual orientation. That issue remains unresolved and is expected to be addressed sometime in the future.

article_content: Team Sky chief Sir Dave Brailsford has set an ambitious goal for his riders: to establish themselves as ‘indisputably the best cycling team in the world’ by 2020. Since Team Sky's launch in 2009, Brailsford’s vision to produce a British Tour de France winner became reality, with Sir Bradley Wiggins claiming victory in 2012 and Chris Froome following in 2013. Despite amassing 165 victories since its foundation, Brailsford is determined that the team can still improve. He reflected, ‘We had a clear vision for our first five years: to win the Tour de France and inspire a million people to take up cycling. We achieved both goals—twice, in fact, with the Tour de France—which was a terrific accomplishment. But we’re not resting on our laurels; looking back, we believe we could have performed even better.’ As Team Sky looks ahead to the next five years, Brailsford underscores his team’s hunger and commitment to raising their performance to new heights, aiming to be not just the best cycling team, but among the world’s top sports teams.

article_content: Over the past two years, I have consistently advocated for Google to bring back the Pixelbook. My expectations were boosted after Google announced the Pixel 7, Pixel Watch, and Pixel Tablet, but these hopes dimmed when the Pixelbook 2 was reportedly shelved. Still, I am convinced that the time is right for a new Pixelbook. Some may question my persistence, particularly now that the Chromebook Plus initiative is gaining traction. While I appreciate what Chromebook Plus brings, choosing the right Chromebook remains confusing—even for knowledgeable customers like myself. It feels as if Google is leaving the door open for something more premium. Currently, several types of ChromeOS devices exist, though Chromeboxes are relatively uncommon. The main categories are standard Chromebooks, Chromebook Plus, and Chromebooks that meet Plus requirements. The primary difference is which models display the 'Chromebook Plus' branding, appearing with software updates. Introducing these device categories hints that Google might have additional plans. AI advancements, such as those enabled by the new Tensor G3 alongside the Pixel 8 series, and features like Magic Eraser or Photoshop integration, illustrate how central AI is to Google’s vision. More AI features are anticipated for ChromeOS, including customized wallpapers generated from text prompts and other yet-to-be-announced tools. Such technology seemed out of reach not long ago. With Chromebook Plus models available and being marketed, the groundwork is laid. After broader market adoption, it might be time to introduce a new category. The lower end of the Chromebook market has both impressive and disappointing options under $400. For instance, the HP Chromebook x360 13b is a $349 convertible using a MediaTek processor, which makes it ineligible for Chromebook Plus branding (requiring Intel or AMD chips). Similarly priced devices can deliver very different experiences. A future Pixelbook could compete with premium Chromebooks like the HP Dragonfly Pro Chromebook or Acer Chromebook Spin 714. The Framework Laptop Chromebook is another option, although its modular design is unlikely to appear in a new Pixelbook. The $700–$999 Chromebook segment remains open for innovation. If Google wants to lead in AI integration, a new in-house Chromebook—like how Pixel phones showcase Android—could demonstrate its capabilities. Despite a range of existing Chromebooks, Google could set a benchmark in the market. Whether a Pixelbook 2 is in development or not, something feels missing, and I hope Google will address this soon.

article_content: Japan's long-standing political impasse could soon end, as the ruling coalition led by the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and Prime Minister Shinzo Abe now holds a substantial majority in the Upper House, giving it significant legislative power. With this victory comes increased responsibility to deliver on past promises. Abe has been credited with revitalizing Japan’s economy after years of stagnation, though some caution against overconfidence. His economic policies, known as 'Abenomics,' include three main components: aggressive monetary easing, expanded fiscal stimulus, and structural reforms. The first two measures have proceeded without significant opposition and boosted the stock market, though this progress is fragile; market stability faltered when US Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke discussed tapering monetary stimulus. Abenomics aims both to stimulate the economy and encourage consumer spending, but lasting growth depends on deeper structural change. When Abe’s administration released preliminary reform proposals in June, markets were disappointed by their lack of ambition. Concerns persist that entrenched interests within the LDP may block substantial reforms, making delivery challenging. Japan’s involvement in the Trans Pacific Partnership (TPP), a trade agreement with the US and other Asia-Pacific nations, is controversial. Agriculture and medical lobbies strongly oppose market liberalization, and a petition last year gathered eleven million signatures against TPP. Although agriculture accounts for only 1% of GDP, it wields considerable political influence. Leading exporters support trade openness, but many domestic businesses and healthcare advocates are apprehensive. Structural reforms also must address deregulation of the electricity sector and Japan’s high energy import costs. Abe faces public resistance to restarting nuclear reactors, especially after the 2011 Fukushima disaster—about 70% of Japanese favor phasing out nuclear power, even as business interests advocate its return. TEPCO’s management of Fukushima’s cleanup has faced ongoing criticism, and there are concerns that political pressures may override public safety. Abe has additionally proposed changes to corporate taxes and social welfare, both controversial. The Ministry of Finance worries about Japan's high debt-to-GDP ratio (around 240%), and there is reluctance to increase the sales tax for fear it could slow the economy. Critics argue that Abenomics benefits large corporations and the wealthy, while job security and wages lag for ordinary workers. According to an NHK poll, nearly 90% of Japanese said they saw no benefit from Abenomics. Labor market challenges persist, with 38% of workers in unstable, low-wage jobs—twice the level of two decades ago. Addressing these conditions is key to combating deflation. Women are also underrepresented in management and face a wage gap twice the OECD average. While Abe has supported increasing daycare options for working mothers, other measures to support women remain vague, though their participation is considered vital for Japan’s growth. Concerns remain regarding Abe’s focus on constitutional revision, in particular amending Article 9, which renounces war. He currently lacks enough parliamentary support for such changes. Visits to the controversial Yasukuni Shrine, associated with Japan’s wartime legacy, create tension domestically and abroad; since 1978, after war criminals were enshrined, neither Emperor Showa nor Emperor Akihito has visited. While a more patriotic narrative on history is promoted by Abe and allies, critics warn this could damage Japan’s reputation. Japan’s key foreign policy challenge is improving relations with China and South Korea. The territorial dispute with China over the Senkaku/Diaoyu islands remains unresolved. Confidence-building measures, including agreements like the 2008 joint development of East China Sea resources, could help reduce tensions. Abe’s responses to these economic, political, and diplomatic challenges will determine Japan’s direction. Whether his government pursues inclusive, forward-looking policies or reverts to traditional nationalist approaches remains to be seen.

article_content: Jack and Bianca Vaughan began their marriage in an unconventional way, opting to spend their honeymoon at Glastonbury Festival. The pair, hailing from Reading, wed in Glastonbury town before immersing themselves in the festivities at the renowned Somerset event. With thousands entering the grounds, Bianca stood out wearing her wedding gown with classic white Hunter boots, while Jack traded formalwear for a grey t-shirt, shorts, and trainers. The newlyweds strolled hand in hand through the sun-dappled festival fields, merging the joy of their wedding with the lively festival spirit. Glastonbury is celebrated not only for its top-tier music acts but also for its eclectic and adventurous festival fashion. Attendees display a vast range of outfits, from dependable wellies and Barbour jackets to imaginative costumes that include astronauts, Pacman, and vibrant neon looks. Traditional staples like denim shorts mix with daring choices, such as floral crowns, sequined ensembles, and even duvet-inspired dresses. Given the changeable British weather, many come ready for both sunshine and Glastonbury’s storied mud. Bianca’s boots combined fashion with function, well-suited for whatever the weekend might bring. For those seeking a bit more comfort, luxury camping options abound. A standout is the pop-up hotel near the festival grounds, where guests can access amenities like a spa, salon services in a converted train carriage, a restaurant, and high-end showers. Glastonbury’s opening day showcased its signature blend of awe-inspiring music, flamboyant fashion, creative self-expression, and a shared sense of adventure among revellers, promising a weekend of memorable experiences.

article_content: Pakistan has struggled at the Cricket World Cup, suffering three consecutive losses, but the team is looking to start a new winning streak beginning with their upcoming group match against South Africa, according to all-rounder Shadab Khan. Pakistan started the tournament strongly with victories over the Netherlands and Sri Lanka, but then lost to India, Australia, and Afghanistan. The defeat to Afghanistan, their Asian neighbors, was a major upset, with Pakistan losing by eight wickets, which left them in fifth place in the standings. Despite the setbacks, Shadab expressed confidence that the team can recover. Speaking to reporters ahead of Friday’s game against second-placed South Africa in Chennai, he said: 'I think we have underperformed in all three matches. We haven't performed this poorly before. We know we are not playing good cricket.' He added, 'But our team has bounced back from difficult situations in the past, and hopefully we will come out of this one as well. We have complete faith in our team. Before the World Cup, we were performing well, but we haven't played well during the tournament. Bad days happen, but I believe we will begin our winning run starting tomorrow.' Pakistan also has to overcome a negative run rate as they compete for a top-four finish. Shadab described the match against South Africa as the first of many 'do-or-die' games for Pakistan. He identified fielding as a particular area of concern, citing dropped catches on batting-friendly pitches, and noted that the fast bowlers have struggled as a group. 'If you drop a catch or give away an easy boundary, there's no pressure on the batsman, and it can be very costly in the end. The way we’re fielding right now is far below our usual standard,' he explained. 'Our fast bowlers have performed well over the last couple of years wherever they've played. We have faith in them, but sometimes teams go through rough patches. The main problem now is that everyone seems to be struggling at the same time. Hopefully, things turn around tomorrow and everyone finds their form again.'
