article_content: Recent data shows that baby boomers are faring well in the current economy, while millennials continue to struggle. According to the latest findings from Morning Consult’s financial well-being index—which measures feelings of financial security and freedom of choice—baby boomers saw their well-being score rise by 4.04 points from August 2022 to August 2023. For comparison, all U.S. adults experienced a .93-point increase. Morning Consult notes that a one-point gain typically correlates with positive financial changes such as a $15,000 income boost or a 20-point credit score rise. Essentially, boomers saw these improvements multiply four times over the past year. Meanwhile, millennials saw their financial well-being score decrease by .94 points—the largest drop for any age group. This highlights the contrasting economic experiences of millennials and baby boomers, especially in the wake of the pandemic. While older Americans benefited from established savings and home ownership during the pandemic’s economic shifts, younger generations like millennials took on more debt and faced greater uncertainty. According to Jaime Toplin, a financial services analyst at Morning Consult, part of millennials' financial challenges relates to their stage of life. Many are in their peak earning years, starting families, and purchasing homes—positive milestones, but ones that come with mounting expenses. The recent resumption of student loan payments adds to their financial pressures. Morning Consult’s data shows that 26% of millennials have educational debt, compared to just 5% of baby boomers. The survey also found that nearly half of millennials feel their financial situation will prevent them from achieving their life goals, marking a 4% increase from the previous year. In contrast, this sentiment is shared by 38% of all adults. Additionally, 55% of millennials are concerned that their savings won't last, a figure that's up 3% year-over-year and 9% higher than the rate among all adults. Despite these challenges, millennials’ financial standing isn’t entirely dire. Data from the Federal Reserve's 2022 Survey of Consumer Finances reports that Americans aged 35 to 44 (an age group aligning mostly with millennials) had a median net worth of $135,300—an improvement from $105,610 in 2019. However, this group also carries the most debt, with a median of $140,400 per person. In terms of credit card debt, Morning Consult found that 43% of millennials carry such debt, compared to 36% of boomers. On the other hand, baby boomers are consistently performing better financially than younger generations, according to Toplin. Many are financially established, have significant savings, and are less worried about saving for retirement. They're currently benefiting from high interest rates on retirement investments and increased home values. As the economy slows and job prospects shift, boomers are expected to remain resilient. Their entrenched financial position enables them to weather economic challenges effectively, whereas millennials face much greater financial uncertainty.

Indonesia’s top constitutional judge, Anwar Usman, who is President Joko Widodo’s brother-in-law, has been demoted by a judicial ethics panel after being found in violation of court ethics. Usman failed to step aside from a key case about election age requirements, a move that enabled President Widodo’s 36-year-old son, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, to become eligible as a vice presidential candidate with Defense Minister Prabowo Subianto. The court’s narrow five-to-four ruling allowed candidates under 40 who have previously held elected office to run, igniting public criticism and questions about judicial fairness.

The ethics panel, led by former chief justice Jimly Asshiddiqie, determined that Usman committed a serious breach of neutrality and independence, having made room for outside interference in the court’s decision. While Usman will retain his position as one of nine constitutional court judges, he is prohibited from handling election cases where conflicts of interest might arise. The panel also reprimanded the court’s other judges for ethical shortcomings in the case.

Panel member Bintan R Saragih argued Usman should be dishonourably dismissed for his "gross violation" of ethical standards. However, the panel stopped short of removing him entirely, aiming to avoid potential complications before the 2024 elections. Usman cannot serve as chief justice for the remainder of his term, and the court will choose a new leader in the coming days. The decision has intensified debate about President Widodo’s alleged attempts to form a political dynasty, given his son’s nomination for vice president. Widodo, completing his final term, has not formally endorsed any candidate.

John Prescott is making a surprise return to frontline politics at the request of Labour leader Ed Miliband, who has appointed him as a special adviser on climate change. Despite previous criticism of Miliband’s leadership and election strategy, Lord Prescott has been brought in for his experience, particularly from his role as one of the architects of the 1997 Kyoto Protocol. This appointment comes just weeks before the general election and during a period marked by reports of significant divisions within the Labour leadership, particularly between Miliband and Shadow Chancellor Ed Balls.

The move coincides with the increased involvement of other senior Labour figures from the New Labour era, such as Alastair Campbell, who has pledged to help Miliband’s campaign. Some see Prescott’s return as an effort to recapture past electoral successes. However, the decision has raised questions about Labour’s direction, given Miliband’s previous emphasis on moving beyond the New Labour years.

Douglas Alexander, Labour’s election co-ordinator, stated that Prescott is expected to support the party’s campaign in the months ahead, in addition to his policy role on climate change. Yet, only a few months ago, Lord Prescott was publicly critical of Miliband’s strategy, describing it as ‘too timid’ and warning the leadership to avoid cautious approaches.

Current reports highlight ongoing disputes at the top of the Labour party, particularly disagreements over how to pay for Miliband’s pledge to reduce university tuition fees from £9,000 to £6,000. A recent meeting intended to resolve this issue was reportedly unproductive. The divisions have led to some Labour MPs describing tensions as "the Ed aches" or the two leaders being "at logger-Eds," reminiscent of conflicts between previous leaders Tony Blair and Gordon Brown.

Amidst these internal challenges, a new Opinium poll for The Observer shows the Conservatives ahead of Labour for the first time in three years, with the Tories at 35 percent and Labour at 33 percent. Additional recent polls have also indicated a Conservative lead. Ukip and the Greens are polling at 15 and 7 percent respectively, with the Liberal Democrats at 6 percent.

Senajana prasida pernah ngemantenangang Miliband indik kepemimpinan lan strategi pemilihan, Lord Prescott kapilih malih nganutangang pengalaman ida, utamane ring perannyane dados arsitek Protokol Kyoto 1997. Pengangkatan puniki matemu ring warsa, mrasidayang ring cening pemilihan umum lan ring mangda polemik ring puncak pemimpinan Labour, khususnya antara Miliband miwah Shadow Chancellor Ed Balls.

Sasampun puniki, senior New Labour pinaka Alastair Campbell prasida ngerauh anggen nyokong kampanye Miliband. Presidan ida ngajengang wantah dados upaya ngulati kasuksesan ring pemilihan-pemilihan sane sampun kaseksan. Patah punika, ajengan puniki nyidayang tekenan ring para angga Labour ring mana arah partai, nyantosangang Miliband sampun kebet pomembé nyantosang era New Labour.

Douglas Alexander, koordinator pemilihan Labour, maosang Lord Prescott becik nyokong kampanye partai ring pedirgan warsa, taler ring tugasnya indik kebijakan perubahan iklim. Senajana, makta ring bulan-bulan sane sampun, Lord Prescott prasida nampenin strategi Miliband sane kaanggep ‘kelewat ati-ati’ tur ngelingangang pemimpin sane nyantosang pendekatan lebih tegas.

Warsa mangda polemik ring pemimpin Labour, utama indik cara ngidangang biaya janji Miliband ngurangin biaya kuliah saking £9,000 dados £6,000. Laporan ring patemon panglimbak punika prasida tan prasida hasil becik. Polemik sampun nglaksanaang anggota Labour nyarengin istilah "the Ed aches" utawi dua pemimpin dados "at logger-Eds" mila nenten cenik mrasidayang anak ring zaman Tony Blair miwah Gordon Brown.

Ring tengah indik polemik puniki, polling anyar saking Opinium ring The Observer nglaksanayang Partai Konservatif ring 35 persen nglaksanayang puncak ngungkulin Labour ring 33 persen – pisan ring tiga warsa. Polling sané rauh prasida nyidang Tories ngajeng ring Labour. Ukip ring 15 persen, Greens ring 7 persen, miwah Liberal Democrats ring 6 persen.

article_content: Aali attended his first protest on Saturday, joining a major pro-Palestinian march in Washington, DC. "It's important to act when you can," he said. Coming from Pennsylvania by bus that morning, Aali was one of numerous people arriving from outside the city for the National March on Washington: Free Palestine, arranged by nine activist groups. Organizers reported that hundreds of buses, coordinated by community and progressive organizations, brought attendees nationwide to what they hoped would be the largest pro-Palestinian gathering in U.S. history, with expectations around 100,000 participants. Watta made the two-hour drive from Philadelphia, noting, "Distance isn’t important—solidarity is what matters." Others like Mary from Chicago felt compelled to join despite not protesting in decades. Large delegations traveled by bus, such as 750 participants from Boston with Thejas Wesley, and 200 people from Atlanta who traveled overnight, led by K.B. Butler. Many attendees were new to protesting, joining a wave of global support for Palestinians. Recent weeks have seen massive rallies in cities like London, Istanbul, San Francisco, and Los Angeles, spurred by Israel’s ongoing operations in Gaza. On October 7, attacks by Hamas in southern Israel caused over 1,400 deaths and the kidnapping of between 100 and 200 people. In response, Israel has carried out major airstrikes and ground actions in Gaza, a region of about two million residents, nearly half of them children. The Palestinian Health Ministry reports that close to 10,000 people have died in Gaza, including around 3,900 children. While President Biden questioned these numbers’ reliability, the United Nations and World Health Organization have backed the published casualties, though outlets such as Insider could not verify the data. At the Washington rally, demonstrators carried a banner with the names of those killed in Gaza, intending to highlight the conflict’s human impact. As Butler observed, the demonstration marked a political awakening for many attendees.

Akeh peserta sane makta protestan puniki anyar ring aksi, ngametuangangang gelombang solidaritas internasional ring Palestina. Rahina-rahina anyar puniki sampun kalaksanayang demonstrasi ageng ring London, Istanbul, San Francisco, sareng Los Angeles, ring rauh serangan Israel ring Gaza. Ring tanggal 7 Oktober, serangan Hamas ring Israel kidul nyantosangang olih wenten 1,400 tiang medem miwah 100–200 sane kapidabdabangang. Israel nglaksanayang serangan udara miwah darat ring Gaza, daerah sane ngidangangang 2 juta warga, wantah rauh setengah anak-anak. Kementerian Kesehatan Palestina wantah ngemargiang laporan korban sami ngidangang ring 10,000, sekadi 3,900 anak. Presiden Biden nenten nglaksanayang, namun PBB miwah WHO ngedukung data punika, nanging media indik nenten prasida verifikasi. Ring Washington, peserta protestan magehang banderang indik daftar ajengan ring Gaza, nenten wenten nyidayang humanisasi indik korban. Miwah rasan Butler, aksi puniki dados kebangunan politik ring krama sane ngiringang ring aksi punika.

article_content: Tracey McLaughlin, a 51-year-old mother from Manchester, underwent gastric bypass surgery in December 2010 after being warned her weight was putting her health in severe danger. Originally weighing 19 stone, she was wheelchair-bound due to crippling arthritis. Although she lost about 10 stone in the first year and was happy at first, her weight continued to drop. Now at just 5 stone 7 lbs and a BMI of 16, Tracey finds herself mostly bedridden due to extreme weakness, forced to wear children's clothing, and fearing potentially fatal malnutrition. Medical professionals suspect her body's difficulty absorbing nutrients may be related to post-surgical changes or scar tissue, but the exact cause remains unclear after various tests. Despite eating high-calorie meals like bacon sandwiches and takeout, Tracey is unable to gain weight. She says she feels frail and unrecognizable, and deeply regrets undergoing the operation, believing she was happier before it. In her 30s and 40s, Tracey embraced her larger body despite health problems. But with worsening arthritis and unsuccessful attempts at dieting, she was offered gastric bypass as a last resort. The initial rapid weight loss has now become dangerous, and if her condition worsens, she may need to be put on a feeding drip. Gastric bypass surgery is a serious, irreversible procedure typically offered to people with a BMI above 40, or above 35 with significant health issues. The operation reduces stomach size and alters digestion to promote a feeling of fullness and limit calorie absorption. While it can help people lose weight quickly, it carries risks such as internal bleeding, blood clots, and rarely, death. Additional surgeries may be required to address excess skin after significant weight loss. The NHS considers gastric bypass appropriate only when other weight loss methods have failed, reflecting its potential dangers and the commitment required.

Operasi gastric bypass adalah prosedur yang tidak bisa dibatalkan dan hanya dilakukan untuk orang dengan BMI di atas 40, atau di atas 35 jika ada masalah kesehatan yang serius. Operasi ini mengecilkan ukuran lambung dan mengubah sistem cerna agar pasien cepat kenyang dan menyerap lebih sedikit kalori. Meski membantu menurunkan berat badan dengan cepat, ada risiko berat seperti pendarahan internal, penggumpalan darah, atau kematian di kasus langka. Kulit berlipat setelah penurunan berat badan besar bisa membutuhkan operasi tambahan. NHS hanya merekomendasikan operasi gastric bypass setelah cara penurunan berat badan lain gagal, mengingat risiko dan komitmen jangka panjangnya.

article_content: Dr. Ashraf Elnazir, a leading colonic specialist at Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, is facing possible removal from the medical register after being accused of defrauding wealthy widow Gabriella Adler-Jensen out of hundreds of thousands of pounds. It is alleged that Dr. Elnazir befriended Ms. Adler-Jensen after the death of her husband, Harry, who left her a £1.4 million estate. Between 2003 and 2006, Dr. Elnazir is said to have persuaded her to invest money in joint bank accounts, fund his children's education, and purchase properties, according to the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service. He is also accused of convincing Mrs. Adler-Jensen to transfer significant sums into foreign bank accounts for his own benefit. Testimony indicates that as Mrs. Adler-Jensen’s financial position declined, Dr. Elnazir’s wealth increased. Mrs. Adler-Jensen allegedly paid for Dr. Elnazir’s £5,000 holiday to Dubai in 2003, during which their relationship reportedly became intimate. He is said to have used her funds for personal expenses, including airline tickets, private club fees, dental bills, his children’s school fees, and purchases of cars. The tribunal found Dr. Elnazir’s conduct to be dishonest and likely to bring the medical profession into disrepute. The panel concluded that he misappropriated Mrs. Adler-Jensen's money for his personal benefit, violating professional standards. Dr. Elnazir denies the allegations, maintaining there was no close personal relationship and describing Mrs. Adler-Jensen as merely a business associate. The hearing was told the two became acquainted after Mrs. Adler-Jensen’s husband died in 2001, having lived in the same apartment block in Kensington, and developed a closer friendship over time that included frequent socializing. Ed Morgan, representing the General Medical Council, argued that Dr. Elnazir exploited Mrs. Adler-Jensen's trust and manipulated their relationship to serve his interests. Between 2003 and 2006, about £779,000 was transferred by Mrs. Adler-Jensen into a joint HSBC account intended for investments, of which Dr. Elnazir withdrew approximately £70,000 for personal purposes. In 2003, Dr. Elnazir allegedly persuaded Mrs. Adler-Jensen to purchase his flat for £429,000, above its valuation of £375,000, while retaining joint ownership despite substantial contributions from her. He later claimed the money was either a loan or a gift. A joint US dollar account for currency trading was also opened in 2004. Mrs. Adler-Jensen is reported to have transferred a total of $645,645, including $440,000 that was intended for buying land in Egypt, which did not occur. On one occasion, Dr. Elnazir requested $20,000, citing his brother’s supposed trouble with the Egyptian mafia. When Mrs. Adler-Jensen sought reimbursement, Dr. Elnazir allegedly referred to her as ‘the enemy’ and denied any responsibility for her financial losses. The panel described his actions as sustained, deliberate, and devoid of remorse. The tribunal is now considering whether Dr. Elnazir’s actions amount to professional misconduct and if his fitness to practice medicine is impaired. Possible outcomes include practicing under conditions, suspension, or removal from the register. Dr. Elnazir is not present at this stage of the ongoing hearing.

article_content: Petr Cech told CNN he hopes for a swift resolution to the controversy surrounding Chelsea and referee Mark Clattenburg. The Metropolitan Police ended their investigation into alleged remarks by Clattenburg toward Chelsea players John Obi Mikel and Juan Mata on Tuesday. Clattenburg has denied using inappropriate language, and the Football Association is expected to conclude its own investigation on Friday. Cech, Chelsea's goalkeeper, expressed his hope that the situation will be brought to an end soon. "For me, it's difficult to comment on something I did not see or hear, or was not involved in," Cech told CNN. "If someone brings up such serious allegations, there must be a strong case, otherwise it wastes everyone’s time and is not good for football." "If there is a case, it is not because Chelsea simply wants to act, but because there is a reason," he added. "Again, I hope this story will be finished as soon as possible." Cech also suggested that referees should explain their decisions more openly to foster better relationships with fans and players. "I believe referees should communicate better with the public. It would help," he continued. "There are many initiatives to respect referees, and increased openness would contribute to that." "Players can admit mistakes and gain respect for that, and the same can apply to referees. Their job is difficult and everyone understands that, but improved communication could help."

Kerja wasit sampun angel, tur sami prasida ngametuangangang, nanging komunikasi sane luwih becik prasida nambahan preti."

article_content: As anticipation builds for the 2023 ODI World Cup final between hosts India and Australia at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, home fans are hopeful that unbeaten India will continue their impressive run and secure a third title. However, as players know, finals come with their own pressure, regardless of previous tournament form. India has not lost a match, winning all 10 league games and the semifinal against New Zealand. Australia, after losing their first two league matches, won the next seven to qualify for the semifinals and defeated South Africa to extend their unbeaten run to eight matches. Out of the 12 ODI World Cup finals held since the tournament began in 1975, only six centuries and two five-wicket hauls have been recorded. Some notable statistics from World Cup finals history: 1. From 1975 to 1992, the first five finals were won by teams batting first: West Indies over Australia by 17 runs (1975); West Indies over England (1979); India over West Indies by 43 runs (1983) – all at Lord's; Australia over England by 7 runs at Kolkata (1987); Pakistan over England by 22 runs at Melbourne (1992). 2. Two other finals where teams batting first won were both by Australia: by 125 runs against India at Johannesburg (2003), and by 53 runs against Sri Lanka at Bridgetown (2007). 3. Finals in 1996, 1999, 2011, and 2015 were won by teams batting second. The 2019 final at Lord's was tied after both New Zealand and England scored 241 runs, and England won on boundary count after the Super Over was also tied. 4. Six centuries have been scored in World Cup finals: 149 by Adam Gilchrist (Australia) vs Sri Lanka at Bridgetown, 2007; 140* by Ricky Ponting (Australia) vs India at Johannesburg, 2003; 138* by Vivian Richards (West Indies) vs England at Lord's, 1979; 107* by Aravinda de Silva (Sri Lanka) vs Australia at Lahore, 1996; 103* by Mahela Jayawardene (Sri Lanka) vs India at Mumbai, 2011; and 102 by Clive Lloyd (West Indies) vs Australia at Lord's, 1975. 5. Mahela Jayawardene is the only player to score a century in a losing cause in a World Cup final. 6. Aravinda de Silva is the only all-rounder to score a century (107*) and take three wickets in a World Cup final. 7. Only two bowlers have taken five-wicket hauls in the finals: Joel Garner (5 for 38, West Indies vs England, 1979) and Gary Gilmour (5 for 48, Australia vs West Indies, 1975). Both matches were at Lord's. Four-wicket hauls were recorded by Shane Warne (4 for 33, Australia vs Pakistan, 1999) and Keith Boyce (4 for 50, West Indies vs Australia, 1975). 8. The most ducks in a World Cup final were recorded in 1979: eight in total (five England, three West Indies), an unwanted record. 9. The highest match aggregate in a World Cup final is 593 runs (Australia 359/2, India 234) at Johannesburg in 2003. (Stats compiled by Rajesh Kumar)

article_content: Archbishop Vincent Nichols, the highest-ranking Catholic leader in England and Wales, urged people to pray for Christians facing persecution in the Middle East, where attending church often comes with grave risks. Speaking at Westminster Cathedral on Christmas Eve, Nichols drew attention to the hardships endured by Christians in Egypt, Iraq, and Syria—countries plagued by religious violence. Nichols emphasized Christianity's origins in the Middle East and called on his congregation not to forget those who continue to practice their faith under threat. His message came alongside recent remarks by Prince Charles, who has shown support for Middle Eastern Christian communities newly arrived in Britain. Coptic Christians in Egypt, making up about 10% of the country's population, have faced increased hostility since President Mohammed Morsi’s removal. In Syria, Christians—similarly about 10%—have become more vulnerable due to the ongoing civil conflict. Nichols described Christians as 'currently the most widely persecuted religious group in the world,' focusing particularly on the Middle East. Echoing Prince Charles, he stressed the need to remember and support Christians in the region. He noted that while people in London can worship freely, others must show extraordinary bravery just to attend church. Nichols praised their courage and called their faith an inspiration. Prince Charles had also voiced worries about Christian persecution in the Middle East, saying that efforts to build bridges between Christians and Muslims are being intentionally sabotaged. He warned that such actions threaten long-standing interfaith relationships. Nichols, reflecting Pope Francis’s call for hope and tenderness, noted the importance of healing divisions and nurturing compassion. He urged the congregation to value unity and to recognize a shared humanity. Approximately 1,500 worshippers attended the Christmas midnight mass at Westminster Cathedral, the main church for England and Wales’s 5.8 million Catholics. Appointed in 2009, Nichols also serves as president of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference and has addressed past issues faced by the Church, including child abuse, advocating for accountability.

article_content: China’s Foreign Ministry has officially announced that President Hu Jintao will visit the United States early next year. The trip is viewed as a major milestone that could greatly impact bilateral relations, according to Chinese state media. Arrangements are already being made, and both countries are keeping in close contact, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Ma Zhaoxu told China Daily. President Obama also spoke about the upcoming visit last month while Premier Wen Jiabao was at the United Nations. Obama highlighted that U.S.-China cooperation is critical for global peace and that their partnership is watched worldwide due to its influence on international security. Over the past year, relations between the two countries have experienced strains, including U.S. calls for China to let the yuan appreciate and criticisms over currency policy. Military cooperation was put on hold after U.S. arms sales to Taiwan, which China considers a breakaway province. Recently, however, ties have shown improvement; China’s Defense Minister General Liang Guanglie and U.S. Defense Secretary Robert Gates met in Vietnam during a security meeting hosted by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. President Hu’s visit next year will be his first state trip to the U.S. since April 2006 during the Bush administration.

article_content: Parts of the UK experienced their coldest November night since 2010 on Wednesday, with snow and ice warnings expected to continue for the next three days. On Aonach Mor in the Scottish Highlands, temperatures dropped to a bitter -8°C (18°F). In Prestwick, Ayrshire, temperatures reached -5.5°C (22°F), and in Keswick, Cumbria, it fell to -6.1°C (21°F). Snow has fallen across Scotland and eastern England, reaching as far south as Norfolk. The cold weather is forecasted to persist for several more days. Freezing fog has made travel hazardous in the Midlands, north-west England and Northern Ireland, and could spread to other areas. Later on Wednesday, additional snow is expected in northern and eastern Scotland, as well as eastern England; there is also a chance of overnight snowfall on the moors in south-west England. In Northern Ireland, light rain and snow have dampened the ground, and together with freezing fog, have created icy conditions on roads and pavements. North Wales has experienced some sleet. These cold air masses originate from Scandinavia, which is currently experiencing near-record November cold. The Met Office has issued weather warnings for snow and ice from 17:00 GMT Wednesday across northern and eastern Scotland, north-east England and Yorkshire. Further warnings are in effect Thursday for eastern Scotland, north-east England down to North Yorkshire, and most of south-west England. Much of Northern Ireland is also under an ice warning Thursday. The snow and ice warning now extends into Friday morning for most of the UK's east coast. These yellow warnings mean hazardous conditions are likely, with potential disruption to roads and railways and icy surfaces on roads and pavements. Drivers have been urged to take extra care, and many face road closures, including the A169 in Goathland in the North York Moors and the A171 between Whitby and Pickering. In London, Mayor Sadiq Khan activated a 'severe weather emergency protocol' to protect rough sleepers as overnight temperatures are expected to dip below freezing. This protocol requires all councils to provide extra shelter for the homeless. Separately, the UK Health Security Agency issued an amber cold-health alert for health services in northern England, indicating 'significant impacts are probable' and that the whole health sector and population could be at risk. A yellow cold-health alert, less severe, is in place for the Midlands. Both alerts are effective from 18:00 GMT Tuesday until 5 December. Dr Agostinho Sousa from the agency has urged people to check on vulnerable individuals and advised the elderly and sick to keep their main living spaces warm. For local weather updates and forecasts, the BBC Weather app is available for download in the UK.

article_content: The UK government is considering significant new measures that could reduce tax credits for migrant workers by up to £100 million each week. According to Home Secretary Theresa May, the Treasury is closely examining how to limit access to these benefits, which are seen as a major incentive for migrants coming to the UK. Currently, Britain spends nearly £5 billion annually on tax credit support for migrants from both EU and non-EU countries. These payments can greatly increase the incomes of low-paid families, occasionally even tripling a minimum wage worker's earnings. However, any restrictions on access to these benefits for EU nationals could result in disputes with the European Union. Prime Minister David Cameron recently visited Rochester ahead of an important by-election against UKIP, warning that Britain could leave the EU if it fails to gain greater control over immigration. He advocated for a return to the EU’s original focus as a Common Market, rejecting further political integration like a shared European army or country. Ministers are also advocating for an 'emergency brake' to limit migration from EU nations if arrivals surpass set thresholds. Simultaneously, the Conservative Party is facing a possible revolt, with over 100 MPs threatening to oppose the European Arrest Warrant, which enables authorities abroad to request arrests in the UK. While the government has already limited out-of-work benefits for migrants, many experts believe that in-work benefits like tax credits remain a stronger attraction. According to the Migration Advisory Committee, 415,000 foreign nationals are currently receiving these credits, and groups like MigrationWatch report that these benefits can boost a single person’s weekly income from £184 to £254, and for a family, up to £543. Migrants from countries such as Romania or Bulgaria could see their income increase as much as eightfold compared to home. Theresa May reaffirmed the government’s commitment to reviewing and tightening these policies. Ahead of the upcoming by-election, Cameron asserted that it is worth making one last effort to improve Britain’s relationship with the EU.

article_content: NASA's Lucy spacecraft made its first encounter with an asteroid on Wednesday, beginning its 12-year journey to Jupiter. The probe flew past the small asteroid Dinkinesh, located about 300 million miles (480 million kilometers) away in the main asteroid belt, beyond Mars. According to NASA, it was 'a quick hello,' with Lucy passing Dinkinesh at a speed of 10,000 mph (16,000 kph). During the flyby, Lucy came within 270 miles (435 kilometers) of Dinkinesh, which is only about a half-mile (1 kilometer) wide and likely the smallest asteroid on its route. This close approach allowed mission engineers to test Lucy’s instruments in preparation for future, larger targets. Lucy’s main scientific objective is to study the Trojan asteroids near Jupiter. These unexplored asteroids are thought to be relics from the early solar system. Over the mission, Lucy is scheduled to closely observe eight Trojan asteroids, which are estimated to be between 10 to 100 times larger than Dinkinesh. The spacecraft will complete its final flybys in 2033. Launched two years ago with a budget close to $1 billion, Lucy is named after a 3.2 million-year-old early human fossil discovered in Ethiopia in the 1970s. Its next target is an asteroid named for one of the fossil’s discoverers, Donald Johanson. A NASA graphic illustrates the expected movement of Lucy and its instrument pointing platform as it tracks Dinkinesh. The spacecraft’s tracking system autonomously follows the asteroid, allowing for continuous observation. Directional arrows in the graphic indicate the positions of the Sun, Earth, Dinkinesh, and Lucy’s path. Flight controllers noted that one of Lucy’s two solar panels remains unlocked, but it is considered stable for the entire mission. This flyby is part of what NASA calls 'Asteroid Autumn.' Recently, NASA returned its first samples from an asteroid in September and launched a new mission in October to study the metal-rich asteroid Psyche. Unlike those missions, Lucy will only fly by its targets without stopping or collecting material. Data and images from the Dinkinesh encounter are expected to be transmitted to Earth over at least the next week. Before this flyby, Dinkinesh was known only as 'an unresolved smudge in the best telescopes,' remarked Hal Levison, Lucy’s lead scientist at the Southwest Research Institute.

article_content: UK Security Minister James Brokenshire has criticized the Guardian for jeopardizing national security by publishing intelligence obtained from whistleblower Edward Snowden. Speaking in Parliament, Brokenshire argued that revealing details about government surveillance techniques could help terrorists and cybercriminals evade monitoring. He warned that making these stolen NSA files public enables dangerous groups to adapt and avoid detection. Brokenshire referenced Osama bin Laden, who changed his behavior when aware of surveillance, to illustrate the consequences of exposing intelligence methods. The minister stressed that the release of such information jeopardizes ongoing operations against terrorism and organized crime. He insisted that confidential intelligence is essential for thwarting plots and protecting public safety. Conservative MP Julian Smith, who initiated the parliamentary debate, accused the Guardian of exceeding journalistic boundaries by sharing classified material with the New York Times, suggesting it put security personnel and their families at risk. The Guardian defended its actions, stating that investigative collaboration among journalists constitutes responsible reporting, not terrorism. The discussion remains divided between those viewing Snowden as a whistleblower revealing government excesses, and others seeing him as a traitor who compromised vital intelligence efforts.

article_content: Danny DeVito has revealed plans to reunite with his Matilda co-star Mara Wilson for a special concert event, where they will narrate the 1996 film together. DeVito shared with The Messenger that he and Wilson intended to perform Matilda live with the New Jersey Philharmonic Orchestra before the SAG-AFTRA strike caused a postponement. He explained, 'We had it all set, but after the strike hit, we couldn’t proceed because it would be seen as a promotion for a movie.' 'However, we’re still planning to do it. We want to watch the movie with David Newman’s score and hope to do it soon, as the strike may be ending,' DeVito added. DeVito directed the film, which is based on Roald Dahl's children's book about a six-year-old genius with telekinetic powers who is neglected by her family. The 'Matilda in Concert' event was originally set for September 9 at State Theatre New Jersey but was postponed due to the actors’ strike. A statement on the theater’s website noted, 'Everyone involved was looking forward to the performance this September, and we are disappointed to have to postpone it. We look forward to holding it at a future date once the strike is over.' Although only DeVito is listed as the event's narrator on the official site, he indicated Mara Wilson will also take part.

DeVito maosang ring The Messenger yening ia sareng Wilson prasida ngelaksanayang Matilda live sareng Orkestra Filharmonik New Jersey sane kebet kaslametang antuk perang SAG-AFTRA. Ia ngaturangang, 'Sampun prasida kasusun, nanging sawireh perang rauh, jagi wenten perasaan promosi film.' 'Nanging, prasida nyidang ngelaksanayang punika. Tiang ngajengang prasida nglaksanayang ngemargiang film puniki sareng musik David Newman, sareng ngarepang prasida prasida wenten antuk perang prasida akir,' makta DeVito. DeVito sane ngarahang film puniki, sane adhedasarang buku anak-anak olih Roald Dahl, nyaritayang anak cilik umur 6 warsa sane nglimbakang kekuatan telekinetik tur kawigunayang olih keluargane. article_content: Rio Ferdinand has addressed the racism controversy involving John Terry and his brother Anton, criticizing the former England captain and also accusing both Terry and Ashley Cole of betrayal. In his new autobiography, Ferdinand reflects on the events at Loftus Road on October 23, 2011, when Terry was accused of racially abusing Anton Ferdinand. While Terry was found not guilty in a criminal trial, a Football Association tribunal found him guilty of racially abusing Anton and imposed a four-match ban and a £220,000 fine. Ferdinand describes in his book how his relationship with Terry and Cole collapsed after the incident. Despite having played together 50 times for England and attending Cole’s stag party, Ferdinand felt let down when Cole testified in support of Terry at the trial. Ferdinand told Cole in messages that their friendship was over if he gave evidence, and later called him a 'fake' on social media. Ferdinand was subsequently found guilty by the FA of improper conduct for another social media comment. Ferdinand recounts the toll on his family, who received racist abuse and threats, including bullets sent in the post and windows being smashed at his mother’s home, leading to her hospitalization due to stress. He writes that the controversy harmed both football and race relations in Britain, blaming Terry for much of the fallout. He claims Terry could have spared everyone pain by admitting what he said immediately and apologizing, but says Terry never offered an apology to Anton or the family. Ferdinand also discusses how England manager Roy Hodgson’s handling of the situation affected his international career, leading to fewer appearances for England than he had hoped. He felt Hodgson should have asked whether he could still play with Terry, as Rio says he would have been willing to do so. Ferdinand expresses sadness over his broken friendship with Cole and disappointment that Cole chose to support Terry in court. He also criticizes Chelsea FC and the FA for their handling of the situation and points out that Chelsea's lawyers summoned Anton Ferdinand to court. Ferdinand's last contact with Cole was a text conversation before the trial, where Ferdinand warned Cole testifying would end their friendship. In court, Cole said he was a reluctant witness and a long-time friend of the Ferdinand family. The FA's judgment also criticized Chelsea secretary Dave Barnard, expressing doubts about some of his evidence. Ferdinand emphasizes that the incident was reported to police by a member of the public, not his brother, and voices frustration with delays in the FA's disciplinary process. Ferdinand officially retired from international football in May 2013, and has not spoken to either Terry or Cole since the events.

Ring buku otobiografinya sane anyar, Ferdinand ngemiten indik kejadian ring Loftus Road tanggal 23 Oktober 2011, sane indikang John Terry kaanggep nglaksanayang penghinaan rasis ring Anton Ferdinand. Ajengan pengadilan kriminal nyantosang John Terry tusing kayang luwih salah, saning asapunika Komisi Asosiasi Sepak Bola (FA) nangunangang John Terry kayang nglaksanayang penghinaan rasis ring Anton, nyidayang hukuman larangan main sekancan patang pertandingan tur denda £220,000. Nyantosangang yening kontroversi puniki ngidangang karusakan ring sepak bola tur hubungan ras ring Inggris, nyalahang Terry pinaka penyebab utama. Ia nglaksanayang ucapang yening sekadi wenten pengakuan ring maktaang ento ajak mrasidayang ngaturangang panyama dosa, mewah ring keluarga Anton tusing sampun wenten. Ferdinand ngraosang sedih ritatkala wenten hubungan dados ruruh ring Cole tur kecewa indik Cole milih nyaksiang majengang Terry ring pengadilan. Ia sareng nglaksanayang kritik ring Chelsea FC sareng FA, nyidang maktaang yening pengacara Chelsea sane ngrawat Anton Ferdinand ring pengadilan. Kontak penutup Ferdinand sareng Cole mawasta sawireh pesen teks saning ngajeng pengadilan, magantosang Ferdinand kaanggen wantah Cole nyaksiang dados pamateh pesudargan. Ring pengadilan, Cole ngidangang yng dadi saksi sané maktaangang ketudusan, sane sampun mapatruh sane prasida dados pesudargan daging wawu, tur keluarga Ferdinand. Komisi FA sareng ngamolihang kritik ring sekretaris Chelsea, Dave Barnard, ngantosangang indik kesaksianyane kurang presisi. Ferdinand nyidang maosangang yening laporan ring pihak kepolisian rauh saking masyarakat umum, nenten saking adine, tur nyarengin indik keresehan ring penundaan proses disiplin saking pihak FA. Ferdinand resmi megantung sepatu saking timnas Inggris ring Mei 2013, tur sampun tusing nyidang arubuhang saking Terry utawi Cole tiang keto indik peristiwa punika.

The Right Reverend Justin Welby, the new Archbishop of Canterbury, has expressed deep concern over reports of children in Britain going hungry. Welby stated that in some respects, certain areas of the country are faring as poorly today as they did during the 1930s. Speaking at his farewell service as Bishop of Durham, he remarked: 'Whether or not we experience another recession, economic conditions remain bleak.' He found it particularly troubling that some children lack sufficient food, believing this was a problem Britain would have overcome by now. Welby acknowledged that while the scale is not the same as during the Great Depression, traces of such hardship persist in modern Britain.

Welby, who takes up his new role on Monday, highlighted the efforts of churches in organizing food distribution centers to help those unable to feed themselves. His warning is reminiscent of previous interventions by church leaders, most notably former Bishop of Durham Dr David Jenkins, a vocal critic of Margaret Thatcher in the 1980s, who drew attention to child poverty in his diocese.

Welby’s remarks also echo comments made by former Chancellor Alistair Darling in 2008, who warned that Britain could be facing its worst economic conditions in sixty years—a comment that drew criticism from Gordon Brown’s allies. Some government ministers had expected relations with the Church of England to be less confrontational following the departure of Dr Rowan Williams and Welby’s appointment, given Welby’s business background.

Welby steps into leadership at a time when the Church faces debates on issues such as same-sex marriage and the appointment of women bishops. He has made clear his determination that the Church should make progress in appointing women bishops and that it should be outward-looking and inclusive. Acknowledging the significant divisions within the Anglican Communion, Welby emphasized the need for the Church to be a centre of peace and hope, welcoming and supportive to all.

Justin Welby will formally begin his duties after a service at St Paul’s Cathedral on Monday and will be enthroned at Canterbury on March 21.

article_content: Nearly 6.2 million students in the United States between ages 16 and 24 dropped out of high school in 2007, according to a report released Tuesday. This represents 16 percent of people in that age group. Most of the dropouts were Latino or Black, the report from the Center for Labor Market Studies at Northeastern University and the Alternative Schools Network in Chicago found. The report urges a national strategy to re-enroll former dropouts, calling for this to become a core priority in America's education agenda. It warns that, due to a lack of new federal and state funding since the 1980s, re-enrollment programs have suffered decades of disinvestment. Despite this, several cities—including Chicago, Los Angeles, Milwaukee, and Portland—have seen successful re-enrollment efforts. The most effective programs are small, enroll between 80 and 150 students, offer comprehensive after-school and summer activities, are led by experienced principals and teachers, focus on real-world learning, and are locally funded and managed. They also track measurable student outcomes, including skill gains, attendance, credit recovery, and graduation rates. One student, Jesse Williams, 22, is working toward her diploma after dropping out due to gang violence and experiences with discrimination. She credits her re-enrollment school and mentor in Chicago for helping her persist. Researchers used U.S. Census Bureau data and other official sources to analyze dropout trends nationally and in the twelve largest states. Dropout rates are particularly high among males and Black and Hispanic youth. Marc Morial, president of the National Urban League, highlighted the disproportionate impact on communities of color and advocated for equal educational opportunities. The report stresses that a high school diploma is vital for avoiding poverty and finding a good job. It notes that dropouts, especially young men, face substantial earnings losses—averaging $400,000 less over their lifetime, and up to $485,000 for males. The fiscal impact extends to society: dropouts contribute less in taxes and place a greater burden on public resources, while high school graduates add significant fiscal benefits that outweigh the cost of re-enrollment programs.

Mayoritas siswa druwung lulus punika pinaka Latino sareng iraga Ireng, manut laporan saking Center for Labor Market Studies ring Northeastern University lan Alternative Schools Network ring Chicago. Sané pinaka indik punika, sawatara kota—kayang Chicago, Los Angeles, Milwaukee, sareng Portland—sampun ngewak sukses ngajak siswa sane druwung. Signature Entertainment has acquired the UK and Irish distribution rights to 'Terrifier 3' from The Coven, continuing their role after releasing the first two films in the horror series. David Howard Thornton and Lauren LaVera are set to return as Art the Clown and Sienna in this Christmas-themed horror movie. The film is slated for North American release on October 25, 2024, with filming scheduled to begin in January 2024.

A statement from Cineverse and Bloody Disgusting notes that Art the Clown will haunt the residents of Miles County on Christmas Eve. The sequel is directed and written by Damien Leone and produced by Phil Falcone, maintaining the creative team from previous installments. 'Terrifier 3' will feature a substantially increased budget in the low-to-mid seven-figure range compared to 'Terrifier 2'.

'Terrifier 2' made a surprising impact in 2022, grossing $10.6 million in North America and $5 million internationally on a $250,000 budget. It sold out its world premiere at the UK’s FrightFest and topped the UK digital download charts, also ranking in the UK’s top 10 physical releases across platforms.

The UK deal for 'Terrifier 3' was negotiated between Signature’s Director of Acquisitions and TV, Elizabeth Williams, and The Coven’s CEO and Founder, Priscilla Ross Smith. Williams commented, “We’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Damien and The Coven for the third entry in his runaway hit franchise. 'Terrifier 3' feels like Damien at the height of his filmmaking craft, and we look forward to bringing another jaw-dropping experience to the UK in 2024.”

article_content: A Montana man, Markus Kaarma, was convicted of deliberate homicide on Wednesday for shooting and killing German exchange student Diren Dede in his garage. The case drew widespread attention as it tested 'stand your ground' laws regarding the use of deadly force in defense of life and property. Cheers erupted in the courtroom when the guilty verdict was announced. Kaarma, 30, of Missoula, shot 17-year-old Diren Dede early on April 27 after being alerted to an intruder by motion sensors. Witnesses testified that Kaarma fired four shotgun blasts at Dede, who was unarmed. Kaarma faces at least 10 years in prison, with sentencing set for February 11. His lawyers plan to appeal. Dede's parents, Gulcin and Celal Dede, embraced and showed visible emotion after the jury's decision. Kaarma's defense argued he feared for his safety after previous burglaries and didn't know if the intruder was armed. They maintained that Kaarma acted under Montana's 'stand your ground' law to protect his family. Prosecutors argued Kaarma intended to lure an intruder and harm that person; on the night of the shooting, Kaarma left his garage door partially open with a purse inside. The case generated an outcry in Germany, prompting a government investigation. At trial, neighbors testified Kaarma’s girlfriend, Janelle Pflager, said they planned to bait a burglar themselves because they felt police response was inadequate. Prosecutors stated Kaarma fired a pump-action shotgun four times, pausing between the third and fourth shots, possibly adjusting his aim before the final shot, which struck Dede in the head. Diren Dede was a student at Big Sky High School in Missoula and was set to return to Germany shortly after the incident. Over 30 U.S. states have expanded 'castle doctrine' self-defense laws allowing homeowners to defend their homes. The article references the 2012 George Zimmerman case, wherein Zimmerman was acquitted under similar self-defense laws after shooting Trayvon Martin. Hamburg prosecutor Carsten Rinio stated that Germany's investigation into the Dede case is still ongoing, pending document requests from U.S. authorities.

Kasus puniki maosangang perhatian ageng dados ngujian hukum 'stand your ground' sane ngelah indik anggen ngawatesin kekerasan dados upaya nglindungang urip lan gumi. Sorsorak cangkem kadadosang ring ruang sidang waktu surat keputusan salah punika kabukaang. Kaarma, umur 30, saking Missoula, ngamargiang nembakin Diren Dede sane umurnya 17 ring dini Rahina 27 April sawireh detektor gerak nyidayang ngelaksanayang pidabdab. Saksi nyarengin Kaarma ngidangang empat peluru saking senapan ring Dede sane tan dados ngidangang senjata. Kaarma ngidangang hukuman sekurang-kurangnya 10 warsa ring pakraman, lan setata ngantos tanggal 11 Februari prasida kaputusang. Pengacara nyane ngajeng ngelaksanayang banding。 Ortiang Diren, Gulcin lan Celal Dede, peluk-pelukan nglaksanayang rasa haru sawireh keputusan juri punika. Pembela Kaarma nyaturang rasa takut sawireh maling sadurung ring mangkin, sareng nenten nyidang makta apakah maling ngidangang senjata. Antuk hukum 'stand your ground' ring Montana, pembela nglaksanayang Kaarma ngemargiang tindakan punika prasida nindihin keluarga nyane. Jaksa nglaksanayang Kaarma makudang nylu maling lan ngalaksanayang kekerasan; ring rahina punika, garase kadadosang mebukas wenten tas ajak sajeroning punika. Kasus puniki nyenengang prabawa ageng ring Jerman, ngantosang pamarentah nglaksanayang penyelidikan. Ring sidang, tetangga nyarengin Janelle Pflager nglaksanayang rencana ngumpanin maling, sawireh merasa polisi durung becik ngewastanin kasus maling ring wilayah punika. Jaksa nyaturang Kaarma nembak senapan empat bes, ngantosang antara tembakan katiga sareng kaempat, prasida ngatur arah malih sadurung tembakan panungkas matilarangang Dede ring sirah nyane. Diren Dede siswa ring Big Sky High School ring Missoula lan prasida ajak balik ke Jerman rat ngantos kasus puniki kedados. Nenten kurang saking 30 nagara bagian ring Amerika Serikat ngelah hukum perluasan 'castle doctrine', ngajengang warga nindihin gumi nyane. Artikel nyeritaangang kasus George Zimmerman ring 2012, Zimmerman kasengguh bebas ring hukum sami sawireh nembak Trayvon Martin. Jaksa saking Hamburg, Carsten Rinio, nyarengin penyelidikan kasus Dede taksung jalan, ngantosang dokumen saking pihak Amerika Serikat.

Just a week after David Letterman announced his planned retirement from late-night television in 2015, CBS made a swift move, naming Stephen Colbert of Comedy Central's 'The Colbert Report' as his successor. Colbert, who has portrayed a satirical conservative pundit since 2005, told The New York Times' Bill Carter he would appear on CBS as himself, leaving behind his well-known comic persona.

Colbert’s appointment is a notable gain for CBS, especially given his strong following on social media. For both Colbert and his fans, however, the transition represents a significant risk. CBS faced a choice: promote Craig Ferguson—who has hosted the show following 'Late Show' for as long as Colbert has helmed his cable program—or go with an outside hire. While Ferguson will soon turn 52 and Colbert 50, age seems less important than the 'buzz' Colbert generates through his online presence.

The key question: How much of his characteristic edge can Colbert bring to CBS, especially without his Comedy Central alter ego? The experience of Bill Maher—whose edgy material fared better on HBO than on network TV—raises questions about how much Colbert might have to adapt to fit CBS's expectations and audience.

As a sharp and witty interviewer, Colbert is likely to excel out of character, perhaps even surpassing late-night hosts like Jimmy Kimmel and Jimmy Fallon in that regard. Yet, to compete, Colbert may need to produce viral segments, including musical content—a strength of his, evident in his work with Stephen Sondheim’s 'Company.' Whether he wishes to pursue that path, and whether his Comedy Central audience will follow him, remain open questions. Previous shifts between TV formats, such as Oprah’s, have shown that success doesn't always translate.

CBS stands to benefit from Colbert’s work ethic and creativity. The potential for him to develop a new show as himself brings anticipation and media attention. Still, the transition could be challenging; younger viewers and fans accustomed to Colbert’s subversive style might not be eager to tune into CBS, and many will lament the end of 'The Colbert Report.'

Adding to the changes, 'The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson' may also end with his contract, meaning viewers could lose two beloved late-night programs as a result of Letterman's departure. While John Oliver—a former 'Daily Show' correspondent—might be a future candidate, he is beginning a new show on HBO and may not be available soon.

In the end, whether viewers see this as a positive exchange will depend on the new direction of late night TV and how well Colbert adapts to his new role. There’s a strong possibility Colbert will create an excellent show as himself, but with CBS’s mainstream platform in the evolving media landscape of 2015, it remains to be seen if that will be enough.

article_content: Anne Milton, the Conservative MP for Guildford and a prominent anti-obesity advocate, drew attention on social media after tweeting about a crowded train journey. Milton described feeling 'squashed' between fellow passengers, particularly noting discomfort caused by a larger man seated beside her. She urged overweight commuters to consider losing weight so they can better fit into train seats. Milton, who served as public health minister from 2010 to 2012, has previously suggested that general practitioners should directly refer to patients as 'fat' rather than 'obese' to encourage weight loss. Her recent comments, however, spurred backlash on Twitter, with users criticizing her for lack of sensitivity and calling for greater decorum from public officials. Earlier that morning, Milton was involved in a minor collision with a van while cycling to the station. Though shaken, she was uninjured, attributing her safety to her bicycle's frame. Milton later remarked that starting a 'Twitter storm about big bottoms' was a way to cope with the incident.

Milton nglaksaninang pada rasa 'kenyen' ring tengah penumpang sane pamedalang puniki, utamanyane mara ngametuang rasa ten nyaman teken penumpang sane lianan sane magenah ageng ring sebelahne. article_content: Tensions erupted in global football after FIFA announced there was no significant corruption by Russia or Qatar in their bids to host the 2018 and 2022 World Cups. Michael Garcia, the investigator who led the review, publicly criticized FIFA’s decision, stating the conclusions were incomplete and inaccurate. Over 18 months, Garcia compiled a comprehensive report, but only a 42-page summary by FIFA's ethics committee chairman, Hans-Joachim Eckert, was released, which cleared both nations. Meanwhile, the FBI intensified its investigation into alleged corruption among senior FIFA officials. FIFA asserted that its findings did not justify reopening the bidding process and stated preparations for the tournaments would continue. Garcia countered that Eckert’s summary omitted key information and distorted the report’s findings, arguing that his original investigation was misrepresented. He declared he would appeal the decision to FIFA’s appeals committee. Although issues such as Qatar’s sponsorship of a CAF congress and conduct by certain individuals were mentioned, the report found these incidents did not compromise the overall bidding process. Russia’s bid faced limited examination due to the destruction of leased computers used during its campaign. The English Football Association faced allegations of attempting to influence votes, including hosting a gala dinner for Caribbean officials and providing favors. The FA denied any misconduct, highlighting its transparency and cooperation with investigators. Some, like Simon Johnson from England’s bid team, labeled FIFA’s report as politically motivated and said Garcia was unable to fully investigate all members, leaving doubts about the investigation’s thoroughness.

Sasampun indik punika, FBI nambah antuk penyelidikan kasuratang korupsi ring petinggi FIFA. article_content: A Royal Navy warship, HMS Argyll, seized cocaine valued at a minimum of £10 million from a yacht in the Caribbean, just 24 hours after assisting with hurricane relief efforts in Bermuda. The crew had been supporting local authorities in Bermuda following damage caused by Hurricane Gonzalo. During their operation, the crew of HMS Argyll's Lynx helicopter spotted a suspicious yacht in the Atlantic and notified the ship, which then pursued and halted the vessel. Following a successful interdiction by the Royal Navy, a search conducted by the US Coast Guard Law Enforcement Detachment, operating from HMS Argyll, uncovered 10 bales of cocaine onboard. These drugs, estimated to have a wholesale value of £10 million, were confiscated before two crew members were taken into custody. Defence Secretary Michael Fallon commented, 'This is another clear demonstration of the flexibility and versatility of the Royal Navy. HMS Argyll and her crew are playing a vital role in disrupting the drugs trade that harms the UK. The British public should be proud of their work.' This bust marks HMS Argyll's second major seizure in two months, after confiscating £21 million worth of cocaine in August. The Type 23 frigate, based in Plymouth, Devon, is part of a 15-nation partnership aimed at preventing criminal organizations from moving illegal drugs from South America to the western world. HMS Argyll's Commanding Officer, Commander Paul Hammond, stated: 'I am extremely proud of my ship's company; they made significant efforts to aid Bermuda after Hurricane Gonzalo, and immediately carried out a smooth interception of a drug smuggling vessel, showing dedication and professionalism.' Able Seaman Specialist Alex 'JR' Hartley added: 'Life onboard is hectic at the moment. After helping locals recover from Hurricane Gonzalo, I was involved the next day in intercepting a yacht carrying drugs. This deployment has certainly been challenging but also very rewarding.'

Krune sampun ngebantu pamarentah lokal ring Bermuda sida ngeredang karusakan timpal Hurricane Gonzalo. Krune helikopter Lynx saking HMS Argyll ngelaksanayang nyidang prahu layar ngelah indik mencurigakan ring Samudra Atlantik lalu ngaturang indik kapal, sane prasida ngudang prahu punika lan nyaga pinaka wenten. article_content: Mychal Bell, a Black teenager and the last member of the 'Jena 6' still in custody, was released on Thursday after a juvenile court judge set his bail at $45,000. Bell's release followed LaSalle Parish District Attorney Reed Walters' decision not to appeal a higher court's ruling moving the case to juvenile court. Dressed in a blue striped shirt and jeans, Bell exited the LaSalle Parish courthouse a week after over 15,000 demonstrators marched through Jena, Louisiana, to protest the local authorities' handling of the 'Jena 6' case. Protesters argued the Black teens were treated more harshly than three white students who hung nooses from a tree at Jena High School. While the white students were suspended, they did not face criminal charges, which many felt should have been filed as hate crimes. Outside the courthouse, the Rev. Al Sharpton said, "We do not condone violence of any kind, but we ask that people be given a fair and even chance at the bar of justice." He continued, "We are fighting for one level of justice for everybody. You cannot have adult attempted murder charges for some, and a fine for others, and call that equal protection under the law." District Attorney Walters stated his choice not to appeal was for the best interest of the victim, Justin Barker, and his family. He insisted the recent march, led by Sharpton and Martin Luther King III, did not influence his decision. Bell, now 17, had previously been the only member of the Jena 6 still in jail, with an earlier bond set at $90,000. His previous conviction for conspiracy to commit second-degree battery was overturned as the case was deemed to belong in juvenile court. Originally, all six Black students were charged with second-degree attempted murder and conspiracy, but charges were later reduced against at least four, including Bell. Bryant Purvis still awaits arraignment, while charges for Jesse Ray Beard, who was 14 at the time, remain undisclosed due to his age. Following numerous threats after widespread national attention, Louisiana Governor Kathleen Blanco announced state police would protect the Jena 6 families and investigate any threats. The FBI also confirmed it was aware of and investigating these allegations. Racial tensions in Jena intensified following the noose incident and subsequent student altercations. District Attorney Walters has said there was no direct link between the noose-hanging and the attack on Barker, and Governor Blanco has publicly supported Walters’ record. Walters highlighted the stress on the community and credited community prayers with guiding Jena through the ordeal, suggesting last week's peaceful march was due to divine intervention. In contrast, Reverend Donald Sidley criticized Walters’ religious framing, urging that faith should serve to unite the community.

Saking ngajengnyane, 'Jena 6' kasalahang ring pidana percobaan pembunuhan tingkat dua miwah persekongkolan, ring sekancan kasubang pidana sane prasida Bell. Jaksa Walters ngaturang tan wenten langsung hubungan antara kasus gantungan miwah kasus kekerasan ring Barker, miwah Gubernur Blanco nyantosang Walters ring hasil gawenya. Pastor Donald Sidley malu ring komentar Walters, ngajin agama dados penyatu ring masyarakat.

article_content: Nestlé has announced plans to close its infant formula factory in Askeaton, Ireland, citing a significant decline in China’s birth rate as a major reason. The company, the world's largest in food and beverages, stated on Wednesday it plans to shut the facility by the first quarter of 2026 unless a buyer can be found. Demand for infant formula in China has decreased substantially, as the number of newborns dropped from about 18 million in 2016 to fewer than 9 million projected in 2023. The market is also seeing rapid growth in locally-produced infant formula, reducing dependence on imports. The Askeaton facility produces infant formula exclusively for export to Asian markets. Nestlé’s proposal includes closing the plant’s research and development center by 2025, with the work shifting to its operations in China and Switzerland. China’s fertility rate has declined over several decades, hitting a record low of 1.09 babies per woman in 2022, according to the country's Population and Development Research Center. This decline is partly due to population control policies, like the one-child policy. In response to workforce shortages, China has ended the one-child limit and introduced financial incentives for families to have more children, according to the China-Britain Business Council. Despite these measures, the US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies reports that China’s demographic shift may slow its economic growth and global competitiveness over the next 20 to 30 years. Nestlé’s planned closure may impact around 542 employees. The company will begin a consultation process with affected staff and is open to offers from credible buyers during this time.

Perusahaan sane pinaka ageng ring bidang pangan lan minuman puniki nglaksanayang indik pabrik puniki prasida ditutup ring kwartal kapertama 2026 kecuali wenten sane prasida meli. Permintaan susu formula ring Tiongkok sampun turun, antuk jumlah kelahiran anyar ngejog saking kira-kira 18 juta ring 2016 dados ngidang 9 juta ring 2023. Pasar taler ngalaksanayang pertumbuhan pesat ring produk lokal sane nyirangang impor. Pabrik ring Askeaton ngahasilang susu formula taler khusus ngantosang ekspor ke pasar Asia. Rencana Nestlé punika ngedengin pusat riset lan pengembangan manten prasida tutup ring 2025, sareng kerjanya kasurung ke fasilitas ring Tiongkok lan Swiss. Tingkat fertilitas ring Tiongkok sampun turun dekadeg, prasida nyantos angka 1.09 anak per istri ring 2022, ngantosang Pusat Studi Populasi lan Pengembangan Tiongkok. Penurunan puniki kabuat olih kebijakan pengendalian populasi, seperti one-child policy. Nenten lali, pemerintah Tiongkok prasida ngosain kebijakan one-child lan ngemehang insentif rupiah ring keluarga sane ngemetuang anak kaping kalih utawi ketiga, ngantosang China-Britain Business Council. Senajana wenten upaya punika, Center for Strategic and International Studies saking Amerika ngedengin yening pergeseran demografis ring Tiongkok prasida nglambatin pertumbuhan ekonomi lan daya saing global warse ring ajeng. Rencana penutupan Nestlé puniki nyangra pengaruh ring kirang langkung 542 karyawan. Perusahaan prasida ngamolihang konsultasi ring para pegawai lan tetap nampi penawaran saking pembeli ring mangkin.

article_content: A recent report reveals that no UK city or town currently achieves 'superfast' broadband speeds, defined as 24Mbps or higher. Data from uSwitch indicates that Telford has the fastest average download speed in the UK at 22.99Mbps, despite major networks like Virgin, BT, and Sky advertising contracts with speeds over 50Mbps. According to Akamai's latest State of the Internet Report, the average broadband speed for UK users is just 8.4Mbps, placing the UK ninth globally. The report, which compared web speeds in 129 countries, found South Korea leads with an average speed of 13.3Mbps. The UK shares 10th place with Sweden, as both average 8.4Mbps, but the UK follows Sweden alphabetically. UK internet speeds rose by 48% over the past year, the highest increase globally. However, more than a quarter of UK postcodes still cannot access speeds above 3Mbps, meaning downloading a HD film could take up to six hours. Among the UK's largest towns and cities, Telford tops the list with 22.99Mbps, while Hull averages 10.49Mbps. London ranks 26th, with an average of 17Mbps, and nearly 20% of its users receive speeds below 3Mbps. The uSwitch study confirms that no UK city or town meets the 24Mbps threshold for superfast broadband. Urban areas do see faster speeds than rural ones, but many places, like Hull and Norwich, remain behind. While Leeds enjoyed an 87% increase in speed, Hull’s speeds rose only 26%, and Norwich's 75% increase still leaves over a third of its users below 3Mbps. Internationally, South Korea maintained the fastest average speed at 13.3Mbps, although this was a 6.4% drop from last year. In the United States, the District of Columbia was top with 11.4Mbps, followed by Connecticut at 10Mbps. US speeds are more consistent across states, but some states like Vermont dropped out of the top 10 due to declining speeds. Akamai, a cloud services company, compiles its State of the Internet report by analyzing global internet speeds, security, and mobile usage in 129 countries. Based on survey data, average mobile network speeds worldwide range from 9.7Mbps to as low as 0.5Mbps. Globally, mobile data traffic has doubled over the past year. Marie-Louise Abretti, a telecoms expert at uSwitch.com, points out that even in urban areas, UK broadband speeds remain below superfast standards. She emphasizes that while the government's goal—95% superfast broadband coverage by 2017—is positive, actual uptake depends on affordability and public awareness. The government, through Broadband Delivery UK, has allocated £530 million to improve broadband infrastructure.

article_content: Gone are the days of searching for spare change at the coffee shop – a new gadget is making payments easier than ever in the UK. The latest innovation, called Watch2pay, is a watch with built-in payment technology that lets users pay for small purchases simply by tapping it on a payment terminal. Developed by the watchmaker LAKS in collaboration with MasterCard, Watch2pay acts like a prepaid card: you load it with funds online, then use it for transactions up to £15 in value. Available in eight different colors and priced at £99, this device can be used in around 70,000 shops across the country – including popular spots like Pret A Manger, Subway, McDonald’s, and various independent retailers. Since it isn’t directly linked to your main bank account, you can only spend the amount you’ve already put on the watch. If it’s lost or stolen, your account can be swiftly cancelled via phone or the internet. The watch offers another alternative to current contactless payments via mobile phones, such as the recently introduced Quick Tap system. Advocates say it’s more convenient than a smartphone because it’s always accessible on your wrist, not hidden away. It could also help people manage their spending, especially for kids’ pocket money, since there are no overdraft capabilities. Experts predict that contactless technology may soon make cash obsolete as more people opt for digital payments. PayPal’s UK managing director, Carl Scheible, suggests that by 2016 mobile phones could function as digital wallets, making traditional wallets unnecessary. However, many consumers are still attached to cash and checks; public resistance recently led banks and retailers to drop plans to phase out checks by 2018.

Jam puniki kaanggen olih LAKS sareng MasterCard dados prepaid: ngametuangang nyisi duite ring online, dados kaanggen pembayaran maksimum £15. Wantah wenten ring 8 warna, maharga £99, genggeman puniki dados kaanggen ring 70,000 toko ring Inggris, prasida ring Pret A Manger, Subway, McDonald’s, miwah toko mandiri sane lenan. Nyerahen jam lenyap utawi kasuri, akun prasida kabatalang ring telpon utawi website. article_content: On Thursday, Jeff Kyle, the brother of slain Navy SEAL Chris Kyle, stated that although he wished Eddie Ray Routh, his brother's killer, had received the death penalty, he was relieved that the trial was over and Routh was found guilty. Appearing on Fox & Friends after the verdict, Jeff Kyle explained that seeking the death penalty would have prolonged the trial and increased the family's distress. Prosecutors did not pursue the death penalty for Routh, who has now been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for the 2013 murders of Chris Kyle and Chad Littlefield at a Texas shooting range. Jeff Kyle described the nine-day trial as 'grueling' for his family but said they were grateful for the support received from people around the world. He expressed frustration with Routh's defense, which claimed mental illness and PTSD. Jeff Kyle stated that he believed Routh was not genuinely mentally ill but was instead affected by substance abuse. The jury in Stephenville, Texas, reached a verdict after just over two hours of deliberation, rejecting the defense's arguments and finding Routh guilty. Jurors explained they believed Routh understood the consequences of his actions when he shot Kyle and Littlefield. Family and friends had testified that Routh changed after overseas service and struggled with marijuana and alcohol use, as well as episodes of paranoia. However, the prosecution argued, with expert testimony, that Routh was not mentally ill and had been under the influence of drugs at the time of the crimes. Chris Kyle's widow, Taya Kyle, who testified during the trial, thanked the jury after the verdict and paid tribute to her husband in a social media post, describing him as 'the love of my life' and expressing hope that people would continue to honor his legacy.

article_content: Washington D.C. Attorney General Brian Schwalb filed a lawsuit alleging that 14 of the city’s largest landlords conspired with a property management software company to artificially increase rental prices across Washington D.C. According to a November 1st Ars Technica report, the civil complaint claims the landlords collaborated with RealPage, a Texas-based provider of rental pricing software, to set rents above fair market value. The alleged scheme reportedly affected over 30% of D.C. apartment buildings with five or more units, and 60% of buildings with 50 or more units. Schwalb contends that RealPage and the defendant landlords engaged in a centralized, anticompetitive plan that caused residents to pay millions of dollars above fair market prices. The lawsuit focuses on RealPage’s YieldStar rent optimization software, which uses algorithms to recommend rental prices based on market data. Schwalb alleges that by inputting data into YieldStar and largely following its pricing guidance, Washington D.C.’s largest landlords effectively formed a 'cartel' that distorted the housing market. According to the lawsuit, a former high-level Greystar Management Services employee admitted landlords used the software specifically to raise rents in a coordinated manner. Internal documents cited in the suit show landlords were expected to closely follow RealPage’s pricing recommendations in most cases. This is the latest legal action challenging RealPage’s pricing practices, which have come under increasing scrutiny. The U.S. Department of Justice opened an antitrust investigation into RealPage last year, following a ProPublica investigation that found YieldStar discourages negotiation and favors high occupancy over lower rents. RealPage has maintained that it complies with antitrust laws and that its software offers a more data-driven approach to pricing than traditional manual methods. The company did not respond to a request for comment on the D.C. lawsuit. Major real estate companies named as defendants include Greystar, Bozzuto Management Company, and Equity Residential, which collectively own and manage tens of thousands of units in D.C. Schwalb claims their coordination raised rents by 'hundreds of dollars per month' in a city experiencing a significant housing affordability crisis. Washington D.C. had the highest median rent of any major U.S. city last year, averaging over $2,100, according to census data. Schwalb’s complaint estimates that the alleged collusion generated over $200 million in excess rental income, depriving tenants of fair market prices. The lawsuit alleges violations of D.C.’s antitrust laws and, if successful, could seek civil penalties and restitution for tenants harmed by inflated rents. It follows a similar price-fixing class action suit filed against RealPage and major landlords in California last year.

Manut laporan Ars Technica 1 November, gugatan puniki maosang pengelola punika sareng RealPage asal Texas, ngatur harga sewa satondenangang harga pasar sane adil. Gugatan puniki ngemantenangang pelanggaran hukum antimonopoli ring D.C., indik sukses prasida ngawitang sanksi perdata tur pengembalian dana ring penyewa sane dados korban harga sewa luwih tinggi. article_content: Softbank, a Tokyo-based company, has revealed Pepper, a humanoid robot designed to detect and respond to human emotions. Showcased at a launch event, Pepper interacted through gestures and sounds, even sharing a playful moment with Softbank CEO Masayoshi Son. Using an 'emotional engine' and cloud AI, Pepper interprets body language, speech, and facial expressions. The robot stands at 121 cm tall, weighs 28 kg, and includes expressive eyes, a chest-mounted touchscreen, and articulated arms, though it lacks legs. Pepper can dance, sing, tell jokes, and reacts to touch. Pepper is scheduled for sale in Japan at 198,000 yen (about £1,130 or $1,900). The robot was co-developed with Aldebaran Robotics of France, and its CEO, Bruno Maisonnier, attended the unveiling. Japan's affection for companion robots fits within its 'kawaii' culture, although previous efforts, like Sony's Aibo and Honda's Asimo, have not achieved mainstream commercial success—Aibo was discontinued, while Asimo remains too expensive for homes. Companies such as Hitachi, Toyota, and others have also pursued companion robots with mixed results. Robots in Japan are often intended as friendly companions more than utilitarian aids, but with an aging population, their use for elderly care and reducing social isolation is likely to grow. Already, some robots help monitor and support seniors. There are doubts among experts about whether robots can truly possess emotions. Giulio Tononi, from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, contends that machines lack the capacity for consciousness because they cannot integrate complex information as humans do. Technologically, Pepper features more than twelve sensors, including multiple touch sensors in its hands and head, laser and bumper sensors at its base, two cameras, four microphones, and both Wi-Fi and Ethernet connectivity. Maisonnier envisions robots enhancing life as supportive, emotionally aware companions. Aldebaran’s earlier Nao robot is mainly used for education and research, but Pepper aims to offer companionship in daily life.

Robot puniki binangun sareng Aldebaran Robotics saking Perancis, nenten wenten CEO-nya, Bruno Maisonnier, dados kaanggen ring peluncuran.
