article_content: James Herard, a 25-year-old South Floridian, faces sentencing after his conviction on 18 felony charges related to a series of armed robberies in 2008, including two murders. During court, despite his conviction, Herard challenged the judge to sentence him to death, holding firm to his claim of innocence. He boldly declared he dared the judge to issue the death penalty, saying he was certain the Supreme Court would not allow him to be executed for a crime he did not commit. Prosecutors accuse Herard and four associates, believed to be part of the 'Bacc Street Crips,' of robbing a Dunkin' Donuts in Tamarac during which Kiem Huynh, age 56, was fatally shot. Another man, Tharod Bell, is said to have shot a second victim, Eric Jean-Pierre, with Herard allegedly inciting the act. Evidence presented included a recorded confession from Herard in 2008, in which he admitted his influence in the fatal shooting, though he has since stated his confession was forced. At sentencing, the defense highlighted Herard’s positive influence in prison, offering testimony from inmates like Angelo Coicou, who said Herard helped him communicate with his family and learn to read. Court evidence and surveillance footage show Herard’s group carried out several armed robberies using shotguns. Authorities cite Herard's key role in these crimes as part of the Bacc Street Crips. Herard’s trial has been marked by erratic behavior, including an incident where he barked at a judge. Herard is already serving several life sentences for unrelated violent crimes in Palm Beach County, where his actions left two men with serious injuries.

Jeroning pengadilan, Herard ngidangang juri ngemarginang hukuman mati, sareng ngaku nenten salah. Bukti sane kaatur ring pengadilan ngelanturang pengakuan sane kawentenang ring 2008, Herard nyarengin pengaruhe ring kedadian punika, nanging ipun ngaku pengakuan punika kadadosang ring paksa. Ring hukuman, tim pengacara Herard ngemargiang saksi napi sane nyaksian Herard dados pisan sayan di sel tahanan, prasida mabantu napi lianan ngubungin keluargane sareng ngajahang maca. article_content: Carrying out maintenance work in Gaza now comes with extreme risk to the lives of technicians. Ahmad*, a PalTel electrician, was called by the Network Operation Centre just after 10 pm during the third week of Israel's offensive on Gaza. The main data centre in Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City had lost power, jeopardizing all communications in the area. Ahmad traveled through the city under intense aerial bombardment, choosing to ride in an ambulance for some added safety. He told the ambulance driver that failure to restore the generator would disrupt critical communications, including for emergency services. 'We are as vital as medical staff—a phone call can save lives,' Ahmad explained. He succeeded in repairing the generator by 2 am, keeping the telecom network operational, and stayed on-site until dawn before returning home during a lull in bombing. 'Thank God my family is safe and I survived another day. This is my job—I do it every day,' Ahmad reflected. Ahmad’s story is typical among the 750 PalTel staff in Gaza, who risk their safety to keep networks running amid war, displacement, and loss. The toll has been high: at least five staff members have been killed by Israeli attacks, while many have lost loved ones. One technician, Samir*, died alongside his brother in an air raid only 15 minutes after returning home from a fuel delivery between data towers. The loss of telecom services would severely hinder rescue operations and documenting events, humanitarian workers and journalists note. Since October 7, more than 13,000 Palestinians have died in Israeli attacks on Gaza. Videos have shown citizens and civil defense searching through rubble to rescue people, drawing international attention. Israel cut off Gaza's electricity on October 7, but PalTel’s network functioned for almost six weeks due to extensive contingency planning. CEO Abdul Majeed Melhem explained that PalTel has prepared infrastructure for emergencies over 15 years, including deep-buried cables (up to 8 meters underground) and redundant power sources. Every piece of PalTel equipment entering Gaza must be approved by Israeli authorities, complicating repairs. Staff can be directed remotely from the West Bank, and Gazan workers have autonomy if communications are severed. Despite preparations, continuing bombardment has disabled about 70% of the mobile network. Solar panels have been destroyed or rendered ineffective by debris. Staff work under constant danger, from home to the field. Technicians like Rabih* must provide detailed ID details to Israelis before repairs near the border, facing risks from drones and shelling. 'A mistake could be deadly,' Rabih says, noting that volunteering for such dangerous work is driven by a sense of duty, not obligation. West Bank staff like Mohammed* hesitate to ask Gaza colleagues to risk their lives for repairs. Workers volunteer despite danger, and phone calls about repairs are stressful for both sides. 'I can't imagine their courage; I don't know if I could do it,' Mohammed admits. Ultimately, Gaza's network depends on Israel, which controls cables connecting Gaza to the outside world and has at times cut off services. Fuel supplies are also restricted—recently, Israel allowed 120,000 liters for hospitals and bakeries, and 20,000 liters every two days for PalTel's generators. PalTel warned of a total telecom blackout when fuel was exhausted, but the limited deliveries are only enough to support part of the network. The company remains dependent on Israel for future connectivity and fuel. As CEO Melhem stressed: 'No ambulances, emergency services, civil defense, or humanitarian organizations can operate without telecommunications.' * Names changed for safety.
translated_content: Nglaksanayang kerja pemeliharaan ring Gaza tusing gampang, tur nglantarang resiko sane ageng ring nyawa teknisi. Ahmad*, teknisi PalTel, kasuratang olih Network Operation Centre sawirèh jam 10 magiang ring minggu ketiga serangan Israel ring Gaza. Data centre utama ring wengid Sheikh Radwan, Kota Gaza, sampun tusing listrik, ngancam ngalanturang komunikasi ring wewidangan punika. Ahmad nyantosang ring kota ring tengah serangan udara sane geting, milih numpak ambulans ring perjalanannya. Ia wentenang ring supir ambulans yening indik generator tusing dados nyala, komunikasi krusial, pelindungan darurat ten wenten. 'Tyane sami penting sareng tenaga medis—talipun prasida nyelamatang nyawa,' makta Ahmad. Ia prasida ngedengin generator ring jam 2 dini hari, jaringan telekomunikasi prasida makarya terus, tur ngantosang ring kantor ngantos suba, mantuk ring jerone waktu sepi bom. 'Suksma, keluarga titiang selamet, tur titiang prasida idup ngeranjing rahina anyar. Puniki tugas titiang; titiang lakonin saban rahina,' makta Ahmad. Cerita Ahmad puniki dados agem ring 750 karyawan PalTel ring Gaza, nglaksanayang pengorbanan ring nyawa nglaksanayang jaringan ngidang makarya ring tengah perang, pengungsian, tur kelangan. Kosto sane ageng: sekancan lima karyawan sampun ngajalang nyawa indik serangan Israel, tur wenten sane kelangan keluarga. Teknisi Samir* sareng adine sedasa manten taler nyidang ngajalang nyawa, rauh hancur ring serangan udara sawirèh 15 menit prasida mantuk saking ngirim bahan bakar ring data tower. Tan wenten jaringan telekomunikasi, operasi penyelamatan sareng dokumentasi prasida kesulitan, menurut humanitarian sareng wartawan. Ring 7 Oktober, sampun langkung 13.000 warga Palestina sedasa indik serangan Israel ring Gaza. Video nunasang warga sareng pertahanan sipil ngamargiang nggihang ring reruntuhan ngabantuang sane kejebak, ngidangang perhatian ring donia. Israel ngeresuming listrik ring Gaza ring 7 Oktober. Nanging jaringan PalTel prasida makarya genep minggu malih indik persiapan ring perencanaan krusial. CEO Abdul Majeed Melhem ngaturangang infrastruktur ring 15 warsa wenten, sareng kabel sane keb buried ngantos 8 meter sareng sumber tenaga cadangan. Sabe kalaksanayang alat ring Gaza dados ngidangang persetujuan pihak Israel, sane makta perbaikan jadi susah. Staff prasida matemuang instruksi ring West Bank, tur ring Gaza prasida ngalaksanayang mandiri indik komunikasi maputus. Sapunika, sekancan usaha persiapan, serangan sane ngidang nyidang 70% jaringan mobile. Solar panel kadadosang tusing malihang, rusak utawi kaselimur debu. Karyawan prasida ngalaksanayang mantenan ring tengah ancaman. Teknisi Rabih* harus ngedaut detail ring perbaikan ring kawasan dekat garis batas, kerjane ring tengah suara drone tur bombardiran. 'Kesalahan nyidang dadi bencana,' makta Rabih, ngawilang tugas sane prasida kaanggen rasa tanggung jawab, tusing keharusan. Karyawan ring West Bank, sakadi Mohammed*, prasida ragu nelpon semeton ring Gaza ngalaksanayang perbaikan sebab resikon tusing ageng ring nyawa. Karyawan ring Gaza prasida sukarela ngajakan sane nglaksanayang, sareng telepon punika dados memenekangang. 'Beli ten nyidang membayangang keberanianene, beli ten apang prasida lakonin,' makta Mohammed. Antuk punika, jaringan Gaza gumantung ring Israel, sane ngontrol kabel internasional nyambungang Gaza ring donia, tur wenten waktu nyidang nyarengin komunikasi. Bahan bakar ring Gaza wenten batas—Israel ngalelaang 120.000 liter ring rumah sakit sareng bakery, sareng 20.000 liter ring generator PalTel saben dua rahina. PalTel kalaksanayang pengumuman bakal mati jaringan total indik bahan bakar abis, nanging pasokan sane wenten prasida laksanayang sebagian jaringan. Perusahaan prasida gumantung ring Israel ring sambungan sareng bahan bakar ring warsa kedepan. CEO Melhem ngaturangang: 'Tan wenten ambulans, layanan darurat, pertahanan sipil, utawi organisasi kemanusiaan prasida makarya tan wenten telekomunikasi.' * Dados nagih ngubah nama indik kaselamatan.

article_content: Keith MacDonald, 28, known for fathering several children with different women, avoided a prison sentence after assaulting his ex-partner, Clare Bryant, and their young daughter Paige, aged three, during an argument over sunglasses. The court heard that MacDonald kicked and punched 24-year-old Ms. Bryant and struck their daughter's head with a fridge door. MacDonald attempted to evade photographers as he left Sunderland Magistrates Court after receiving his sentence. Magistrates decided against immediate imprisonment after learning MacDonald claimed he wanted to change his life and needed their support. Outside the court, MacDonald insisted on his innocence, saying he pleaded guilty only to avoid imprisonment. MacDonald reportedly has children with multiple women, first becoming a father at age 15, and says he has slept with more than 40 women. The incident occurred at Ms. Bryant's home in Houghton-le-Spring in June. MacDonald allegedly kicked Ms. Bryant in the face and punched her, then opened a fridge door that hit Paige on the back of the head. Paige suffered a sore head, and Ms. Bryant sustained a graze and cut lip. MacDonald's lawyer, Gavin Sword, stated that MacDonald wanted to change and was working to address his behavior. MacDonald pleaded guilty to assault and was sentenced to 20 weeks in jail, suspended for two years. He was also ordered to attend a ‘building better relationships’ program, complete unpaid work, and pay £100 compensation. He is also banned from contacting Ms. Bryant and Paige directly. The court heard MacDonald currently lives on income support and pays modest child support. Clare Bryant said she was angry about the sentence and concerned for her children's safety, criticizing the court's decision as inadequate. MacDonald claimed he no longer planned to have more children and maintained he had eight children, not eleven.

article_content: Indian equity indices rose on Thursday, rebounding alongside global stocks after the US Federal Reserve adopted a less hawkish monetary stance than expected. After two consecutive losses, the NSE Nifty 50 index closed 0.76% higher at 19,133 and the S&P BSE Sensex advanced 0.77% to 64,081. Technical analysts observed market indecision. Kunal Shah of LKP Securities noted that Nifty formed a Doji candle on the daily chart, signaling a balance of bulls and bears. The 19,000-18,900 range is seen as support, while resistance is at 19,200. Breaking above this resistance could trigger short covering, potentially pushing Nifty to 19,300-19,350. Nagaraj Shetti of HDFC Securities stated that Nifty's short-term uptrend remains intact, and the index may approach 19,200-19,300 in the coming sessions before consolidating. Immediate support lies at 19,050-19,000. US stock markets rallied on hopes that the Federal Reserve's rate hikes have ended, aided by strong corporate earnings. The Fed left rates unchanged, and Chair Jerome Powell cited the economic impact of rising bond yields. This led to US Treasury yields hitting nearly three-week lows. At 9:38 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones increased by 0.92%, the S&P 500 by 1.22%, and the Nasdaq by 1.32%. European equities climbed as well, spurred by rate-sensitive real estate and technology stocks, after the Fed kept rates steady. The STOXX 600 index jumped 1.6%, reaching a two-week high. The MACD indicator showed bullish signals for Vodafone Idea, NLC India, Oberoi Realty, Indian Oil Corporation, Vedanta, and Global Health. Meanwhile, IndusInd Bank, Abbott India, Star Health, Home First Finance, Prestige Estate, and Bajaj Auto showed bearish trends. Most active stocks on the NSE by value were HDFC Bank, RIL, ICICI Bank, Tata Steel, IndusInd Bank, Bajaj Finance, and SBI; by volume, Tata Steel, HDFC Bank, Power Grid, ONGC, SBI, Tata Motors, and ICICI Bank led the session. Stocks such as Vodafone Idea, REC, Power Finance Corporation, Macrotech Developers, Sonata Software, Oberoi Realty, and Global Health reached new 52-week highs, indicating strong buying. In contrast, Sumitomo Chemical, Aegis Logistics, Petronet LNG, Atul, Polyplex Corp, and IGL hit 52-week lows, showing selling pressure. Market breadth was positive, with 2,269 stocks advancing and 1,387 declining. In other news, Indian telcos accused global tech firms of bypassing regulations for business messaging, the government asked Apple to join an investigation into alleged iPhone hacking, and DGCA informed the Delhi High Court that Go First's lessors may reclaim planes and engines, affecting the airline's future.

article_content: THE HAGUE: Geert Wilders, leader of the anti-Islam Party for Freedom, achieved a major victory in the Dutch parliamentary elections, according to nearly complete vote counts released early Thursday. This represents a significant shift to the right for a country long known for its tradition of tolerance. The election outcome is expected to have widespread implications across Europe, where support for far-right politics is growing. Wilders' Party for Freedom is projected to win 37 seats in the 150-seat lower house, two more than exit polls suggested after Wednesday's voting, and more than double the 17 seats the party won in the last election. 'I had to pinch myself,' Wilders remarked, expressing his surprise at the outcome. Political parties were scheduled to meet Thursday to discuss the election results, ahead of what is anticipated to be a difficult coalition-building process starting on Friday. Despite his previously harsh rhetoric, Wilders has already reached out to other right and center parties, saying in his victory speech that any policies his party pursues will remain 'within the law and constitution.' Wilders' election platform included proposals for a referendum on leaving the European Union, a complete halt to accepting asylum-seekers, pushbacks at Dutch borders, and policies aimed at limiting the influence of Islam in the country. He stated his intention to have no mosques or Islamic schools, though his tone regarding Islam was milder this campaign than in the past. Wilders' success appears motivated primarily by calls to limit migration—an issue that caused the last coalition government to collapse in July—as well as promises to address the cost-of-living crisis and housing shortages. Voter Norbert van Beelen in The Hague said, 'I think, to be honest, very many people are focused on one particular problem, which is immigration. So I think that's what people voted for. Immigration and other aspects, such as leaving the European Union, are less prominent.' In his victory speech, Wilders said he wants to end what he called an 'asylum tsunami' and declared, 'The Dutch will be No. 1 again. The people must get their nation back.' However, before he can become prime minister, Wilders needs to form a coalition—a challenging task as many mainstream parties have been hesitant to work with him, despite his strengthened negotiating position. Pieter Omtzigt, leader of the New Social Contract party, which won 20 seats, indicated openness to discussions. The Labor Party-Green Left alliance, led by Frans Timmermans and expected to win 25 seats, ruled out joining a coalition with Wilders. 'We will never form a coalition with parties that pretend that asylum seekers are the source of all misery,' Timmermans said, promising to defend Dutch democracy. This historic election result follows the success of Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni and the rise of other right-wing leaders in Europe, such as Viktor Orban of Hungary, who quickly congratulated Wilders. Wilders, known for his strong criticisms of Islam, the EU, and migration, softened his tone in the final weeks of his campaign and pledged to be a prime minister for all Dutch citizens, earning the nickname 'Geert Milders.' The election was triggered when the previous coalition, led by outgoing Prime Minister Mark Rutte, resigned in July after failing to reach agreement on migration policy. Another significant candidate, Dilan Yeşilgoz-Zegerius—an immigrant from Turkey—could have become the Netherlands' first female prime minister if her party, the VVD, had won the most votes; instead, it is projected to finish with 24 seats, a loss of 10. The result is part of a trend of elections transforming the political landscape across Europe. Populist and right-wing parties have succeeded in some EU countries and faced challenges in others. In The Hague, voter Barbara Belder called Wilders' victory 'a very clear sign that the Netherlands wants something different.'

article_content: Uruguay celebrated a crucial 2-1 win over England in their World Cup Group D clash, thanks to two goals from Luis Suarez. Oscar Tabarez, Uruguay's coach, highlighted Edinson Cavani's relentless defensive efforts, which he believes were key in disrupting England captain Steven Gerrard's usual playmaking influence. Although England posed a significant threat with a strong midfield and multiple attacking options, Cavani neutralized Gerrard, limiting England's usual rhythm, according to Tabarez. He praised the squad's teamwork and called the win a testament to their resilience, especially after their initial 3-1 loss to Costa Rica. The victory ended Uruguay's 15-game drought against European teams, but Tabarez emphasized that qualification for the tournament's next round was not yet secured. Tabarez expressed immense pride in Suarez, who returned from recent surgery to dominate with two crucial goals. He credited the medical staff and Suarez's determination, noting how the striker’s presence inspires the entire team. The coach also thanked Suarez's family for their support throughout his recovery. While Uruguay celebrated the end of their winless streak against European sides, Tabarez reminded his team of the challenges ahead in the World Cup journey.

article_content: Google has introduced new features for Search and Lens, designed to help users solve challenging math, physics, and geometry problems. According to a blog post published Monday, users can now type an equation into the search bar or take a photo of their homework with Lens to receive a step-by-step explanation and solution. These updates, powered by large language models, enable students to address a wide variety of problems through Google’s search interface. The increasing prevalence of AI tools like ChatGPT, which can write essays and assist with assignments, has raised concerns in education about facilitating cheating. Google’s integration provides similar problem-solving abilities directly through its search bar. The new tools can also tackle word problems, especially those common in physics homework, helping students find answers quickly and efficiently. TechCrunch recently reported that users can also take pictures of certain geometry problems and use Lens to obtain solutions. Some educational institutions, such as New York City public schools, initially banned AI tools like ChatGPT due to concerns about academic dishonesty. However, this ban was lifted at the end of the previous school year, with educational leaders emphasizing the need to teach students how to work responsibly with generative AI. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and several experts suggest fears about AI-enabled cheating are overstated, comparing the use of these AI tools to calculators and emphasizing their role as modern educational resources.

article_content: On October 10, 2012, singer Jessie J joined 19 other celebrities in supporting BBC Children In Need’s new fundraising campaign, 'Show You Care With The Lindt Bear.' Actresses Emilia Fox and Helena Bonham Carter are among the supporters. The campaign aims to raise £100,000 for Children In Need by auctioning limited edition porcelain Lindt bears signed by celebrities. Twenty celebrities have each signed a gold porcelain Lindt bear, which will be auctioned in phases on eBay over five weeks. Other participating stars include Tom Jones, Olly Murs, Emma Bunton, and Alexandra Burke. Each week, four bears are made available for auction for ten days, with proceeds going directly to the charity. As part of the campaign, Jessie J, Emilia Fox, Arlene Phillips, and Angela Griffin participated in a photo shoot by photographer Lorenzo Agius. At the time of reporting, Natalie Imbruglia's signed Lindt bear had a top bid of £52.23, Emma Bunton's was at £51, Sara Cox's at £31, and Helena Bonham Carter's at £43. Bidding for these bears closes at midnight on October 18. If fans don’t win a signed bear, they can still support Children In Need by participating in the 'share a bear' campaign on Facebook. When 25,000 shares are reached, Lindt will donate £25,000 to the charity. A Lindt spokesperson said, 'We are thrilled to be supporting BBC Children In Need this year, a charity close to our hearts. Our chocolate Lindt bear was a big success last year, and we hope the celebrity signed editions will be just as popular. We encourage everyone to join the auction and support this worthy cause.' To participate in 'share a bear,' visit Lindt's Facebook page.

article_content: A set of six Argentina jerseys worn by Lionel Messi during the 2022 World Cup is set to be auctioned by Sotheby's this December, with an estimated value of $10 million. Messi wore these shirts in the first halves of group-stage matches against Saudi Arabia and Mexico, as well as in later games against Australia, the Netherlands, Croatia, and the final against France. Argentina's triumphant run in Qatar marked Messi's crowning achievement, following four previous unsuccessful World Cup campaigns. If the jerseys surpass $10 million at auction, it would make them the most valuable sports memorabilia collection ever sold, according to Sotheby's. The current record for an individual jersey is held by Michael Jordan's 1998 NBA Finals Chicago Bulls shirt, which sold for $10.1 million last year. Auction houses have shown growing interest in sports memorabilia as the market expands in recent years. The jerseys are being auctioned by US tech startup AC Momento, which assists athletes in managing their memorabilia collections. A portion of the proceeds will be donated to the UNICAS Project, an initiative in collaboration with a Barcelona children’s hospital supporting children with rare diseases. Fans can view the jerseys for free at the auction from November 30 to December 14.

Kaos puniki kasob nyidang olih Messi ring babak pertama indik pertandingan group lawan Saudi Arabia miwah Mexico, tur ring pertandingan sisan lawan Australia, Belanda, Kroasia, miwah final lawan Prancis. article_content: Sheikh Ahmed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, managing director of the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), was confirmed dead on Tuesday—four days after his glider went down over a Moroccan lake, Morocco’s news agency reports. Aged 41, Sheikh Ahmed was also the brother of Abu Dhabi’s ruler and UAE president, Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan. His disappearance followed a crash on Friday. Aside from leading the world-renowned ADIA, Sheikh Ahmed chaired the board for the Zayed Foundation for Charity and Humanitarian Works. His body was recovered from Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah lake in Skhirat Temara, near Morocco’s capital Rabat, by rescue teams. The search, as detailed by the Moroccan Press Agency, mobilized about 225 personnel—including over 100 divers from Morocco, the UAE, France, Spain, and the USA, plus four emergency doctors. The plane’s pilot was rescued and found in good health, according to UAE’s WAM news agency. Sheikh Ahmed’s remains are being repatriated to the Emirates and are expected to be buried on Wednesday. Three days of official mourning have begun, with the ruling family to offer prayers at Sheikh Zayed Mosque, per Abu Dhabi TV. In 2009, Forbes named Sheikh Ahmed the 27th most powerful person in the world. ADIA itself, founded in 1976, is owned by the Abu Dhabi government. Interviewed by Germany’s Handelsblatt in January, Sheikh Ahmed expressed a preference for describing ADIA as a globally diversified investment institution, emphasizing its mission to secure Abu Dhabi’s welfare for current and future generations. While reports estimate ADIA's assets at $300–800 billion, Sheikh Ahmed insisted the fund does not disclose figures and described media estimates as exaggerated. Nonetheless, the Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute credits ADIA as among the wealthiest worldwide. Reporting was contributed by CNN’s Saad Abedine and Caroline Faraj.

article_content: Longtime fans Claire Sanford and Chad Richhart have been attending Baltimore Orioles games since 1992, arriving at Camden Yards to celebrate the team’s return to the postseason. This season marks the Orioles clinching a playoff spot for the first time in seven years. Maureen Hall called the moment a dream come true for dedicated supporters, comparing it to Christmas. Along with Robin Goodwin, Hall attended a September game dressed in Orioles gear, reflecting the growing excitement throughout Baltimore. This optimism follows the success of a young, skilled roster developed after the Orioles’ 2018 season, when the team lost a franchise-record 115 games. New management prioritized homegrown talent, resulting in 101 wins and securing first place in the American League East, ahead of wealthier rivals like the Yankees and Red Sox. Columnist Jon Meoli, who has followed the team since 2016, explained the overhaul began with a focus on developing young players with lower salaries. Key contributors include catcher Adley Rutschman, shortstop Gunnar Henderson (a top candidate for AL Rookie of the Year), and pitchers Grayson Rodriguez and Kyle Bradish. A mix of energetic newcomers and leadership from veterans like Ryan Mountcastle and Austin Hays has fueled the Orioles’ recent success. However, some fans are cautious about the team’s limited playoff experience. Erick Byorum, who has followed the team since the 1970s, acknowledged this concern while remaining hopeful. General Manager Mike Elias, who joined in 2018 after time with the Houston Astros, believes the team is ready for the challenge, even when facing more experienced divisional opponents. Elias wishes for Baltimore’s 2023 achievement to be the foundation for future success. The Orioles, rooted in Baltimore since the 1950s with three World Series titles, have long symbolized city pride. Fans like Kathy Buckner remember both the historic victories and the difficult stretches, highlighting the steadfast loyalty within the community. article_content: Jeffrey A. Miron, a senior lecturer in economics at Harvard University, argues that any economic stimulus should follow the principle: 'first, do no harm.' Libertarians often critique President Obama's stimulus package, suggesting that some interventions could do more harm than good. They support removing policies that hurt the economy regardless of whether there is a recession. Miron offers several policy proposals compatible with libertarian views: 1. Repeal the Corporate Income Tax: Miron asserts this would encourage investment, improve accounting transparency, lower compliance costs, and minimize tax code distortions. Repeal could quickly increase corporate share prices and cash flow, lessen reliance on bank loans, and stimulate both short-term growth and long-term efficiency. 2. Adjust Carbon Taxes and Marginal Tax Rates: While opinions differ on reducing fossil fuel use, Miron suggests higher carbon taxes combined with lower marginal tax rates would more effectively address environmental concerns and incentivize the private sector, all without raising deficits. 3. Moderate Entitlement Growth: With Social Security and Medicare facing strains as the population ages, Miron recommends gradually raising eligibility ages to maintain fiscal health and reassure markets. 4. Reduce Wasteful Spending: Miron identifies many current government expenditures—such as some subsidies, costly infrastructure, and inefficient systems—as wasteful. Cutting these could improve the nation’s fiscal situation. 5. Expedite Military Withdrawal: Faster withdrawal from Iraq and Afghanistan would reduce costs and allow resources to be redeployed elsewhere. 6. Limit Union Power: Opposing increased unionization measures (like the card check bill) and repealing the Davis-Bacon Act, Miron argues, would promote labor market efficiency. 7. Support Free Trade: Miron warns that protectionism, including stimulus provisions requiring domestic goods, can harm the economy. He calls for a strong reaffirmation of America’s support for free trade. 8. Expand Legal Immigration: Increasing quotas for skilled worker visas (H-1B) would enhance US productivity and provide opportunities for international workers. 9. End Risky Bailouts: Miron argues against bailing out companies that engaged in excessive risk-taking, saying such actions only encourage further risk. Miron concludes that the focus should be on resolving known issues and reducing ineffective government policies, rather than expanding government intervention. The key, as in medicine, is to avoid causing additional harm. These opinions reflect the views of Jeffrey Miron alone.

De nglaksanayang; pemikiran libertarian majengin ngilangi kebijakan sane ngerugiin ekonomi, nenten dadi resesi. Miron nyidayang sawatara proposal kebijakan ring ajengan libertarian: 1. Ngilangi Pajak Penghasilan Korporasi: Miron yakin puniki prasida nyungsung investasi, ngedengin transparansi akuntansi, ngidikang biaya kepatuhan, lan nyuda distorsi ring kode pajak. Ngilangi pajak prasida langsung ngedengin harga saham tur kas perusahaan, nyingakin ketergantungan bank, tur ngedengin pertumbuhan ekonomi jangka pendek lan panjang. 2. Ngatur Pajak Karbon lan Turunkan Tarif Marginal: Miron nyarengin ganjalan lingkungan becik ngelaksanayang pajak karbon lebih tinggi dipaduang tarip marginal endeke, prasida dadosang solusi becik polih sektor swasta, tanpa ngedengin defisit. 3. Ngelanturang Pertumbuhan Hak Sosial: Social Security lan Medicare ngalantur beban fiskal waktu generasi lanjut, Miron ngusulin ngedengin umur kelayakan supaya kas fiskal jagi stabil tur pasar ten waswas. 4. Ngurangin Pengeluaran Pemerintah Sia-sia: Miron ngorahang pengeluaran pemerintah kadang sing efektif, kayang subsidi, proyek infrastruktur melarat, lan sistem sing becik. Nyuda pengeluaran puniki prasida ningkatin kesehatan fiskal negara. 5. Nyepatinin Mundur Militer: Mundur pasukan ring Irak lan Afghanistan ngidang nyuda beban biaya tur sumber daya prasida dimanfaatkan malih. 6. Batasi Kekuatan Serikat Kerja: Sing setuju aturan sane ngedengin kekuatan serikat kerja (contoh card check bill), lan ngusulin mbatalang Undang-undang Davis-Bacon, Miron yakin puniki prasida ngedengin pasar tenaga kerja. 7. Nyokong Dagang Bebas: Miron wantah tua ring proteksionisme, adan aturan stimulus maksa angge produk lokal, nenten becik ring ekonomi. Ia ngusulin Amerika tegas nyokong dagang bebas. 8. Meluasang Imigrasi Legal: Nambahin quota visa pekerja ahli (H-1B) prasida ngedengin daya saing Amerika lan nyidayang peluang ring pekerja manca. 9. Stop Ngebantu Bisnis Berisiko: Miron nyarengin nenten mambantu perusahaan sane polih resiko, ngorahang puniki nyangsang resiko makin gede. Miron makta musti fokus nyelesaiang masalah sane nyata tur nyangsang kebijakan pemerintah sing tepat. Maangge prinsip kedokteran: tong nambahang masalah. Opini puniki sane kadadosang ring Miron sane dados indik ajengan.

article_content: British taxpayers have contributed thousands of pounds to support Kenyan graffiti artists as part of the Mtaani Initiative, funded through the £6.7 million aid program Making All Voices Count. Around £8,000 in public funds is dedicated to this project, which aims to collaborate with artists to spread data-driven information in Nairobi's slums, empowering local citizens to make informed decisions and hold their government accountable. Some murals produced as part of this initiative, which criticized politicians ahead of upcoming elections in Nairobi, were removed by local officials within hours of being painted. Critics, such as Andy Silvester of the Taxpayers’ Alliance, argue that the funding is a misuse of taxpayers’ money, claiming foreign aid should prioritize helping the world’s poorest rather than subsidizing graffiti. They note that in the last two months of 2013, the UK spent £3.75 billion on aid to meet spending targets, with the government pledging 0.7% of national income toward aid, totaling £12.6 billion for the year. The initiative is part of a broader program supported by the Department for International Development, which also funds projects addressing police corruption in Liberia and improving maternal health care in Nigeria. Officials have defended the Mtaani Initiative, stressing its role in helping youth in slum areas participate in civic processes and influence the future of aid in their communities. The article also references previous aid controversies, such as funding the Ethiopian girl group Yegna, sometimes referred to as the ‘Ethiopian Spice Girls’, who have been subject to criticism in their home country.

article_content:
Once a prestigious destination for railway company employees in Eastern Germany, the EisenBahner (Railwaymen) Hotel in the Erzgebirge region has stood abandoned for 25 years. The hotel's corridors, which once welcomed select guests, are now occupied only by insects. With its 25 double bedrooms, restaurant, and kitchen lying in ruin, the building remains a snapshot of its thriving days during the German Democratic Republic (GDR).

The EisenBahner Hotel was rebuilt in 1883 after a fire and, in 1958, became a convalescent home for employees of Germany's national railway system, the Reichsbahnamt. During the GDR era, the hotel was seen as prestigious and accessible mainly to railwaymen and their families. Its furniture and fixtures reflect the limited comforts and consistent design typical of East Germany at the time.

After the fall of the Berlin Wall and Germany’s reunification, many state-owned vacation properties, such as the EisenBahner Hotel, fell out of use and into disrepair. Today, the hotel remains untouched, with the original furnishings gathering dust and decay.

German photographer Stefan Dietze, 31, from Leipzig, captured this sense of frozen time in a photo series. Recounting his experience, Dietze described the distinct atmosphere of the abandoned hotel and how, for him — having grown up in the GDR — it evoked memories of his childhood. He notes that, walking through the kitchen, it seemed as if someone had just finished cleaning up but never returned. According to Dietze, the recreational homes of the GDR often resembled each other closely due to the limited variety of furnishings available at the time. The EisenBahner Hotel, once a lively hub with a bustling restaurant, now stands as a testament to a bygone era.

article_content: A tentative agreement between the actors' union Sag-Aftra and Hollywood studios features new safeguards for artificial intelligence (AI) and requires the presence of intimacy coordinators on set. Details released on Friday reveal the Sag-Aftra national board approved the deal with 86% support. The agreement will be sent to the union's 160,000 members for final ratification next week, but actors can return to work immediately. The announcement, made Wednesday, likely marks the end of a four-month strike that, alongside a separate writers' strike, severely disrupted film and television production. Chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland described the deal as 'the absolute best,' emphasizing its timely agreement. He highlighted that the AI provisions protect actors' rights to consent, fair compensation, and continued employment. Studios have increasingly explored AI technologies, making these protections a central topic in negotiations. There were concerns that background actors could be particularly vulnerable to job loss from digital replication. Crabtree-Ireland explained, 'No use of a digital replica can be used to evade engagement and payment of a background actor under this contract.' Valued at over $1 billion, the three-year agreement has received praise from high-profile actors including Jamie Lee Curtis and Zac Efron. A full summary of the contract is expected Monday. While Hollywood’s top stars earn millions, many lesser-known performers have faced financial challenges, especially amid inflation and industry changes. The 118-day shutdown is the longest in Sag-Aftra’s 90-year history. According to Deadline, the combined actors' and writers' strikes reportedly cost the California economy more than $6.5 billion. During the strike, actors were prohibited from attending events, premieres, and participating in promotion or publicity for projects, in line with union rules.

Rincian sane katurang ring Rahina Sukra nunasang kalau jakang nasional Sag-Aftra sampun nglaksanayang 86% dukungan wenten perjanjian puniki. Perjanjian puniki prasida ngametuangang anggotane sane wantah ngantosang 160,000 krama ring minggu rauh, nanging aktor sampun dados nyagaang karya silih tunggil. Pengumuman puniki sane kabawos ring Budha prasida nyidayang pungkasanin grebek sane sekancan malihan sami perbekel penulis sane ngadadosang gangguan ring produksi film lan TV ring warsa 4 bulan puniki. Negosiator utama, Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, ngicenangang yening perjanjian puniki ‘ika pinaka becik pisan’, dados ritatkala sane patut. article_content: The latest macOS Sonoma 14.1 update introduces a liquid detection feature for USB-C ports. According to 9to5Mac, a new system daemon called 'liquiddetectiond' runs in the background to analyze whether the computer's USB-C ports have been exposed to liquids. This process, described as a 'Liquid Detection and Corrosion Mitigation Daemon,' focuses on collecting analytics rather than directly alerting users. Similar functionality exists on iPhones and iPads, which alert users if liquid is detected in the connector. On Macs, the feature currently appears limited to data analysis and does not provide notifications to end users. Apple's limited warranty does not cover liquid damage, including for water-resistant products like the iPhone, Apple Watch, and some AirPods models. macOS Sonoma 14.1 is the first major update to Apple’s latest operating system. New features include the ability to favorite songs, albums, and playlists in the Music app, with favorited items easily filtered and accessed. Additionally, users can now view the AppleCare+ status of their Mac and connected AirPods in System Settings. In other news, India has approved the first 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) in the defence sector, granting Sweden’s Saab permission to establish a rocket manufacturing facility. State Bank of India (SBI) reported an 8% increase in its second-quarter net profit, driven by steady loan demand and reduced provisions. Byju’s, a leading edtech firm, reported a 2.3 times increase in standalone revenue to ₹3,569 crore for the financial year ending March 2022, along with a reduced EBITDA loss.

article_content: Tonobok Okowa, President of the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN), has pledged technical support for the inaugural MTN CHAMPS athletics championships. The event, organized by Making of Champions (MoC) and sponsored by telecommunications giant MTN in collaboration with the Nigeria School Sports Federation, aims to develop young athletic talent across the nation. More than 7,000 athletes from 500 schools are expected to compete for over 1,000 medals and 32 team titles. The championships are divided into three age categories: cadets (U-14), youths (U-17), and juniors (U-20). The competition will be held in four Nigerian cities: Benin City, Ibadan, Uyo, and Abuja. The schedule is as follows: Benin City from October 12 to 14, Uyo from October 26 to 28, Ibadan from November 9 to 11, and Abuja from November 29 to December 1. The grand finale will take place in Abuja on December 2. Okowa expressed appreciation for the establishment of the competition, explaining that it addresses a critical gap for young athletes. "I am the main beneficiary of this championship because there have been no proper competitions for these age groups, and MoC has resolved this issue through MTN CHAMPS," Okowa told PUNCH Sports Extra. "Athletes often drop out between the ages of 15 and 18 due to a lack of quality competitions. The AFN will provide every possible support for this event." MoC founder Bambo Akani highlighted the importance of the competition, stating, "I am pleased that MTN is now supporting our efforts to raise the profile of track and field in Nigeria. This is a significant moment in the history of school sports and athletics in our country. I am confident that MTN CHAMPS will uncover and nurture athletic talents nationwide."

article_content: Apple has agreed to pay $18.25 million after federal authorities claimed the company’s hiring practices made it difficult for U.S. citizens, residents, and certain other applicants to secure jobs. The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) stated that Apple created unfair barriers by not advertising some jobs publicly and requiring paper applications for certain roles, which limited access for many candidates. According to the DOJ, these actions were intended to favor existing workers on temporary visas under the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM), which allows companies to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency but requires employers to consider U.S.-based workers first. The DOJ said Apple’s recruitment for PERM positions was less accessible to U.S. applicants compared to its overseas hiring, and that the company often dismissed electronically submitted job applications. The investigation started in 2019, prompting Apple to later update its recruitment methods. Apple has said any errors were unintentional and denies any intentional discrimination. Under the settlement, the $18.25 million includes $6.75 million in civil penalties and the remaining amount for back pay to qualified applicants. Apple must now advertise PERM jobs on its website and accept electronic applications, and the company is required to report new PERM hires to the DOJ twice yearly. Although Apple does not admit guilt, it has agreed to implement these changes. A company spokesperson said Apple had already started following a remediation plan. Those eligible for back pay will be able to file claims through a website once it is available.

article_content: Freedom and equality are core American values, and they are also central to Sikhism. This faith teaches equality among all people—regardless of race, gender, or class—and reflects this in practice. A Sikh temple, called a gurdwara or 'House of God,' is open to everyone at all hours. Its four doors face each cardinal direction, symbolizing inclusivity toward people of every faith and background. Gurdwaras exist both in India—home to the famous Golden Temple—and in the United States. One such place is the gurdwara in Oak Creek, Wisconsin, where tragedy occurred when its openness was exploited by someone who rejected those values. Keeping the gurdwara welcoming was due in large part to Satwant Singh Kaleka, the temple president and a longtime friend. Though now remembered as a victim and hero who tried to stop the attacker, Kaleka was known for his warmth and generosity. His family is still a cornerstone of Milwaukee's community spirit. I fondly remember Mr. Kaleka's family leading songs at our home after our wedding, reflecting their joyful spirit. My family and I were not present at the gurdwara that tragic Sunday. The loss weighs heavily, but the unity afterward has been significant, for which I am sincerely grateful. Sikhism welcomes all people. Every gurdwara includes a community kitchen, or langar, providing free food to anyone at any time. All guests sit together as equals, embodying the principle of unity. Sikhs also practice selfless service, or seva, especially toward those in need. Sikh teachings align with the best of America: equality and service for everyone. Sikhs have long made sacrifices for these ideals, in both India and America. Yet, protecting liberty sometimes means making space for those who oppose these ideals. This includes recognizing the existence of people like Wade Michael Page, who carried out the Oak Creek attack. Freedom can be complex. As Americans and Sikhs, our commitment is to respect everyone's fundamental rights. The sacrifices of individuals like Lt. Brian Murphy—injured while helping others—Satwant Singh Kaleka, and many more, affirm these ideals. This is the cost of the inclusive society envisioned by our founders and by Sikh philosophy. Sikh scripture teaches that all are united under one spirit—this unity extends to everyone, not just those we agree with. Remembering this is essential. Chardi Kala. May your spirit rise. These reflections are solely those of Kanwar M. Singh.

Pura Sikh sane kasuratang gurdwara utawi 'Umahe Tuhan,' tetep kabuka ring sami tiang ajengan. Pintu gurdwara ngad facing ring sekancan penjuru angin, nglambangin keterbukaan ring sami agama lan asal. Puniki dados biaya masyarakate sane kebuka indik ajaran para pendiri bangsa sareng ajaran Sikh. Kitab suci Sikh ngajinang ring sekancan dane satu sane wenten ring atma utama—puniki kadadosang ring semeton sekancan, tusing ring sane setuju dogen. Ngidangang puniki dados hal utama. Chardi Kala. Moga semangat ragane ngelantur. Pemargin puniki indik Kanwar M. Singh dogen.

article_content: Thousands of Egyptians assembled in Tahrir Square, Cairo, to oppose a draft constitution perceived to shield the military from civilian accountability. The protest, which happened just before Egypt’s parliamentary elections scheduled for November 28, drew mainly Islamist organizations and also secular participants. After the ousting of President Hosni Mubarak earlier this year, the Supreme Council of the Armed Forces assumed control of government, promising to eventually pass authority to a civilian parliament and president. Despite these assurances, many demonstrators worry that proposed constitutional principles—excluding the military budget from civilian review—would allow the military to remain autonomous and largely unaccountable. These demonstrations highlight the strong influence of Islamist groups, most notably the Muslim Brotherhood's Freedom and Justice Party, within Egyptian politics. Meanwhile, sectarian tensions continue to rise. The day before the protest, a march by Coptic Christians in Cairo was attacked by unknown assailants, leaving at least 32 injured—including two police officers. The group was heading to Tahrir Square to commemorate those killed during earlier clashes involving Copts in the capital, amid a series of violent incidents between Egypt’s Muslim majority and the Coptic minority in recent months.

article_content: Norland College, renowned for training professional nannies since 1892, has just revealed a new version of its celebrated uniform for the first time in seven decades. Though the look still honors its longstanding tradition—retaining the signature beige, brown, and white shades, along with discreet accessories—the design now features modern touches for improved practicality and comfort. The updated uniform includes more tailored panelling at the waist for a flattering silhouette, heavier fabric that holds its shape, and a more open neckline without the classic brown tie. Brown tights and sensible shoes remain, but winter brings a contemporary brown overcoat, complete with a wraparound collar, velvet cuffs, and an embroidered 'N'. In addition to the formal attire, students now have a practical work placement outfit: navy blue trousers, a jumper, a bright blue polo shirt, and a weatherproof jacket, nodding to colors from historical Norland uniforms. Principal Liz Hunt notes that refreshing the uniform matches the college's evolving curriculum, which now teaches students skills like self-defense, Taekwondo, defensive driving, and handling paparazzi—preparing graduates for the unique demands of working with high-profile families. Norland’s rigorous four-year degree, based in Bath, Somerset, integrates courses in subjects like psychology, child development, cooking, and home management. The college’s trademark discipline ensures nannies are easily recognized for their impeccable appearance and professionalism, qualities that have made them the preferred choice for celebrity and royal households alike. Current students and recent graduates have welcomed the changes, praising the contemporary fit, comfort, and practical features such as larger hidden pockets—all while celebrating the continued elegance and heritage that set Norland nannies apart. Founded by Emily Ward to distinguish her professionally trained nannies from housemaids, Norland College remains a trailblazer in childcare. The new uniform balances tradition with modern needs, ensuring future Norlanders look as polished and capable as ever.

article_content: John Barnes, the Jamaican-born former Liverpool and England footballer, recalls the racist abuse he experienced during his career. One notable incident occurred 27 years ago, when a fan threw a banana at him during a Merseyside derby between Liverpool and Everton. Barnes calmly kicked the banana away. In 2014, Barcelona’s Dani Alves faced similar abuse—a Villarreal supporter threw a banana at him, which Alves picked up and ate. According to Barnes, such incidents show that football still struggles to address discrimination effectively. "The way we’re trying to tackle racism is wrong," Barnes explained at a CNN interview during a YO! Sushi promotional event promoting support for Japan in the 2014 World Cup. "True change requires education—explaining why racism is wrong, not just telling people not to do it or punishing them." He added: "If you simply fine or ban people, racism doesn’t disappear. People just keep quiet about it. Do we want to eradicate racism or merely silence it?" A week after Alves’s experience, Levante’s Papakouli Diop claimed he heard monkey chants from Atletico Madrid fans. Diop responded by dancing in front of the alleged offenders, an action Barnes questioned. While Barnes fully supports Alves’s response, he reflected: "If bullies see their abuse isn’t affecting you, they may stop. If you react, they continue." From a footballer’s perspective, Barnes suggests showing disregard is effective. Barnes praised Villarreal’s swift ban of the fan who threw the banana at Alves, but cautioned that football alone cannot end racism: "These aren’t just football problems. Unless racism is eradicated in society, it will persist in football." Institutional responses exist. FIFA, after a series of prominent racism cases in 2013, introduced punishments: first offenses can lead to warnings, fines, or playing in empty stadiums; more serious or repeated offenses may result in point deductions, demotion, or expulsion from tournaments.

article_content: Michal Zyro’s last encounter with a Scottish team was memorable yet painful. The Legia Warsaw midfielder scored in both legs of a decisive 6-1 aggregate win over Celtic in the Champions League qualifiers, only to see those efforts undone by an administrative mistake. In the closing minutes of their victory at Murrayfield, Legia substituted Zyro for the suspended Bartosz Bereszynski, which violated UEFA rules. As a result, UEFA awarded Celtic a 3-0 second-leg walkover, eliminating Legia Warsaw from the competition on the away goals rule. Zyro says he has moved on from the setback, but facing Scotland again adds extra motivation. Now 22, Zyro is part of the Poland squad preparing to play Gordon Strachan’s side in a crucial qualifier in Warsaw. ‘I have mixed memories from playing Scottish teams,’ Zyro admitted. ‘On the field, against Celtic, it was great, but things went wrong off it. I scored in both games, so that was special for me personally. What happened after was extremely unfortunate, but we can be proud of our two impressive matches against Celtic.’ Zyro added that he is focusing only on the upcoming game: ‘It’s a different context—national teams, new players. The important thing is for Poland to win, not just for me.’ He believes his experience against Celtic gives him confidence but recognizes international football is another challenge. After being eliminated from the Champions League, Zyro said, ‘We did everything right on the pitch. The mistake happened off the field.’ Legia have since won both games in their Europa League group but can't help thinking they should be competing among Europe’s elite. ‘Watching the Champions League now, it’s hard to accept we were so close,’ he said. ‘But I’m young and hope to have more chances in the future. For older players, it’s tougher as opportunities are fewer.’ Poland are in high spirits after a historic 2-0 win over Germany and a 7-0 victory over Gibraltar, without conceding a goal so far. Despite a strong start, the squad remains focused and cautious, showing respect for Scotland as a strong opponent. Zyro regards the current Polish squad as one of the best in recent years, blending top talents like Robert Lewandowski and three experienced goalkeepers with emerging players. He states that the team has improved in every match and is determined to win their group and continue progressing.
translated_content: Panglimbak ring tim Skotlandia pinaka momen sane eling lan nyenengin ngajeng nyenengin ring Michal Zyro. Gelandang Legia Warsaw punika ngalanturang gol ring kalih leg ring kemenangan agregat 6-1 ngalawan Celtic ring kualifikasi Liga Champions, nanging upayane dados sia-sia akibat kesalahan administratif. Ring menit pungkasan ring Murrayfield, Legia ngalanturang pergantian pemain, masugang Zyro sareng Bartosz Bereszynski sane kasuspensi, sane ngalanturang aturan UEFA. Akibate, UEFA ngicenang Celtic menang walkover 3-0 ring leg kalih, sane maktaang Legia Warsawa keluar saking kompetisi ring aturan gol tandang. Zyro nyantosang sampun prasida nglaksanayang kasus puniki, nanging nyanggraang Skotlandia malih dados motivasi tambahan. Ring yuswa 22 warsa, Zyro dados anggota timnas Polandia sane ngamolihang nglaksanayang pertandingan penting ngalawan tim asuhan Gordon Strachan ring Warsawa. 'Tiang polih pengalaman campur aduk ngalawan tim Skotlandia,' Ritatkala Zyro. 'Ring lapangan nglawan Celtic, ajengan ngidangang becik banget, nanging masalah akehan kejantenan ring luar lapangan. Tiang prasida gol ring kalih pertandingan sane dados ajengan ring tiang. Saking masalah sane kadaoang, punika pengalaman sane ngidangang pelajaran, nanging tim prasida maktaang ajengan ring kalih pertandingan suba bagus ngalawan Celtic.' Zyro nyantosang fokus kasuratang ring pertandingan sane rauh: ‘Situasi puniki dados beda — tim nasional, pemain anyar. Hal paling penting ring Polandia menang, indik tiang ritatkala. Pengalaman ring Celtic ngidang dados kepercayaan malih ring tiang, nanging bal paling kenceng ring tim nasional.’ Sakewala Legia kaping luar ring Liga Champions, Zyro ngidangang ring lapangan prasida laksanayang tugas, sedangkan kesalahan nyantosang ring administratif. Legia prasida nenten prasida mokohang ring dua pertandingan babak grup Liga Europa, nanging masih ningalin rasa samian ring tingkat tinggi Eropa. ‘Ngantosang Liga Champions i ring TV, ajengan ngidangang ngajeng tim prasida sanget dekat ring langoan,’ beling Zyro. ‘Tiang taler percaya ngantosang ring masa depan prasida maktaang kesempatan nyanggraang, malih ring pemain sane sepuh, kesempatan puniki dados angin-anginan.” Timnas Polandia prasida ring rasa percaya diri sane wenten ulih kemenangan bersejarah 2-0 nglawan Jerman lan 7-0 nglawan Gibraltar, tanpa kebobolan gol. Sanajan awal ring grup prasida mulus, pemain Polandia tetap fokus lan ngajeng ajengan, ngamolihang rasa hormat ring Skotlandia sane pinaka lawan kuat. Zyro ngajeng tim Polandia ring masa puniki pinaka sane ajengan ring warsa terakhir. Gabungan talenta utama ring antuk pemain mewah wantah ring Robert Lewandowski sareng tiga penjaga gawang kawisesa, taler pemain anyar sane maktaang semangat ring lapangan. Ia ngidangang tim prasida ngalanturang ring saban pertandingan lan fokus ring kemenangan grup.

article_content: Barbra Streisand’s memoir, 'My Name Is Barbra,' offers a candid look back on her journey—covering fame, love, setbacks, and memorable encounters with fellow icons. Near the end, Streisand reflects that imagining stardom once brought her more joy than actually living it, bemoaning the rumors and envy her success stirred. Through almost a thousand pages, Streisand explores her deep yet complicated family ties, considers her romantic experiences, and recounts the bumps and victories that shaped her. After losing her father as a baby, developing a close if quirky bond with her grandfather, and dealing with a stepfather she disliked, Streisand’s memories are surprisingly intimate—her grandfather once washed her mouth out with soap for swearing but showed affection in his own way. She shares lively stories from her interactions with men like Marlon Brando—recounting an unanticipated kiss and humorous exchanges—playful uncertainty about a fling with Warren Beatty, and the moment she fell for Elliott Gould thanks to a glimpse of his neck. Streisand also describes her admiration for Pierre Trudeau’s personality and boldness. Attracted to magnetic men, Streisand details her chemistry with Kris Kristofferson during 'A Star Is Born,' and expresses delight over Don Johnson’s appeal. She admits her attraction is sometimes superficial, likening it to collecting art. Not all memories are rosy: Streisand describes ongoing negativity from her mother and incidents of professional sabotage, especially with Sydney Chaplin and Frank Pierson. She also notes her troubled collaboration with Larry Kramer over 'The Normal Heart.' Streisand confides she enjoys directing more than performing, as the repetition of stage roles and a Central Park performance mishap led to reluctance about live shows for decades. Still, her 1994 comeback concert drew dignitaries, celebrities, and politicians, and she recalls a backstage chat about interest rates. The memoir details lasting friendships and impressive acquaintances: Phyllis Diller once mentored her; she knew Joan Rivers early on; and she interacted with President John F. Kennedy and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, who encouraged her to write. Streisand became close to Virginia Clinton, Bill Clinton’s mother, and offers fun trivia like Aerosmith’s hit being inspired by husband James Brolin. As a teenager, musician Prince adored her work. Despite her dislike for cooking, Streisand describes with gusto the foods she loves—simple deli sandwiches, fresh honeydew, fancy dishes recommended by friends, and coffee ice cream (minus chocolate chips). Streisand’s affection for her pets culminates in the story of cloning her late dog Sammie, resulting in two lookalike puppies. She observes that while you can recreate a pet’s appearance, personality and spirit cannot be copied.
translated_content: Memoir Barbra Streisand, 'My Name Is Barbra,' ngidangang wenten kisah nyata ring perjalanan hidupné – dados kawentar, tresna, penglimbak, tur ketemu sareng tokoh-tokoh ageng. Ring pungkasan, Streisand ngebahas yening melajah ngimpi dados kawentar ngalanturang rasa seneng ring kenyatan mamargi dados kawentar, malih nyidaangangangang rasa kecewa ring isu-isu sareng rasa iri sane teken suksesné. Ngantosang sekancan ring buku puniki, Streisand nyarengin kadeketan kulawarga sane rumit, pengalaman asmara, lan lika-liku ring uripné. Majeng kehilangan bapa semeng kecal, ngemargiang rasa dekat ring ajin semengang alit mesakadi masolahang cangkem nganggén sabun, namun tan wenten rasa tresna ring cara nenten biasa. Ida ngidangangang kisah unik sareng para lanang nenten biasané, indik Marlon Brando, ring pengalaman ciuman sing diwareg, tur adegan lucu. Suksma ring hubungan sareng Warren Beatty, kewewinan ring Elliott Gould sekadi ngidangang gulu né, tur matemu Pierre Trudeau sane cerdas tur berani. Suksma dado ring iraga magnetis, Streisand nyarengin chemistryné sareng Kris Kristofferson ring 'A Star Is Born', tur ngetok Don Johnson sane ngidaangang rasa tertarik. Ida ngaku katresnan kadang prasida superficial, sekadi ngumpulang seni. Tan kebeh ring uripne becik, ring buku puniki nyarengin rasa negatif saking ibuné sareng kolega-kolega ring pekerjaan, prasida kelaksanayang ring Sydney Chaplin lan Frank Pierson, sareng pengalaman adu argumen ring Larry Kramer ring 'The Normal Heart.' Streisand ngaku lebih demen ngatur ring balik layar ketimbang anggon manggung, ngalanturang kenangan ring kejadian Central Park sane dados alesan tusing konser sekancan warsa. Nanging, konser come back tahun 1994né dados magnet pejabat, selebritas, lan politisi ageng, sareng kenang-kenangan ngobrolang wicara ekonomi ring backstage. Memoir puniki ngemargiang hubungan sareng sahabat sareng kenalan tiang – Phyllis Diller dados mentor, iraga kenal Joan Rivers, sareng ketemu Presiden JFK sareng Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis tolongang nulis buku. Deket sekancan ring Virginia Clinton, ibuné Bill Clinton, lan kisah menarik sekadi inspirasi lagu Aerosmith saking James Brolin. Prince dados penggemar setia ring masa timpal. Sané ten demen memasak, Streisand tetap sayang ngidang ring rasa makanannya – sandwich sederhana, honeydew, masakan mewah rekomendasi sahabat, tur es krim kopi tan coklat chip. Ring asu Sammie, ceritanya nglaksanayang cloning taler dadosang dua asu mirip namun beda kepribadian. Streisand matemu ring kawentenan nglaksanayangang wujud prasida, tapi ajin manten tusing prasida kaanggenang.

article_content: Kenya's David Rudisha effortlessly advanced to the 800m final at the Commonwealth Games by winning his semi-final at Hampden Park. The Olympic champion posted a time of 1:46.61, just ahead of fellow Kenyan Ferguson Rotich. Guy Learmonth from Scotland delivered a strong performance, taking the last qualifying spot for the final. In another semi-final, Botswana’s Nijel Amos finished first with a time of 1:45.65. England’s Michael Rimmer also made it into the final, grabbing a fastest loser spot by a margin of 0.10 seconds. Rudisha told BBC Sport that the semi-final was demanding and explained he led from the start to control the pace. He was pleased with his condition and is optimistic about the upcoming final. Learmonth, 22, from Berwick, described reaching the final as a dream realized. He attributed his success to the enthusiastic home supporters, saying their energy pushed him to the finish line.

article_content: A recent survey suggests that while President Joe Biden is expected to win more overall votes than former President Donald Trump in the 2024 election, the electoral college could result in a Trump victory. Stack Data Strategy polled over 15,000 registered voters across the US from August to November, using quotas to ensure all key groups were represented, especially those often overlooked but critical to outcomes. Results indicate that Trump could reclaim the presidency by winning Arizona, Georgia, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin—battleground states Biden secured in 2020. Combined, these states would give Trump enough electoral votes to surpass the 270 needed for victory. If this scenario plays out, Trump would be the third president since 2000 to win without a majority of the popular vote, alongside George W. Bush and his own 2016 campaign. The survey also assessed independent candidates’ impact. Their influence appears minor, though they could help Trump narrowly win Nevada as Robert F. Kennedy and Cornel West divert over 8% of votes. Despite facing 91 felony charges, Trump leads the Republican primary field by a substantial margin. Conversely, if Florida Governor Ron DeSantis became the Republican nominee, the poll predicts he would lose decisively to Biden—by about 180 electoral votes. Although recent Democratic victories in other elections have been significant, Biden has not managed to extend his lead over Trump in national head-to-head polling, keeping the race highly competitive.

Stack Data Strategy ngawentenang survei ring langkung 15.000 pemilih terdaftar ring Amerika Serikat maktaang saking Agustus dumogi November, geringang metode quotas majalarang indik kawentenan taler ring kelompok pemilih sane kadadosang ajeng pisan. Hasil poling nentenangang Trump prasida dadosangang Arizona, Georgia, Pennsylvania, miwah Wisconsin—negara bagian battleground sane dadosangang Biden ring 2020. Gabungan suara electoral puniki prasida nyantosang Trump malih langkahang 270 suara dados dados presiden. Yen indik puniki kelaksanayang, Trump dados presiden ketiga sawirang warsa 2000 sane prasida maktaang kemenangan tanpa polihang suara terbanyak, prasida kasub ring George W. Pengaruh indik punika prasida alit, silih sinampura nyantosang Trump dadosangang Nevada malih ring bantuan suara saking Robert F. Ring tengah-tengah kemenangan ageng Demokrat ring pemilihan lain, Biden durung prasida mapolih margin utama saking Trump ring poling nasional. Puniki dados indik kompetisi presidensial teken banten pisan.

article_content: An American tourist has been accused of spraying graffiti at 155 locations in central Seoul's Yongsan district, according to police. The Yongsan police department reported arresting an unnamed American man in his 30s, who arrived in South Korea as a tourist in October, local news agency Yonhap stated. The man was detained on Saturday and has been charged with damaging both private and public property, such as underpasses, trash cans, roads, electric poles, house gates, and store shutters, as reported by Chosun Ilbo. Police say the suspect used the words 'bruxism' or 'brux,' in both English and Korean, as his graffiti. He was identified and apprehended with the help of surveillance cameras, according to reports. The tourist told police that he suffers from severe bruxism—a condition where people involuntarily grind or clench their teeth—and wanted to raise public awareness about this issue, as reported by Seoul Shinmun Daily. However, police are continuing to investigate his exact motives and actions, according to Yonhap. Authorities first received complaints about the graffiti on October 25, which prompted them to launch a search for the suspect. An Instagram account, @bruxism.hunter, with no followers, appears to have documented many instances of the graffiti since late October, posting photos from various locations including walls, stairwells, road barriers, and storefronts. The account’s description invites reports of additional sightings, though Business Insider could not independently confirm who runs it. In the meantime, Yonhap reported that the American tourist has been banned from leaving South Korea while investigations continue. Yongsan is known as a popular area for tourists and is home to the Itaewon neighborhood, where more than 150 people died in a crowd crush last year during Halloween.

Lalaki puniki kasangkep ring rahina Sabtu lan kasambat ngalantur kerusakan ring prabot krama miwah gumi, pinaka anggen ngalantur ring jalantitas, tempat sampah, dalan, tiang listrik, pamedalan graha, antuk jalid, makdaang Chosun Ilbo. Polisi nyidangang pelayon puniki nyuratangang aksara 'bruxism' utawi 'brux' ring basa Inggris miwah Korea dados graffitine. Lalaki puniki kasuratang ring CCTV, rauh kapidabdabang olih prajuru. Wiadinang olih polisi, pelayon puniki ngametuangang ring polisi menadosang dados kalaksanayang bruxism sane keras—punika indik kondisyon taler nglaksanayang nyepitin utawi ngemel nyangsang. Lalaki puniki ngidang ngajahang sane wenten indik bruxism, lan ngidang ngajahang masyarakat indik indik punika, maktaang saking Seoul Shinmun Daily. Akunne nenten prasida ngicenangang laporan ring sane nyantosang, tur Business Insider taler durung prasida ngicenang punika indik sane ngelaksanayang akun punika. Wenten ring tengah punika, Yonhap malaksana pelayon Amérika punika sampun dados anggen nenten prasida matilar saking Korea Selatan ring iraga penelitian wenten dados. Yongsan punika dados wilayah sane teken pisan ring pelayon, tur dados panggriya ring kawasan Itaewon, ring nguniang warsa ring Halloween wenten karusakan dados ring tun, ngantos sane setata langkung ring 150 tiang.

article_content: Vince Cable, the 69-year-old Business Secretary, is facing claims from some Liberal Democrats that he may not be fit to lead the party, after reports that he nods off during meetings. Supporters of current leader Nick Clegg have promoted this rumor after Cable hinted he could step in if Clegg were to depart. Although Cable made a public display of energy dancing on Strictly Come Dancing in 2010, critics say he doesn’t show the same enthusiasm in his official duties. They argue his busy schedule is taxing, and question whether he’d be up for a leadership contest at 72, his age at the next election. Cable himself rejects these concerns, affirming he takes on a tough workload, remains healthy, and still has the vitality for his job and for dancing. His supporters also say he does not intend to challenge Clegg, but wouldn’t defer to younger colleagues if a vacancy arose. If Clegg were to step aside, Cable would likely face challengers such as Energy Secretary Ed Davey, Home Office Minister Jeremy Browne, and party president Tim Farron. Cable’s supporters call the rumors unfounded, with one pointing out, ‘Few could manage his government role and still dance ballroom, salsa, and tango.’

Pasikian sane nyokong pemimpin Nick Clegg rauh nyebarin wacana puniki saatos Cable mapikayangang yening ida prasida ngadagangang Clegg pacang melancaran jabatan. article_content: Mira Murati, currently interim CEO of OpenAI, is in talks to potentially bring back Sam Altman, the recently ousted former CEO, and previous President Greg Brockman, though their roles are still not finalized, according to people familiar with the situation. Murati, who took over after Altman’s removal by the board on Friday, is negotiating with Adam D’Angelo, CEO of Quora and a representative of the OpenAI board, sources said, requesting anonymity due to the private and ongoing nature of the discussions. Greg Brockman, who left the board in protest hours after Altman's dismissal, is also involved in these discussions. At the same time, some OpenAI board members are independently looking for a new CEO, contacting known tech industry figures, as per someone with knowledge of the search. Appointing a different CEO would be seen as a strong rejection of top investors like Microsoft and Thrive Capital, who have urged the board to step down and reinstate Altman. These parallel moves—trying to bring Altman back while seeking a new CEO—underscore significant divisions within OpenAI, creators of ChatGPT. Altman was removed from his CEO and director roles by board members led by Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever, who cited his lack of consistent candor in communications. Altman led the company’s efforts to shift from a nonprofit to a more commercially driven model, which conflicted with some board members concerned that progress was too fast and potentially disregarded AI safety implications. However, OpenAI’s COO Brad Lightcap stated safety was not the main factor in Altman’s firing, pointing instead to a communication breakdown. Major investors had little advance warning of Altman's ouster and were upset over losing a leader with a record of developing successful products and securing large investments. Executives such as Murati have aligned with investors in supporting Altman's return. Board members currently include Sutskever, D'Angelo, entrepreneur Tasha McCauley, and Helen Toner from Georgetown University. It remains to be seen whether the board can select a new CEO and what future roles Altman and Brockman might have.

article_content: Kodak, the iconic camera and film company, has confirmed it used weapons-grade uranium in an underground laboratory in upstate New York for over 30 years. According to company representatives and a former scientist, the amount of uranium was too small to sustain a nuclear chain reaction. Former researcher Albert Filo explained that the uranium was alloyed with aluminum and stored in sealed plates that remained stationary for three decades. The total amount, about 3.5 pounds, is less than one-tenth of what experts say would be needed to make a basic nuclear device. Eastman Kodak spokesman, Christopher Veronda, stated that the material could not easily be converted into a weapon, emphasizing that disassembling the device and removing the plates was a complex process requiring highly trained professionals. However, nuclear proliferation advocates warn that the situation highlights the risk of such materials falling into the wrong hands. Edwin Lyman, a nuclear physicist with the Union of Concerned Scientists, stressed the importance of securing all nuclear-weapons-usable material and called for commercial companies to eliminate materials that could potentially be converted into nuclear weapons. Kodak transferred the uranium to the government in 2007 under strict security. For more than three decades, Kodak operated a californium neutron flux multiplier (CFX)—a device about the size of a refrigerator—in a fortified lab beneath Building 82 at its Rochester, New York facility. While not a reactor, the CFX was designed to create a neutron beam for scanning and testing various materials. The device's primary source of neutron radiation was californium, but it used highly enriched uranium to multiply the neutron stream. A Nuclear Regulatory Commission spokesperson confirmed that Kodak’s uranium was enriched to 93.4%—well within weapons-grade material. For comparison, Iran's uranium enrichment program, which has reached 20%, has drawn international sanctions. While Lyman acknowledged the amount at Kodak was insufficient to make a bomb, he cautioned that coordinated efforts could theoretically combine small sources. Although Kodak did not station armed guards, Filo stated that security measures prevented unauthorized access and extracting the uranium would take hours or days. He also noted the robust construction and regular inspections of the lab ensured there was never any radiation leak or risk to nearby residents. Kodak maintains that the existence of the CFX was never concealed and that it operated with the appropriate state and federal licenses. Nevertheless, the use of highly enriched uranium was not widely publicized. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission notes that the U.S. has 31 research or testing reactors, most using low-enriched uranium. Some exceptions, such as reactors at MIT and the University of Missouri, still use highly enriched uranium. The Department of Energy is pushing for a shift to safer alternatives, but technical and financial challenges remain. CNN’s Chris Kokenes contributed to this report.

article_content: Ola Olukoyede, the Chairman of Nigeria’s Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), has urged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) to pursue diligence and innovative thinking for the country’s growth. At NYSC orientation camps in Kwara and Kogi States, EFCC officials relayed his message, stressing the vital role that dedicated and creative youth can play in national progress, urging them to avoid economic and financial crimes like 'yahoo-yahoo.' Olukoyede underscored that the intelligence and enthusiasm of young Nigerians are key assets in battling corruption. He encouraged corps members to be positive influencers by steering clear of wrongdoing and serving as role models in their communities and workplaces. He also invited them to support the anti-corruption fight by reporting misconduct through the EFCC’s Eagle Eye App, ensuring reports are both credible and honest while preserving anonymity. EFCC representatives, including Ayodele Babatunde and Gbenga Adewoye from the Ilorin Zonal Command, assured the corps members that the Commission will continue to fight corruption in all its forms and is committed to prosecuting offenders.
